Ineffective immunotherapy (about 50% of treatments) could be timely stopped, saving high costs (about 80.000euro per treatment versus less than 500euro for a metabolic MRI) and preventing potential severe side effects, while knowledge of insufficient chemotherapy response can prevent surgery and potential toxic side effects..Metabolic MRI is in line with recent innovation investments by Philips (collaborator with UMCU and part of the users committee) using 7 tesla technology, in line with CE approval of metabolic MRI by Siemens and commitment of GE in enabling metabolic MRI, and in line following an earlier NWO-groot funded prototype called META-scan (PI: Klomp). Futura is the partner that provides mechanical interfacing to the MRI. The second partner MRCode (SME) will develop the scan software plug-in to generate quantified metabolic maps, and the third partner Wavetronica (SME) will provide an RF hardware patch to enable a 31P MRI upgrade to the installed base.
Partners: Futura Composities B.V, Mrcode, Technische Universiteit Eindhoven, Wavetronica

Projectbeschrijving: Surgery is the only cure for many types of cancer. In up to 20-30% of patients, however, surgery is.inadequate because either tumor tissue is left behind or critical healthy structures, like nerves, are.damaged leading to long lasting complications (e.g. sexual disorders and bladder dysfunction). On preoperative.images, tumors and critical anatomical structures (such as nerves) are clearly visible, but during.surgery, these are not always easy to identify since the surgeon can only rely on visual and tactile feedback..There is thus a need for a tool that can identify tumor tissue and critical anatomical structures during.surgery, in vivo and in real time..Hyperspectral reflectance imaging (HSI) is a prime candidate for such a tool. HSI images tissue over a.wide wavelength range (Vis-NIR), far broader than visible by eye. HSI measures diffusely reflected light.after it has traveled through tissue, which contains an ‘optical fingerprint’ that reflects the composition and.morphology of the tissue. Many ex vivo studies have shown the great potential of HSI for the detection of.tumors and critical anatomical structures. In this project, we will address a number of essential.fundamental and technical challenges to translate HSI to the laparoscopic (robotic) in vivo surgical setting..For the clinical use case, we will focus on the application in colorectal cancer..We will combine both the visible and near-infrared wavelength ranges and state of the art machine.learning to analyze the hyperspectral information. To ensure robust results in a surgical setting, we will.address two main challenges: (1) the variable distance and orientation between the laparoscope and the.tissue surface which will influence the measured spectra, and (2) the influence of specular reflections,.including glare on the measured spectra. We will develop methods to address these challenges and we will.validate our methods by laparoscopic imaging of ex vivo surgical resection specimens from colorectal.cancer patients. Finally, we will demonstrate the clinical feasibility of the hyperspectral laparoscopy system.by performing in vivo measurements in a small group of colorectal cancer patients.
Aanvrager: Stichting Het Nederlands Kanker Instituut-Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Ziekenhuis
Partners: Academisch Medisch Centrum, Offroad Medical B.V., Stryker

Projecttitel: aiREAD - Accurate and Intelligent Reading for EArlier breast cancer Detection
Projectbeschrijving: With the introduction of artificial intelligence (AI), now a computer can interpret a digital.mammogram (DM) as well as a screening radiologist. This powerful possibility needs to be used to.optimize the balance between benefits and harms of breast cancer screening and further reduce breast.cancer mortality. Presently, in the Dutch national screening program, one in four screened women will.have a cancer that is not detected at screening. Although some of these cancers appear in the period.between screenings, about half of them were already detectable on previous screening mammograms,.but were not recalled. The introduction of AI, together with the development of other image analysis.processes, could reduce this problem by maximizing the reading performance of the radiologists..Currently, all screening DMs are read by two screening radiologists independently. Which two.radiologists read each DM, and in what order, are completely arbitrary decisions. Based on a number of.our studies, we know that incorporating the right methodology to reading DMs would improve screening.performance. For this, algorithms to analyze the DMs, in terms of probability-of-malignancy presence,.difficulty of reading, and tissue composition and texture patterns, need to be leveraged to optimize which.DMs need to be human read, by how many and which specific radiologists, and in what order. We’ve.shown that incorporating AI-based analysis of the images into the reading process potentially reduces.false positives, while assigning the ideal pair of radiologists to read each DM could reduce false.negatives. Finally, setting the order of DM reading based on the patterns present in them, could drive the.human visual system to adapt in such a way that cancers are easier to detect..In this project, we aim to use a synergistic integration of existing AI systems and newly developed.image analysis technologies to improve screening mammography. We will evaluate how screening.radiologists best interact with the new technologies, and design workflows that optimize the screening.mammography reading process. If our project is successful, it will potentially lead to reductions in breast.cancer mortality and morbidity, false alarms for healthy women, and healthcare costs, without the need.to replace the current imaging technology, DM, with any other new, more expensive imaging modality.
Partners: Screenpoin medical, Universitair Medisch Centrum Utrecht, Volpara, sectra benelux

Projecttitel: Probing Intercellular heterogeneity in Circulating TUmor cells of de novo metastatic Hormone Sensitive Prostate CanceR patiEntS (PICTURES)
Projectbeschrijving: Treatment options available for cancer patients are increasing rapidly. Biomarkers to predict which.therapies will be effective are however lacking, resulting in the frequent administration of ineffective.therapies. Here we propose to apply a novel technology that will enable the testing.of drug effectivity and heterogeneity therein on individual tumor cells present in blood of metastatic.Hormone Sensitive Prostate Cancer (mHSPC) patients and it is our assumption that these read-outs.predict the outcome to a given treatment. In the high-risk mHSPC setting we need better biomarkers to.identify the patients who have a poor outcome on primary androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and.docetaxel treatment as well as to underpin the scientific basis to improve the treatment. Inter-patient.and intra-patient heterogeneity both play an important role in the differences in response to treatment in.prostate cancer and research into the nature of the heterogeneity and its significance will aid in.developing an improved individualized treatment strategy. Our hypothesis is that by combined.phenotyping and genotyping of individual circulating tumor cells (CTCs) we can identify patients at risk.for early recurrence. Therefore, we introduce a novel technology which enables the measurement of drug.responses of individual cancer cells of the actual patient and determine whether the heterogeneity of.the response can be predicted by the genotype of the CTC. Our hypothesis is that we will identify the.patients with early treatment failure based on the proportion of the CTC failing to respond and postulate.that the concurrent genetic heterogeneity in CTC is able to predict treatment failure. Overall, success of.our strategy will enable efficacy testing of new drug or drug combination in the mHSPC as well as in the.hormone insensitive metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) setting..To obtain a sufficient number of CTCs for matched pheno- and genotyping, mHSPC patients will undergo.a Diagnostic Leukapheresis (DLA). After enrichment of CTCs from the DLA, the collected CTC are divided.in two portions. Portion 1 is used to determine the genotype of individual single CTCs. Portion 2 is used.to determine the viability of the CTC and measure the secretion of the Prostate Specific Antigen (PSA) to.measure the sensitivity of these cells to external compounds such as anti-tumor agents. This is.measured before and after exposure of the individual CTC to methabolone R1881 which mimicks.androgen deprivation, enzalutamide, doxetaxol and a combination of these compounds. After the.exposure and measurement of the secreted molecules the single CTCs will be genotyped to determine if.intra individual single CTC genomic variation can predict variation phenotypic readouts (i.e. PSA.production). We expect that the data generated in this project will cast the best approach to predict the.efficacy of the clinical response to the drug and ultimately improve the success rate of treatment of.mHSPC patients.
Partners: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC), Menarini, VyCAP B.V.

Projecttitel: Learning-based Control in MR-guided Hyperthermia for 3D Adaptive Cancer Therapy (Learn-2-Act)
Projectbeschrijving: Research Summary.Several clinical studies have shown that heating of tumours to a temperature of 40-44°C significantly.enhances the therapeutic efficacy of both radiotherapy and chemotherapy without adding extra toxicity to.healthy tissue. Hyperthermia (HT) acts along multiple mechanisms on cellular level but also on tissue level.that make malignant tissue more susceptible for radiation and cytotoxic as well as molecular targeted.drugs. Full exploitation of the multifactorial nature of HT requires accurate heating of the tumour to 42-.43°C, while keeping the temperature elevation in normal healthy tissues low. Despite the good clinical.results, widespread use of HT in oncology is hampered by the laborious task to preferentially heat a tumour.surrounded by healthy tissue in a non-invasive manner..To enable the broad application of local HT to improve the efficacy of cancer treatments and decreasing.the burden for the patients, there is a strong need for personalised, adaptive and high-performance control.technologies that accurately regulate the 3-dimensional (3D) temperature distribution of tumours of.various sizes (4-15cm) and shapes. The proposed project aims at the development of effective learningand.optimisation-based control strategies that fill this need. This is a highly innovative and challenging.task due to the complexity of the problem (large-area 3D thermal control inside the human body), the.large variability over patients (different shapes, sizes and locations of the tumour) and time (changing.body temperature regulation mechanisms and organ movements), the tight performance demands and.hard constraints on heating signals. To achieve this task, the control technologies will exploit on-line.measurements of 3D temperature distributions obtained by non-invasive thermometry by magnetic.resonance (MR) to create adaptive feedback during the HT treatments. The technologies will be developed.for both radiofrequency (RF) and focused ultrasound (FUS) heating applicators thereby assuring maximal.applicability and utilisation. The research leading to the envisioned control technologies is based on a.unique combination of multi-physics modelling, novel data-based estimation algorithms, on-line learningbased.model adaptation techniques, and efficient model predictive control (MPC) strategies that exploit.the underlying structure of the problem. The envisioned technologies have the potential for rapid clinical.translation as they can replace current control algorithms in both RF and FUS-based HT devices with the.prospect of a more controlled, effective and personalised HT treatment in oncology care..2.2. Utilisation Summary.Cancer is the number one cause of death in the Netherlands with almost 45,000 deaths annually and the.incidence of cancer is expected to increase rapidly to 133.000 new diagnoses per year due to ageing of.the population. In addition, the burden of toxicity in surviving patients after conventional treatments is.severe. As a result, there is a strong need to improve the effectiveness of current cancer treatments..Hyperthermia (HT) therapies have the potential to be a major contributor to fulfilling this need as several.clinical studies have shown that creating HT by heating of tumours to a temperature of 43°C significantly.enhances the therapeutic efficacy of both radiotherapy and chemotherapy without adding extra toxicity to.healthy tissue..The novel MR-guided learning- and optimisation-based estimation and control technologies envisioned in.this program are expected to realise temperature profiles in which the tumour region is accurately.controlled to the desired 43°C with only a small temperature elevation in the surrounding healthy tissue.during treatment. This enables step changes in the therapeutic efficacy of cancer treatment protocols that.are key in bringing HT treatments towards clinical operation. This potential, the timeliness and the longterm.feasibility of the envisaged approach is underlined by a broad consortium of leading clinics and.companies including Erasmus MC, Isala Hospital (Zwolle), Sensius BV, Dr. Sennewald Gmbh, Klinikum der.Universität München, and Uniklinik Köln. The users provide next to cash contributions also indispensable.opportunities for phantom, ex-vivo and in-vivo animal and patient testing leading to proof-of-concepts of.the proposed MR-guided learning-based model predictive control (MPC) solutions. These would form unique.and unparalleled experiments of MPC-based HT strategies for large target 3D regions (4-15cm). An.additional benefit of these experiments is that they provide the users directly with working in-house.demonstrators that will promote the adoption of these control technologies in their own environment, but.also far beyond. Moreover, knowledge transfer is further stimulated by internships of the researchers to.the involved users. Finally, the MR-guided estimation and control technologies will be developed in a unified.framework for both RF and FUS applicators. These benefits and our utilisation strategy open up better.oncology care for a broad range of patients with significantly increased probabilities of cure, shorter.treatment times and lower toxicity levels.
Partners: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC), Isala ziekenhuis, Sennewald, Sensius B.V., UKK

Projecttitel: ARCHITECT: Adaptive Brachytherapy using Customised Needle Applicators
Projectbeschrijving: Research Summary.Brachytherapy (BT) is a key component in the curative treatment of cervical cancer.[1] BT delivers radiotherapy locally, in close proximity of the tumour or target region. Radioactive sources are guided by applicators in the vaginal or uterine cavity, or by needles in tumour containing tissue. Successful BT requires accurate applicator and needle placement and radioactive source dwell time planning..Preliminary work from our group demonstrated the feasibility to produce 3D printed customised applicators with optimised needle channels, based on pre-brachytherapy magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans of patients.[2] The ARCHITECT programme aims to develop a systematic applicator design approach by constructing fundamental design rules, needle channel path planners and product development tools. We hypothesise that customised BT applicators enhance conformity between target volumes and prescribed isodose. With smart designs, customised applicators may further improve patient comfort, user friendliness and situation awareness, e.g. by design for visibility in MRI and ultrasound. In addition, image-guided corrections of applicators and needle paths in 4D prints, containing embedded compliant mechanisms, will be evaluated. Conformity will be quantified by dose planning software and COIN indices, using CT/MRI scans of applicators positioned in tissue-mimicking phantoms, as well as clinically acquired images. Ultimately, improved conformity will increase local tumour control and cure, and decrease side effects and their impact on quality of life..The programme is divided in three coherent work packages, focusing on development of devices (WP1), path planning (WP2) software to optimise needle channel locations, and utilisation (WP3), evaluation and optimisation of applicators in clinically relevant environments. Documentation, quality monitoring and risk analyses (patient comfort, workflow, just-in-time inventory strategies, etc.) are actively embedded in the programme, in line with Medical Device Regulations (MDR), to expedite and allow progressions to translational and clinical research..2.2. Utilisation Summary.Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cause of cancer and cancer related deaths among women worldwide, with estimated 569.847 newly diagnosed and 311.365 cancer related deaths in 2018.[3] In the Netherlands, 832 women were diagnosed.[4] Currently, local tumour control remains suboptimal,[5, 6] and toxicity and side effects in nearby organs at risk (OAR) are prevalent, impacting on (sexual) quality of life.[7-10] This is of great personal and societal relevance, since 65% of women survive at 5-years, with the majority being in their early decades of life.[6].Recent developments include the introduction of 3D imaging (CT/MRI) and Image Guided Adaptive Brachytherapy (IGABT).[11] The LUMC Radiation-Oncology department has a strong background in clinical trials establishing the role of radiotherapy in gynaecological cancer, as well as contributing to the formation of European guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of endometrial (ESGO-ESMO-ESTRO) and cervical cancer (ESGO-ESTRO-ESP). Rapid dissemination of results is ensured through this network and site visits and advisory support offered by international experts and key opinion leaders in the field (letters of support). In addition, patient advocacy group Stichting Olijf will help optimise research, providing input from the patients’ perspective, and will help in the dissemination of information to patients..The TU Delft and LUMC have actively approached and connected industrial partners that have existing infrastructure, assets and roadmaps to bring proposed developments to the market. The formed consortium connects Elekta/Nucletron as BT market leader and Oceanz as 3D printing company with a focus on medical devices. Together, they will finance and facilitate production of high-grade and.page 4 of 21.clinically safe applicators during the full programme. Requested budget will therefore be available for funding research personnel. In addition, the research interface of clinically used brachytherapy dose planning software (Oncentra, Elekta) will be available for this programme.
Partners: Nucleton BV (Electa), Oceanz, Technische Universiteit Delft

Projecttitel: AMICUS: AI in Medical Imaging for novel Cancer User Support
Projectbeschrijving: Research Summary.The research aim of AMICUS is to develop and utilize technology for distributed deep learning on medical.images in the Netherlands and beyond using the Personal Health Train approach and to show in.compelling examples its value to cancer care organizations and patients..Medical imaging is the cornerstone of screening, detection, diagnosis, staging, treatment and follow-up.in almost every cancer patient and without a doubt is Big Data. However the processing and.interpretation of images is still mainly a human task. With AMICUS we will develop technology that.supports radiologists & oncologists and other stakeholders including the patient in extracting relevant.information from images..The technology used for extracting information from images in AMICUS is deep learning, a form of.artificial intelligence which has proven to be a breakthrough in the field, but which requires large.volumes of imaging data to be successful. However, getting access to imaging data is a problem as it is.dispersed across hospitals and is very privacy sensitive..In AMICUS we will develop technology that allows deep learning from these distributed imaging datasets.without the need for these data to leave the hospital. For this, we will leverage the previously developed.Personal Health Train approach which allows privacy-preserving learning from distributed FAIR (Findable.Accessible Interoperable and Reusable) clinical data and which AMICUS will extend with FAIR imaging.data and deep learning..The work plan of AMICUS consists of four work packages. WP1 and WP2 will focus on developing.technology to make imaging and related data FAIR and to perform distributed deep learning in a way.which requires only minimal computing resources at each hospital. WP3 and WP4 will focus on creating.and demonstrating the value of AMICUS technology by implementing compelling solutions for care.organizations to improve cancer care processes and for patients to improve cancer outcomes..2.2. Utilisation Summary.AMICUS offers a responsible and scalable way to create value out of the petabytes of imaging data of.cancer patients stored in hospital archives. Since imaging is part of all phases of the cancer care path,.the developed technology from AMICUS will create value for all cancer types and in all phases of the care.path. Besides cancer care, imaging plays an important role in almost all health related diseases e.g..cardiovascular, neurology, orthopedy, gynecology, internal medicine etc. All these disciplines could.benefit from the technology, as the use of FAIR methodologies and the accompanying deep learning.platform developed within AMICUS will be applicable to different diseases and medical contexts. Hence.AMICUS will increase the value of (imaging) data for better disease management..We have already identified more than 20 potential users of AMICUS technology. Our utilization plan is.based on an extensive and proven track record supported by experienced technology transfer officers. It.is tailored towards the needs of different categories of potential users incl. Cancer patients;.Infrastructure and data services providers; Medical device vendors; Pharmaceutical companies;.Hospitals; Government; Health insurance providers and Scientific researchers.
Partners: Academisch Ziekenhuis Groningen, Medical Data works, Stichting Katholieke Universiteit Brabant, Universiteit Twente, Varian Medical Systems

Projecttitel: PARTNR - Personalized cAnceR TreatmeNt and CaRe platform
Projectbeschrijving: The PARTNR project researches and develops an intelligent self-learning system for patients with breast.cancer that combines medical data with data about functioning in daily-life and that provides personalized.intervention recommendations for cancer-related fatigue. Mortality after breast cancer has declined, but.there is still limited attention for long-term effects on the quality of life of patients. Fatigue is one of the.most referred symptoms of cancer patients and has a high negative impact on the quality of life. In our.use case, we will focus on cancer-related fatigue after breast cancer. For a holistic view on patients, clinical.data will be augmented with (real-life) data from other sources. With this, the health status of patients will.be quantified in health scores for several health-related domains (e.g. physical, mental) that are of specific.importance to cancer patients. This holistic view makes personalizing care possible, with the direct effect.for the patients that treatment is more effective and their quality of life increases. The health scores provide.insight for patients themselves and makes their health (progression) more tangible. This will empower.patients and their environment to take an active role in their recovery. The holistic patient data will be.combined with individual beliefs, goals and preferences with regard to possible interventions, to form the.input for a self-learning algorithm that will be able to make a tailored treatment recommendation. Patients.will be monitored (semi)continuously, so that changes over time can be identified as well as the extent to.which certain treatment objectives have been accomplished. For the development process, a user-centered.iterative approach will be used, resulting in continuous end user testing, verification and validation. First.decision support will be done based on preferences and decision rules filtered from literature and expert.opinion, but during the course of the project the system will be adapted and learn using the real-life data.that is gathered. In the end of the project we will have a working platform that is able to provide.personalized treatment recommendations. The project does not start from scratch, but builds on results of.earlier projects and existing infrastructure. The multidisciplinary team ensures the availability of the.necessary medical, psychological, technological and implementation expertise. The cooperation between.university, SMEs and health care ensure that chances for uptake of the tools and technologies after the.project are optimal.
Partners: Academisch Ziekenhuis Groningen, Evidencio, Ivido B.V., RDD, Stichting Helen Dowling Instituut

Projecttitel: Messenger RNA as a validator approach towards gene therapy of congenital chronic diseases
Projectbeschrijving: Chronic diseases based on individual gene mutations constitute a major burden for the individual and society. Advances in gene diagnostics have produced a wealth in knowledge for the molecular basis of disease. However, the translation of these insights into novel ATMPs and related therapeutics is lagging behind. In the past years, break-through innovations have been made in gene therapy employing viral vectors which will lift the general scepticism towards this type of therapy. Still, the hurdle for gene therapy is high as the intervention is irreversible. Therefore, in order to enable a broader and more rapid implementation of gene therapy, safe and powerful means are required to assess the potential benefits and risks of gene therapy. This project aims to prove the use of therapeutic mRNA as a safe and powerful therapeutic modality to assess the potential risk/benefit of viral gene therapy in the individual and/or the patient group. Messenger RNA has unique characteristics for this purpose: The therapeutic effect will be achieved through protein expression, thus in the same way as for viral gene therapy. However, in contrast to gene therapy, this change is reversible. Should the desired therapeutic effect not be achieved, or should dosing turn out to be critical or immunogenicity be observed, then the intervention can be stopped without persistent risk for the patient. Together with the Belgian project partners we have identified the congenital chronic disease cystinosis as a highly suited test case. Success in this indication paves the way to accelerated development and approval of novel medications for the more than 6,000 congenital diseases, which often are severely debilitating or fatal.
Partners: Katholieke Universiteit Leuven, Radboud Universitair Medisch Centrum

Projecttitel: Dynamic cell states in epilepsy associated developmental disorders
Projectbeschrijving: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is multisystem genetic disorder that causes abnormal growths throughout almost every organ in the body. Approximately 90procent of TSC patients present with complex structural brain abnormalities throughout the cortex, known as cortical tubers. These tubers cause devastating and therapeutically challenging neurological manifestations, including neurodevelopmental delay, autism and severe epilepsy. Current treatments for TSC associated epilepsy, such as medication or surgical resection of tubers, often come with severe side effects or only provide limited relief. Thus, there is an urgent need to better understand the underlying molecular mechanisms of TSC so that novel anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs) can be developed. The development of AEDs for TSC are currently hampered by the fact that tubers contain a heterogenous mix of cell types, including dysmorphic neurons, giant cells and reactive astrocytes. This high degree of cellular heterogeneity hinders the interpretation of gene expression data generated from bulk tissue and the subsequent drug development. Single-nuclei RNA-Seq (snRNA-Seq) can overcome this limitation. This revolutionary technique is useful for understanding dynamic states, networks and the discrete make-up of the cellular populations in heterogeneous samples. While snRNA-Seq has been previously used on brain tissue, this revolutionary technique has never been applied to TSC cortical tubers. As such, we aim for the first time to elucidate transcriptional cell state changes in TSC cortical tubers and identify specific cell-populations that could be targeted with AEDs. To address these aims we will develop and utilise droplet based snRNA-Seq (DroNc-Seq) on surgical resected TSC cortical tubers. This project unites a unique combination of cutting-edge and innovative bioinformatic and molecular techniques with rare human tissue. The findings from this research project may lead to the development of novel AEDs that will have a dramatic impact on the quality of life of patients, their families and primary care givers.

Projecttitel: New generation mRNA vaccines, the best of both worlds
Projectbeschrijving: Vaccines, such as live attenuated pathogens, inactivated pathogens and subunit vaccines, are widespread used to protect humans and animals from infectious diseases. Recently, versatile vaccine platforms have been generated to be able to respond to newly emerging pathogens like the SARS-CoV-2. Among these platforms are the mRNA-based vaccines, which include self-amplifying mRNAs (SAMs), that are safe by design but need improvements with regards to efficacy. Upon introduction of the mRNA in the target cell cytoplasm, the production of antigens is initiated as well as activation of several antiviral pathways like the type I interferon (IFN) and the integrated stress response (ISR). The activation of the type I IFN pathway shapes the innate and adaptive immune system and is thus crucial for good vaccine efficacy. Yet, the downside of the coin is the negative effect of the ISR pathway on antigen expression levels. Recently, two new viral proteins have been characterized with a unique mechanism to counteract the ISR pathway without affecting the type I IFN pathway. Here we aim to generate bicistronic mRNA vaccines in which such a viral stress antagonist (VSA) is co-expressed with the antigen. The production of the VSA will increase antigen expression levels without affecting innate and adaptive immune system activation, thereby providing the best of both worlds. The increased antigen expression level will increase vaccine efficacy. These novel types of mRNA vaccines will be evaluated in a relevant chicken model, but the application of this technology will be much broader and encompass improved vaccines for use in other animals and humans.

Projecttitel: IMplementation of Advancements in GENetic Kidney Disease
Projectbeschrijving: In the Netherlands, more than 6,000 people require dialysis or kidney transplantation. Patients with end-stage kidney disease have a mean life-expectancy of only 5-10 years and significantly reduced quality of life. Emerging data indicate that genetic defects contribute significantly to their aetiology, not only in children but also at adult age. This particularly applies to diseases affecting the renal interstitium and tubules, together comprising up to 33procent of monogenic kidney diseases. These diseases include ciliopathies/tubulo-interstitial diseases (e.g. nephronopthisis and uromodulin-, mucin 1- and hepatocyte nuclear factor [HNF]1beta-related diseases) and tubulopathies (e.g. Bartter syndrome, cystinosis). Yet, many patients with a suspected ciliopathy or tubulopathy remain undiagnosed. Recent genetic and technological advances, for the first time, not only allow large-scale genetic diagnostics for these patients, but also allow the development of new methods for studying treatment options. This consortium aims to improve diagnostics of patients with ciliopathies and tubulopathies, enhance quality of care, and translate genetic findings to personalized care by testing pharmacological treatment approaches based on patient-derived disease models. To this end, we will address the following key objectives: • A cohort of 150 patients with tubulopathies and ciliopathies will be subjected to nextgeneration sequencing (NGS) genetic diagnostics and extensive biobanking. • Patient-specific cell and tissue models will be developed and used for functional analysis to identify the molecular mechanisms of ciliopathies and tubulopathies. • Using pharmacological screening, the newly developed cell models will facilitate the development of personalized treatment strategies for ciliopathies and tubulopathies. Altogether this proposal will improve diagnostics, genetic counselling, prognostics, and treatment of patients with genetic kidney diseases. The close collaboration with industrial partners will ensure rapid translation from research to practice and open up new economic perspectives.
Partners: Academisch Ziekenhuis Groningen, Mimetas B.V., Newtricious R&D B.V., Nierstichting Nederland, Sanofi B.V., Scinus Cell Expansion Netherlands B.V., Universiteit Utrecht

Projecttitel: A novel egg-protein hydrolysate to boost brain function – mind your blood vessels!
Projectbeschrijving: Age-related chronic diseases including dementia, T2DM and CVD become more prevalent and of increasing societal concern. Common denominators of these co-morbidities are insulin-resistance and impaired vascular function. Newtricious (NWT)-03 is a novel egg-protein hydrolysate that has proven benefits on insulin-sensitivity and peripheral vascular function, which are risk markers for T2DM and CVD. Insulin-resistance is also associated with cognitive decline, while impaired brain vascular function is a key event preceding the development of impaired cognitive performance. We have already shown some short-term beneficial effects of NWT-03 on cognitive performance, but underlying mechanisms were not addressed, and long-term effects still remain unknown. Therefore, we hypothesize that the novel egg-protein hydrolysate NWT-03 beneficially affects brain vascular function and cognitive performance following long-term daily intake. The main objective is to investigate the effect of NWT-03 on cerebral blood flow as a marker of brain vascular function. For this, a randomized, placebo-controlled intervention study with forty overweight or obese adults (aged 60-70) with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) will be performed. SCD has emerged as a pre-mild cognitive impairment (pre-MCI) at risk condition of dementia and these participants will receive daily 5.0 g of NWT-03 or a placebo for 36 weeks. Non-invasive MRI methods will be used to investigate brain vascular function, while we will also focus on potential NWT-03-induced changes on cognitive performance (secondary objective). Exploratory objectives are to study long-term effects on other potential mechanisms responsible for observed effects on cognitive performance, and other perceivable benefits. This project will advance our understanding why NWT-03 is beneficial for different age-related conditions, including cognitive impairment. Except for its scientific relevance, results will contribute to other important areas: (i) reduction of economic and societal costs and (ii) opportunities for Newtricious R&D to launch and market evidence-based nutritional concepts, to develop applications, and to differentiate from competitors.

Projecttitel: Myofiber and myofibril contractility in hiPSC-derived 3D muscle for Pompe disease and facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy
Projectbeschrijving: While there are >700 neuromuscular disorders, for only very few a treatment option is available. A major reason for the lack of therapies is the scarcity of human models for preclinical research. To overcome this limitation, we recently developed a muscle-on-chip model for Pompe disease and FSHD using myogenic progenitor cells generated from patient-derived hiPSCs. As a next step, we now propose to perform contractility experiments in single myofibers and myofibrils isolated from the muscle-on-chip model. These experiments will require a system that can measure contractile forces in the nano-Newton range. In WP1, we will develop the system to measure myofibril contractility, optimize the conditions to isolate myofibers and myofibrils from the muscle-on-chip model, and perform contractility assays on the isolated myofibers and myofibrils. In WP2, we will enhance the maturation of our current muscle-on-chip model using different approaches that promote the formation of distinct myofiber types. Next, we will perform contractility assays on myofibers and myofibrils isolated from the matured muscle-on-chip model. In WP3, we will characterize the defects underlying contractile force generation in Pompe disease and FSHD by combining myofiber and myofibril contractility assays with single myofiber RNA sequencing. The myofibril contractility system that we will develop within this project enables us to study sarcomeric dysfunction in response to Pompe disease and FSHD. The system will further provide important information on the maturation status of the sarcomeres present in our muscle-on-chip model and establish novel readouts for this model. We expect that this system will be relevant for other neuromuscular disorders as it will provide a tool to study basic disease mechanisms and will aid in the development and testing of treatment options.
Partners: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC), Ionoptix B.V., Vrije Universiteit Medisch Centrum (VUMC)

Projecttitel: Human cerebral organoids as a novel cell culture model to accelerate HIV cure research
Projectbeschrijving: Background: HIV persistence in cellular and anatomical reservoirs is the major obstacle to cure, yet many questions about the composition of the viral reservoir are unanswered. The role of the central nervous system (CNS) as a viral Reservoir is still debated and an important reason for this knowledge gap is  related to inherent difficulties associated with (post-mortem) sampling of this unique tissue compartment. Studies have been performed using animal models and 2D-cell cultures for microglia, astrocytes and neurons. Since efforts are ongoing to reduce animal experiments and 2D-cell cultures are limited in how well they recapitulate cell phenotype, function and complexity of the human CNS, we urgently need an alternative model system. Our recently developed human cerebral organoid model in which microglia develop innately may serve as such a model system. Objective: To evaluate the use of our human cerebral organoid model as an alternative to post-mortem human brain tissue in HIV infection. Design: Impact of HIV infection will be investigated in post-mortem biopsies from HIV-positive individuals and compared to ex vivo infection of primary microglia, cerebral organoids and organoid-derived microglia. HIV infection dynamics and reservoir formation will be monitored using ultra-sensitive quantitative PCR. Furthermore, single-cell RNA sequence analyses will provide insights in the impact of HIV on microglia and non-immune cells such as astrocytes and neurons and allow discrimination between infected and non-infected cells. Anticipated impact: Organoids are emerging as pivotal systems to reduce the number of animal experiments, to increase our understanding of disease development and provide an opportunity for personalized medicine. We strongly feel that knowledge regarding our specific human cerebral organoid model will provide important insights that will not only directly benefit HIV cure research but will also proof valuable for the investigation of other neurological diseases.

Projecttitel: Patient Derived tumor Organoid Immuno-Oncology (PDO-IO) model development for combinatorial immuno-oncological (IO) treatment evaluation
Projectbeschrijving: HUB and HUBs academic partners, The Hubrecht Institute and University Medical Centre Utrecht (UMCU) have previously shown that adult stem cell derived organoids are an in vitro culture system that functionally resembles the tissue from which it originates. We have shown that it faithfully mimics disease phenotypes of individual patients with cystic fibrosis (CF) or cancer and drug compounds can be tested for their efficacy in treating such patients. Preliminary data from HUB demonstrate that organoids and immune cells can be cocultured and used to develop and test immuno-oncological treatments for cancer. The main objective of this project is to develop a human relevant Lung and Colon Immuno-oncology model using Tumor Organoids (IOTO), to better predict drug effectiveness for IO/small molecule therapies. Moreover, we will set up biobanks for lung and colon cancer organoids combined with the immune cells of the same patients to study the interaction between them and to functionally improve these. We will first set conditions allowing growth of organoids together with T cells in a highly robust manner. Subsequently, we will activate T cells and develop scalable assays that enable quantification of organoid killing. Together, this will lead to an organoid-T cell coculture platform that can be used for routine efficacy testing of IO-modulating compounds, shortening the time-line from drug discovery to launch. Therefore, the new therapeutic strategies that will come from this will revolutionize the way in which lung and colon cancer are treated and may boost cancer survival rates. The social impact of this project is high since lung and colon cancer have high mortality rates. Economically, HUB and GSK will stronghold their positions as the market leaders in organoid and immuno-oncological research and will even more than before mark Utrecht on the map as a place for highly innovative organoid-based health approaches.

Projecttitel: Using continuous imaging and label free analysis for optimizing differentiation of induced pluripotent stem cells for personalized medicine applications
Projectbeschrijving: A major healthcare problem is that few drugs work for all patients, often due to differences in their genetic backgrounds. Animal models commonly used for drug testing do not always capture human-specific traits, let alone differences between patients. Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) hold promise for personalized medicine since they contain the genomes of individuals from whom they are derived. hiPSCs can be directed (‘differentiated’) to form all cells of the human body including heart and blood vessels. However, differentiation is variable between hiPSCs from different patients and typically requires protocol optimization, using substantial resources prior to starting patient-specific modelling. In CARMEN, we will develop imaging to identify individual steps during differentiation. We will monitor morphological changes of the cells with high fidelity and temporal resolution and use previously developed reporter lines that indicate distinct cardiovascular developmental stages through fluorescent markers. Combined, they will enable the development of algorithms that correlate changes in morphology with key differentiation stages. Continuous monitoring and cell-type identification will also allow better understanding of developmental pathways and facilitate development of optimal differentiation protocols which are not variable between patients patient specific lines. Thus, efficient patient-specific cardiovascular modelling will become available at acceptable cost for financially-pressured healthcare whilst also eliminating or reducing animal testing through better methods. Principles and tools developed here will likely be applicable to differentiation and analysis of other cell types thus benefitting future cell-based therapies.

Projecttitel: Developing and optimizing inhibitors for next-generation immune-oncology
Projectbeschrijving: Immuno-oncology (IO) clinical strategies unleashing T cell-cytotoxicity have significantly improved the perspective of cancer patients. By blocking inhibitory checkpoints, particularly PD-1, PD-L1 or CTLA-4, T cells are functionally reinvigorated to productively respond to their cognate antigens. However, many patients do not show durable benefit, because of decreased immunogenicity by antigen loss or antigen-presentation machinery (APM) deficiencies. Immune evasion can be counteracted by innate immune NK cells, which recognize tumor cells in the absence of antigens and MHC. To identify tumor genes determining susceptibility to both cytotoxic T cells and NK cells, we used a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 library. We identified all three components (RNF31, RBCK1, and SHARPIN) of the LUBAC complex, depletion of which sensitized tumor cells to both CD8 T and NK cell killing, in a TNF-dependent manner. Translating this finding to a preclinical setting, we inhibited RNF31 with HOIPIN-8, a small molecule inhibitor tool compound. This strongly sensitized tumors to both CD8 T and NK cell killing. Moreover, HOIPIN-8 treatment greatly enhanced immune-mediated killing of tumors with antigen-loss and APM deficiencies. However, although RNF31 inhibitors may serve as a potent therapeutic approach in principle, it is highly likely that tumors will eventually acquire resistance. As a PoC for this hypothesis, we found that TNF-receptor 1 loss reverses the sensitization of RNF31-deficient tumors. Recently, a collaboration was launched between Immagene, a recent spin-off of NKI-AVL that develops clinical proof RNF31 medicines, and the Peeper lab at NKI. Together, we will study resistance to both currently available and newly developed RNF31 inhibitors. We expect this PPP to provide invaluable insight into rewiring processes leading to RNF31i resistance, and to contribute to the development of clinically relevant RNF31 inhibitors. We also expect to uncover secondary therapeutic targets that can be inhibited to combat resistance for new IO medicine development, eventually leading to more durable clinical responses.
Aanvrager: Stichting Het Nederlands Kanker Instituut-Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Ziekenhuis

Projecttitel: Novel targets and drugs for the treatment of viral infections of the human pulmonary system.
Projectbeschrijving: Background: Respiratory viral infections are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in infants, children and adults. The epithelial cells of the bronchial tree represent the first line of defence against microbial invaders but are also the primary targets of respiratory viruses. This holds especially true for highly differentiated ciliated cells. These cells play an essential role in mucociliary clearance and signalling of the bronchial epithelium. Unfortunately, viruses such as RSV, Coronaviridae and many Influenza virus strains have a tropism for ciliated cells. Direct antiviral compounds with different mechanisms of action represent the cornerstone of antiviral treatment. However, it has become clear that irrespective of their mechanism of action, antiviral compounds may be unable to completely clear the virus from the bronchial epithelium in a timely fashion. Therefore, LUMC and Janssen Infectious Diseases & Vaccines (Janssen ID&V) would like to discover host-directed targets in bronchial epithelial cells to complement direct antiviral therapy in the human host. Objective and design: Building on preliminary discoveries, LUMC and Janssen ID&V would like to discover and validate more host-directed targets. The technological toolkit of LUMC and Janssen ID&V will be further expanded. Parallel to this discovery and validation effort, the mechanism of action and antiviral activity of certain JNJ (Johnson & Johnson) compound classes will be further elucidated and evaluated. Finally, a novel in vitro model system (lamb bronchial epithelial cells) will be optimised. Social and economic impact: The social and economic impact of respiratory viral diseases varies from serious (RSV, Influenza virus) to crippling (Coronaviridae). Most of all, the cost of human lives is unacceptably high. This is demonstrated by the recent Covid-19 crisis, but it should be clear that these infections have always been an underappreciated cause of human suffering and death in The Netherlands, Europe and the world.

Projecttitel: Artificial-intelligence-supported cancer grading for more efficient and accurate histopathological diagnosis
Projectbeschrijving: Optimal treatment decisions for cancer patients are hampered by variability in grading among pathologists. When there is a suspicion for cancer, typically a tissue biopsy is taken. This biopsy is stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and evaluated by a pathologist for the presence and aggressiveness (i.e. grading) of the tumor. Professional organizations have drafted standardized guidelines on how this grading should be performed however, there is still significant inter- and intra-observer variation among pathologists. Artificial intelligence, specifically through deep learning, has shown to increase efficiency and consistency in histopathological diagnosis, and, recently, to perform grading at the expert level. We have prototypes of such algorithms validated in the lab which could significantly impact clinical practice, but have not yet been tested in routine diagnostics. The aim of this project is three-fold. First, we will further develop our existing grading algorithms for prostate and breast cancer, to enhance robustness to variance in data sources and disease (sub)types. Second, we will conduct studies to determine the most efficient way to integrate algorithms into the routine workflow. Last, we will evaluate the most promising workflow prospectively in pilot lines at both peripheral and academic centers to assess performance. Currently, there are no algorithms commercially available which can do pathologist-level grading of cancer. Thus, this project can have both significant societal and economic impact. From a societal perspective, we can make expert grading available at locations without access to subspecialized pathologists. Outside the Netherlands, there are pathologist shortages in countries such as India and China where these algorithms could have even more impact. Thirona is already ISO13485 certified and has experience with CE certification and FDA 510(k) clearance. As such, upon completion of this project, algorithms could be commercially available quickly, offering the potential for a significant disruption of the health care market.

Projecttitel: Blended lifestyle care for diabetes remission (060.44075)
Projectbeschrijving: Unhealthy lifestyle drives the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetes (T2D). Thus, lifestyle modification should take centre stage in its treatment. DIABLEND is the first phase of the “Den Haag Diabetes Remission programme”. The latter will include a large-scale study on a personalised and tailored strategy for achieving T2D remission using lifestyle programmes based on the physical, mental, behavioural and socio-economic characteristics of the individual with T2D. The major goal of the programme is to develop an ecosystem (“Grozzerdam”) in The Hague for personalised lifestyle optimisation in people with T2D on a large scale. In DIABLEND (phase-1 of the programme), we aim to develop and beta-test an integrated approach for personalised lifestyle optimisation in people with T2D in The Hague (Diabetes Remission framework, DRF), focused on two deprived neighbourhoods in The Hague: Schilderswijk and Bouwlust-Vrederust. The project will start from existing tools/platforms and aims to integrate and innovate towards an ecosystem that can be implemented for thousands of persons with T2D in the “Den Haag Diabetes Remission program” (beyond the current project). Therefore, the DRF will be designed in collaboration with relevant partners and stakeholders. Essential elements of the DRF are: use and personalised blending of home-measurements, generation of a personalised menu of locally, easily accessible lifestyle interventions, and implementation of coaching and e-health options (Diabox). It is of importance to start with assessment of the current local diabetes care system, and design a framework that fits with the needs, capabilities and preferences of citizen-patients (WP1). Outcome of WP1 will tailor the design of the DRF (WP2) and the Diabox (WP3). In WP4 (elements of the) DRF and Diabox will be beta-tested in several small user groups. Finally, WP5 will focus on the living environment. The lessons learnt and output from DIABLEND will be disseminated (WP6) through the Lifestyle4Health platform.
Aanvrager: Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk Onderzoek TNO
Partners: BENU Nederland B.V., Bas van de Goor Foundation, Changing Health Ltd, Diabetes Fonds, Leids Universitair Medisch Centrum (Lumc), Livia Healthcare A/S, Mediq Nederland B.V., MiGuide B.V., Reinier Haga Medisch Diagnostisch Centrum B.V., SELFCARE B.V., Stichting Je Leefstijl Als Medicijn, Stichting Menzis Beheer

Projecttitel: Identification of specific drug sensitivities to eradicate leukemic stem cells
Projectbeschrijving: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a form of blood cancer that is still difficult to cure. Survival rates on average have remained less than 30procent. Older patients, who are at the greatest risk of developing AML, have especially poor survival and since we are living in a continuously ageing society, this results in a significant increase in both social as well as economic burden in the next decade(s). Therefore, better therapies against AML are clearly needed. Within the current proposal, we focus on small molecules targeting the epigenome. Over the past years it has been shown that mutations frequently occur in enzymes that control the epigenome in AML, and indeed as a consequence the epigenome is altered in AML patients. However, work by us and others has also shown that AML is a rather heterogeneous disease, whereby the spectrum of mutations that together give rise to AML can be rather patient-specific. Thus, a personalized approach will be needed. Janssen has identified promising leads that may result in better treatment options. These are small molecules interfering with Menin/MLL1, and secondly synthetic lethal hits in DNMT3A-mutated AML cells. As a continuation of a long-standing collaboration between the Schuringa lab at the UMCG (Groningen) and Janssen we will exploit these potential leads as well as novel targets identified/validated by Janssen in detail, both in vitro as well as in vivo, making use of our preclinical humanized niche patient-derived xenograft models. Our drug screens will be coupled to quantitative proteome screens in order to link drug sensitivities to specific genetic aberrancies and signaling networks. Ultimately, our studies should result in the development of more curative patient-specific treatment options for AML patients.

Projecttitel: Towards an all-in-one method enabling Non-Invasive Prenatal Diagnosis for Monogenic Diseases
Projectbeschrijving: Our current health care system offers various prenatal genetic tests to future parents and pregnant women who wish to be informed whether their unborn child is affected with a severe genetic disease. In case of monogenic disorders such as cystic fibrosis, thalassemia, Duchenne, etc, pregnant couples at risk currently rely on chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis two invasive procedures that both carry a small procedure-related risk of miscarriage. Their invasive character and associated risk of losing a healthy pregnancy are perceived as highly burdensome. To address this, we recently developed a promising new test called Monogenic Non-Invasive Prenatal Diagnosis (MG-NIPD). MG-NIPD only requires taking a small blood sample from both parents, with the mother donating blood early during pregnancy. Based on this the genetic composition of the relevant gene, its disease and healthy copy, is then carefully analysed, which critically enables diagnosing in a sensitive and robust manner which gene copy each parent transmitted to the fetus. MG-NIPD currently is still an academic exercise: in order to implement it in routine clinical diagnostics the method must be more generic and validated. In this project, we aim to transform MG-NIPD into a more generic all-in-one test that can be offered to all risk couples irrespective which of the selected diseases they carry. For this, we will replace our current PCR-based method for analysing the two copies of the disease-relevant gene by a method that employs capture probes. We will optimize this novel capture-based method and validate it on a large cohort of relevant samples that are collected as part of an ongoing MG-NIPD optimization and validation study. If successful, this project will greatly facilitate clinical implementation of a non-invasive blood test that can replace current burdensome invasive tests, much desired by risk couples opting for prenatal diagnosis.

Projecttitel: Exploring novel methods for robust multiplexed HLA-typing
Projectbeschrijving: The role of the HLA (Human Leukocyte Antigen) gene system is to help the body’s immune system distinguish between its own proteins and foreign proteins. In case of cell or tissue transplantation, to prevent rejection, it is necessary to find the recipient an HLA matched donor. This requires HLA typing, which nowadays involves DNA genotyping and comparing the genetic variation of a series of key HLA genes between donor and recipient. The repetitiveness and polymorphic nature of HLA genes presents challenges to the accurate sequencing of HLA genes though. In this project, GenDx, a Dutch biotech company specialized in HLA typing and the de Laat research group at the Hubrecht Institute, which develops novel DNA diagnostic methodologies, aim to collaborate to modify Hubrecht Institute’s proprietary targeted locus cloning (TLC) methods for improved multiplexed HLA genotyping. TLC relies on bacteria for selective amplification of target genes and we hypothesize that this can enable accurate genotyping of the poorly characterized repetitive DNA stretches present in selected HLA genes. If successful, this is expected to uncover new HLA alleles that will help improving HLA typing. We will also modify the current TLC procedure by replacing the bacterial amplification step by an enzymatic in vitro amplification strategy which we hypothesize can facilitate the simultaneous amplification and analysis of multiple selected HLA genes. Such multiplexed targeted HLA amplification method can eventually result in improved and facilitated HLA typing products to support the identification of donor-recipient pairs that match for cell and tissue transplantation.

Projecttitel: Detection and analysis of disease-driving T and B cell responses in tissues of patients with autoimmune disease for development of cell depletive treatment.
Projectbeschrijving: Rationale This project is a continuation of aproject on image-guided detection and analysis of lymphocytes in patients with malignancies (LSHM18090). We aim to develop atool kit for detection and analysis of T and B cells in systemicautoimmune disease. We focus on systemicsclerosis and Sjögren’s syndrome, for which we already developed tools. Systemicautoimmunediseases are driven by autoreactive Tand B cells. These cells collaborate to induce specificdisease features. We found that each autoreactive clone contains cells with various differentiation stages and that these differbetween lymphoid and affected tissue. . Current imaging modalities and functional assays have limited sensitivity and specificity to detect and analyze autoreactive Tand B cells. This has hampered the development of targeted treatments to deplete autoreactive Tand B cells. This contrasts with B cell malignancies for which such tools facilitated the development of therapies. Aim Development of atool kit for imaging and functional analysis of tissue resident autoreactive Tand B cells in patients with systemicautoimmune disease to study pathophysiology and to understand the mechanism of approved and potentially novel T/B cell depletivetreatments. Objectives 1. Preclinical validation of two imaging modalities to detect tissue resident Tand B cells. 2. Validate methods to analyze activation and interaction of autoreactive Tand B cells in patient tissues. 3. Test inhibitors of key survival pathways in T/B cell populations. 4. Use combined methods to analyze the mechanism of approved T/B cell depletive therapies in patients with systemicsclerosis and Sjögren’s syndrome. Expected outcome We expect to develop measurement tools that will allow 1. selective sampling of affected tissues, 2. understanding of critical mediators of activation and survival of disease-driving tissueresident Tand B cells. These tools can be applied for commercial preclinical and clinical drug development.
Partners: Galapagos N.V., GlaxoSmithKline Research & Development Ltd, Imaginab, Radboud Universitair Medisch Centrum, ReumaNederland, Xenikos B.V.

Projecttitel: RBD-CURE: A new gene therapy platform for Rare Bleeding Disorders.
Projectbeschrijving: Rare inherited bleeding disorders (RBDs), include deficiencies of coagulation factors fibrinogen, factor (F)II, FV, combined FV and FVIII, FVII, FX, FXI, FXIII, and deficiency of vitamin K-dependent factors. The incidence is varying from 1 in 500.000 for FVII deficiency to 1 in 2-3 million for prothrombin and FXIII deficiencies. The prevalence can be 4 times higher in parts of the world where consanguinity is common. Symptoms vary significantly between disorders, and patients. Mucocutaneous and surgical associated bleeding are reported in 20procent of patients, whereas post-traumatic hemarthrosis and hematomas are rarely reported in FVII and FX deficiencies. Menorrhagia, spontaneous abortion, and bleeding during vaginal delivery are reported in all deficiencies. Of all RBDs, the most in need of treatment are FVII- and FX-deficient patients. In our ongoing Health Holland project (LSHM19097, X-Cure) we are working on the development of gene therapy for FX deficiency. In the current proposal, we are aiming to develop platform technology which can also improve the expression of our FX gene therapy product as well being applied to other rare bleeding disorders. Currently, the development of gene therapy for ultra-rare diseases is neglected because it is not considered profitable or only at very high prices. The objective of this grant proposal is to develop an affordable gene therapy platform for RBDs. The developed platform has much broader implications, the following protein deficiencies could be targeted:  all clotting proteins including FVIII, Alpha-1 Antitrypsin and C-1 esterase inhibitor. Sanquin and SanaGen will collaborate in the design of a strong synthetic hepatocyte-specific promotor employing rational & bio-informatic approaches. Together with the NIN a novel improved AAV capsid that specifically and efficiently targets hepatocytes will be developed. Lastly, the novel vector including promotor will be tested in vivo in mice at NIN.
Partners: Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie van Wetenschappen, SanaGen B.V.

Projecttitel: HISTO-AI: Artificial Intelligence for HISTOpathological images as the next step towards personalised immunotherapy
Projectbeschrijving: Background: Immunotherapies are revolutionizing the management of cancer patients by producing durable responses with minimal toxicities in a subset of patients. This suggests that a sensitive companion diagnostic test is required to select these patients. Recently a cancer-immunogram was proposed for describing the different cancer-immune interactions in individual patients, to guide treatment choice, such as expression of programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1), amount of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), and tumor foreignness, as reflected by MicroSatellite Instability (MSI) and tumor mutational burden (TMB). In clinical practice however, not every patient is tested for MSI and TMB because this requires additional and expensive genetic tests. Moreover, semi-quantitative analysis of PD-L1 and TILs by pathologists is subjective and suffers from a significant intra-rater variability.Objective: With the possibility of digitizing histopathology slides of tumor tissue, computational analysis has the potential to develop algorithms that can predict MSI and TMB from hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) histology globally available. Secondly, digital evaluation of PD-L1 and TILs will reduce scoring variability and facilitate patient stratification in daily clinical practise. We will develop artificial intelligence algorithms that consistently detect TILs and PD-L1 (WP1), and predict tumor foreignness from H&E histology (WP2). We will evaluate the contribution and correlation of the outcome of the developed AI-algorithms with response to immunotherapy (WP3).Design: Having access to histopathological images of tumors of thousands of patients treated with immunotherapy at NKI and within nationwide consortia capturing clinical, histopathology and genomics data, we will develop artificial intelligence algorithms to objectively evaluate the contribution and correlation of histopathology imaging analysis with response to immunotherapy. This creates an exceptional opportunity to address important clinical problems in this area. Impact: Our ultimate goal is to develop a complementary diagnostic test directly from histopathological slides to achieve rapid, cost-effective and accurate cancer stratification of patients who will benefit from immunotherapy.
Aanvrager: Stichting Het Nederlands Kanker Instituut-Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Ziekenhuis

Projecttitel: Follow the Dot to Beat your Anxiety – Using EMDR in Virtual Reality at home to diminish trauma and anxiety in youth
Projectbeschrijving: Background Around 30procent of trauma-exposed children and adolescents develop post-traumatic stress symptoms. A frequently used therapy to reduce acute and long-term effects of trauma exposure is Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (EMDR). While EMDR is effective, children and adolescents often experience symptom recurrence when exposed to the feared situation outside the therapeutic context. Our proposed solution for decreasing symptom recurrence is the use of Virtual Reality (VR) in the phases of EMDR treatment aimed at installing the positive cognition for practice at home (VR-based EMDR), preparing the child or adolescent for the confrontation the trauma-related event or situation in the own living environment.ObjectiveThis project aims to 1) evaluate the effectiveness of VR-based EMDR, compared to EMDR treatment as usual (EMDR-TAU) in children and adolescents (aged 8-17 years) with post-traumatic stress symptoms, 2) identify for whom VR-based EMDR is most effective, and 3) examine the dynamical underlying emotion regulation mechanism to understand how VR-based EMDR may contribute to faster extinction and less recurrence of trauma-related anxiety.Design A randomized controlled trial is conducted with two conditions: EMDR-TAU and VR-based EMDR aimed at phases concerning desensitization of the traumatic event will be applied by certified EMDR-therapists in the therapeutic context. The phases aimed at installation” of positive cognition are intensified by EMDR practice at home using VR, with support of parents. Questionnaires are administered repeatedly and Experience Sampling Methodology is used before and during intervention.Anticipated impactVR-based EMDR stimulates self-care in the family setting and is expected to reduce symptom recurrence, enhance patient satisfaction and improve quality of life. We expect that less relapse will lead to a reduction in healthcare costs and shorter waiting lists in the long term.
Partners: EMDR-VR B.V., Psychologenpraktijk Oog B.V., Psychologisch Centrum Lambertushof, RIOzorg, Stichting Amphia, Stichting Catharina Ziekenhuis, Stichting Elisabeth-TweeSteden Ziekenhuis, Stichting Karakter, Stichting Máxima Medisch Centrum, Stichting Reinier van Arkel

Projecttitel: Accelerate and improve quality of non-invasive 12-lead ECG recording and data analysis to support early detection of cardiovascular disease in COVID-19 patients

Projectbeschrijving: Targeted vaccination against SARS-CoV2 and future corona viruses

Projecttitel: CoVax2: development of optimized vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 and other human corona viruses.
Projectbeschrijving: Within a few months, a new infectious disease, named COVID-19, has become a severe pandemic with 1.2 million confirmed cases and more than 64.000 deaths. These numbers are still inclining leading to a world-wide increase in morbidity and mortality, with an unprecedented impact on social and economic burdens. The causative agent was identified to be a novel beta-coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2). Clearly, there is an unmet need for treating those affected with SARS-CoV-2, and to protect people from getting infected and further spreading the virus. In this respect, a vaccine against COVID-19 is urgently needed as it can directly protect individual persons and indirectly curb viral spread through induction of herd immunity. International companies and institutes have started to develop vaccines specific for the COVID-19 Spike protein, with the promise to induce neutralizing antibody responses. The Spike protein is however the most heterogeneous amongst other proteins of coronaviruses with mutations already occurring in current COVID-19 isolates. Thus vaccines based only on the mutation sensitive Spike protein may become less effective during ongoing infections. Here, we propose to initiate a unique public-private consortium with a focus on development of improved vaccines against human beta-corona viruses. We will distinguish our approach from other initiatives by including corona antigens that are conserved between virus strains (i.e. present in SARS variants, MERS) and elicit both T and B cell responses. Essentially, we build this on a concerted effort comprising experts in Corona Virology, Immunology, Vaccinology, and on a combination of two strong vaccine platform technologies: DNA- and synthetic long peptide (SLP)-based vaccines. The DNA/SLP-based vaccines, which should generate both neutralizing antibodies and long-lasting T cell immunity, will be generated and tested both in vitro and in animal models with live coronavirus in highly secure BSL3 facilities. These efforts thus aim to develop a broadly applicable, coronavirus vaccine in order to counteract current and potential future outbreaks.
Partners: ISA Therapeutics B.V., Immunetune B.V., Synvolux

Projectbeschrijving: We aim to develop ultrapotent single-chain binding domains (SBDs) and antibodies to combat the novel coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2), the causative agent of the respiratory disease COVID-19. The UU-EMC-Harbour consortium will leverage their experience and expertise in coronaviruses (UU and EMC), heavy-chain antibody platform technologies (EMC and Harbour Antibodies) and establishment of relevant animal models (EMC). The trimeric coronavirus spike glycoprotein on the viral surface enables virus-cell entry and is the sole target for neutralizing antibodies and as such the key antigen for development of vaccines and therapeutic antibodies. Using established technology platforms, we will isolate and characterize potent neutralizing SBDs (in the form of nanobodies and human HCAbs) targeting the spike glycoprotein of SARS-CoV-2. We anticipate to further increase their neutralization potency by generating multivalent antibodies or binding domains through SBD coupling. Hence, potent neutralizing SBDs or antibodies will be coupled resulting in bi- or tri-valent binding moieties targeting one or more epitopes on the trimeric spike proteins. This innovative approach is expected to improve potency by i) increasing the avidity and stability of binding, ii) improved blocking of spike binding to its cellular receptor and/or iii) more effectively preventing spike conformational change needed for fusion. Mode-of-action will be assessed using structural and virological assays. Lead candidates will be assessed for proof-of-concept protective efficacy and safety in animal models. The functional antiviral screening of SBDs will provide profound insights in the vulnerable sites on SARS-CoV-2 spike and contribute to development of biologicals for (emergency) prophylactic and therapeutic use. Moreover, we envision that the innovative optimization strategies of biologicals (e.g. multivalent approaches) will be a starting point for development of generic intervention strategies against coronaviruses, and hence contribute to the international public health preparedness and response against future emerging diseases.
Aanvrager: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC)

Projecttitel: Design and implementation of a novel RNA-based therapy to protect the kidney and lungs against coronavirus infections
Projectbeschrijving: The ongoing coronavirus pandemic has made it painfully clear that in spite of compliance with social distancing efforts (to ‘flatten the curve’) and top-tier medical care (hospitalization in intensive care unit and oxygen support), the number of infected individuals continues to rise rapidly resulting in an alarmingly high healthcare burden. Naturally, the focus of medical attention has been respiratory distress or disease. However, extrapulmonary sites of infection could also be a contributing factor to increased morbidity and mortality. Alongside a SARS-CoV-2 vaccine, the dire need for first lines of defence against the virus have arisen, an option that currently does not exist. Here, we propose to develop antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) that specifically target SARS-CoV-2 viral RNA, thereby blocking viral replication. To achieve this, we will employ bioinformatic approaches to identify critical viral sequences, enabling the design and screening of ASOs that disrupt:1) Genomic replication (blocking 5'- and 3'-UTR structures and interactions required for replication) 2) Subgenomic RNA synthesis (e.g. by targeting TRS elements and RNA-protein interactions needed to produce the 8 subgenomic mRNAs of SARS-CoV-2). 3) Viral genome and mRNA translation (by targeting structural elements such as common leader sequence, hairpins and pseudoknots to interfere with ribosomal binding) 4) Unstructured sequences (to achieve rapid degradation of viral mRNAs) 5) RNA-binding protein interactions (altering accessibility for other proteins and altering structure) 6) Genome encapsidation ASOs that meet efficacy criteria will briefly be optimized and additionally screened, enabling reductions in dosing, after which their pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles will immediately be tested in vivo. In the absence of existing SARS-CoV-2 treatment options, and unclear timelines to effective vaccines or antivirals, our ‘lead’ ASOs represent a much-needed broadening of clinicians ‘first line of defence’ arsenal against SARS-CoV- . This can improve patient outcomes and simultaneously yield a reduction in worldwide healthcare costs.

Projecttitel: Rapid point of care tests to detect COVID-19 patients
Projectbeschrijving: Rapid point of care tests to determine infection (Antigen-tests) and/or past infection (Antibody-tests) are urgently needed in the current COVID-19 pandemic. Supplies are running out for molecular diagnostics, resulting in undertesting and ongoing spread of the virus. Rapid point of care Antigen-tests and Antibody-tests can provide a major benefit, as they produce a result within 10-15 minutes. Furthermore, no specialized laboratories are needs, as testing can be on site. Ingenasa is a company that has the expertise on board to make the tests. Combined with the unique coronavirus cultures and human monoclonal antibody expertise at the Amsterdam UMC there is a public-private partnership that combines knowledge and materials to produce properly evaluated tests.

Projecttitel: Novel antivirals against COVID-19 and related health threats for therapeutic and prophylactic use
Projectbeschrijving: A new coronavirus identified as severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is responsible for the viral pandemic outbreak which commenced in Wuhan (China) and has rapidly spread around the world. SARS-CoV-2 is responsible for the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), which causes fatal pneumonia in a percentage of the infected population. There are no specific drugs or vaccines available to treat the disease and the clinical management of sever cases involves oxygen administration and mechanical ventilation. As a result, the governments of most countries have adopted drastic containment measures with an unprecedented economic impact. In order to rapidly discover lead compounds with potential for clinical use we propose a research program on existing library of peptidomimetic protease inhibitors (partially novel and partially approved drugs) with proven antiviral activity, structure-assisted drug design, state-of-the-art synthesis techniques and advanced biochemical and cellular assays. The screening of novel molecules targeting relevant proteases required in the infection and virus proliferation mechanisms will enable the identification of new drug leads against SARS-CoV-2 and, ideally, broad-spectrum pan-coronavirus inhibitors coud could be applied during future outbreaks of other corona viruses. The public-private consortium to run this project, involves leading academic groups and for-profit parties with a track record in drug discovery and development, has ample knowledge in medicinal chemistry and virology. The development of an effective treatment and prophylactic for COVID-19 will have a profound social and economic impact in the current times. Additionally, a broad spectrum antiviral will help to contain/curb future epidemic coronavirus outbreaks and  to treat future patients.
Partners: Avivia Project B.V., Coöperatie 'Agrarische Natuur Drenthe' U.A., Leids Universitair Medisch Centrum (Lumc), Universiteit Utrecht

Projecttitel: Quick On-site Recognition of viral Objects using Nanosensing
Projectbeschrijving: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic is arguably the largest crisis faced by The Netherlands this generation. A major challenge is to increase the capacity for testing. The gold standard testing approach typically takes 24 hrs - or more including transport - and requires facilities where infectious material can be safely handled, which is not appropriate for massive testing of the population. Here, we propose a lab-on-a-chip platform for fast (several minutes) testing that is sensitive enough to detect SARS-CoV-2 directly in nasal/throat swab samples at the single virion level. The core technology and detection principle have been developed at the University of Twente and gave rise to start-up ECsens B.V. in 2020. This QoroNano system comprises a benchtop device with disposable microfluidic cartridges. Each cartridge houses a sensing array consisting of nano-electrodes coated with virus-specific antibodies. This principle has already demonstrated to be sensitive enough to detect individual nanoparticles in suspension.
