Projecttitel: INFUCOMP - Development affordable high performance vacuum infused composite structures
Projectbeschrijving: The technical aim of the current project proposal is the development of affordable high performance composite structures including a corresponding capability for design, analysis and process simulation:     - Obtain understanding of the loads and heat involved in super- and hypersonic airframe components.     - Obtain processing capability for manufacture of high performance - high temperature composites, including      infusion of low permeability of Uni-Directional Carbon fibre reinforcement preforms.     - Obtain fabrication capability for automated (robotic) manufacture of high performance - high temperature composites.    - Obtain validated new technology for high performance - high temperature composite structures by design,      analysis, fabrication and tests of representative coupons.
Aanvrager: Stichting Koninklijk Nederlands Lucht- en Ruimtevaartcentrum

Projectbeschrijving: Door het exponentieel groeiende gebruik van drones is er behoefte aan stille drones met een lange vliegduur en voldoende payload. De huidige commercieel verkrijgbare elektrisch aangedreven drones worden beperkt in vliegduur en payload door het gewicht en capaciteit van de baterijen. Brandstof aangedreven drones hebben weliswaar een groter bereik, maar zijn niet duurzaam en produceren veel meer geluid. Voor een toekomstbestendige ontwikkeling van onbemande luchtvaart, wil NLR in samenwerking met het Avy een grote stille waterstof drone ontwikkelen met een vliegduur van meerdere uren en een effectieve payload van 15 kg voor hoogwaardige toepassingen. Om in een stedelijke omgeving te kunnen opereren zal het toestel verticaal moeten kunnen opstijgen en landen, maar voor efficiënt brandstof gebruik zal het als een vliegtuig moeten kunnen vliegen, leidend tot een zogenaamde VTOL configuratie. De drone zal gevalideerd en gedemonstreerd worden in een gesimuleerde stedelijke omgeving. Voor deze stedelijke validatie wordt parallel een outdoor testfaciliteit, met een flexibele indeling d.m.v. Stelcon-wegen en tientallen gestapelde 20ft containers, opgebouwd. Om de invloed van de stedelijke omgeving op drones en omgekeerd in kaart te brengen wordt de faciliteit geïnstrumenteerd. Het project ondersteunt de Nederlandse ontwikkeling in het UrbanAirMobility domein en stimuleert daarmee zowel de industriële platform ontwikkeling als de initiële toepassing van UrbanAirMobility in Nederland. Het project richt zich primair op het vergroten van de mobiliteit, maar zal met de ontwikkeling van de eVTOL op waterstof ook een bijdrage leveren aan de duurzaamheid en klimaat en past daarmee binnen het key technology Future concepts van de HTSM Roadmap Aeronautics 2020 - 2025.
Aanvrager: Stichting Koninklijk Nederlands Lucht- en Ruimtevaartcentrum

Projecttitel: Scheepsdek windklimaatmetingen met Helium Filled Soap bubbles
Projectbeschrijving: Bij het NLR is een optische meettechniek ontwikkeld waarmee het mogelijk is met Helium Filled Soap Bubbles (HFSB) voor een groot volume (~1m3) het snelheidsveld op een instantaan ogenblik te meten. De te onderzoeken toepassing van deze meettechniek voor het uitvoeren van windklimaatmetingen op een scheepdek is nieuw en innovatief en kan gebruikt worden om het snelheidsveld rondom het schip te kunnen meten ten behoeve van bv. SHOL en SUOL (Ship UAV Operational Limits) vast  te stellen, maar ook om studies naar rookgashinder uit te kunnen voeren. Schaduwval door belemmeringen van de zichtlijn is een van grootste beperkingen van de techniek, waardoor in de praktijk nooit volledig rondom een object gemeten kan worden. In dit voorstel zal de meetmethodiek zelf zal ook verbeterd worden, zodanig dat het mogelijk is om volledige optische toegang te kunnen verkrijgen rondom het schip
Aanvrager: Stichting Koninklijk Nederlands Lucht- en Ruimtevaartcentrum

Projectbeschrijving: The goal is to study the options for a low-cost analogue phased array antenna to be connected to a commercial off the shelf (COTS) global navigation satellite system (GNSS) receiver chip.
The goal of this project is to optimize architecture for signal-processing algoritms and applications.

Projecttitel: MMF coherence tuning - Tuning spatial coherence via a multimode fiber for metrology
Projectbeschrijving: We will provide in-depth understanding of spatial coherence functions of light sources used for metrology. We will investigate how an optimized multimode fiber together with passive and active optical elements can be used to tune spatial coherence. The optimal system to control spatial coherence and wavefront of bright laser sources will be developed and demonstrated. The approach will allow to: (1) improve imaging quality (2) make the intensity and/or the phase response within small marks flatter (3) decrease the interaction with surrounding structures in order to improve alignment and/or overlay accuracy.

This project is devoted to developing and employing analytical and numerical modelling of hot and dense plasma under conditions relevant for state-of-the-art extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) nanolithography, where laser-driven plasma sources are used to provide the required EUV light. The research program includes the optimization of these plasma sources of EUV light. This work will be conducted at ARCNL by the plasma theory & modeling group, a new research group, in direct collaboration and communication with the EUV light source experts at ASML Research in San Diego and Veldhoven. This new group would provide important insights accompanying the experimental efforts of ARCNL's Source Department and moreover would be able to directly and independently answer some of the key open questions in the field. Moreover, it will provide predictive modeling capabilities to guide the development of next-generation EUV light sources.

The goal of ADiA-2021 is to reduce the amount of unscheduled down time of high-tech systems through the reduction of the time needed to diagnose the root cause of rare failures, by leveraging a methodology based on the combination of causal models and run time data. The causal models are developed using design and engineering knowledge, or automatically derived from design models. The heart of the methodology is a framework to establish the "diagnosability" of a high-tech system, guiding system architects and designers towards a system design and implementation that can be diagnosed: given a symptom of a failure, usually a combination of log data and sensor data, it is possible to identify the failed component. The ADiA-2021 project increases system dependability by improving system availability, addressing this issue as part of a systems' architecture. There is a clear fit with the HTSM Systems Engineering Roadmap high-tech product challenges (architecting/design for key system qualities, data analytics, information ), technology challenges (system health monitoring, diagnostics), and scientific challenges (dependability and related qualities, data management).
Aanvrager: Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk Onderzoek TNO

Projectbeschrijving: Maestro focuses on a model-based methodology and supporting tools for timing prediction and optimization. The timing prediction deals with analysis of variation points in the software, a sensitivity and robustness analysis on timing and on how to make timing predictions about configurations for which we do not yet have data. With a what-if scenario analysis we target to adjust a software platform to perform the computations within their timing requirements. Optimization will focus on finding the optimal system configurations for varying operating conditions based on design-space exploration. Focus for 2021 will be the study of runtime architectures, which should provide insights in the bottlenecks of application concurrency in the context of the computation platforms constraints. The second focus for 2021 is diagnose timing at system, not application software, level. For the ASML TWINSCAN that relates to the wafer process handling sequencing. Timing diagnostics at this level will be used to perform critical path analysis, application software budget analysis and to identify timing opportunities in resequencing the wafer process handling. There is a clear fit with the HTSM Systems Engineering Roadmap high-tech product challenges (architecting for key system qualities), technology challenges (system design with focus on performance, model-based system design and engineering), and scientific challenges (guaranteed functionality and performance).
Aanvrager: Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk Onderzoek TNO

Projectbeschrijving: After modelling the reference architecture for an existing product range (in the PaloAltoproject in 2019-2020), the PaloAlto2-project focuses on the reference architecture for the next generation of systems: (i) future market/business values and workflows, (ii) modelling/evaluating strategic architectural choices for the system. Envisioned business drivers are (amongst others): (i) configuration management, and (ii) the impact of the digital transition. There is a clear fit with the HTSM SE Roadmap high-techproduct and process challenges (platform-based, evolvable, digitalization), methodology challenges (model-based development, systems thinking, design for qualities, design for customer adaptations and also for architectures for data/AI-intensive systems), and scientific challenges (languages for MBSE, design space exploration, systematic analysis of/design for key system values, integral security).
Aanvrager: Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk Onderzoek TNO

Projectbeschrijving: Background: May high tech companies make families of products tailored to a wide range of different domains. The diversity of customer requirements is continuously increasing, and products are delivered in markets with a wide range of requirements for functionality and system performance: (i) entry-level systems, mid-range systems, high end systems; (ii) systems for a large variety of applications, etc. Furthermore, the role and value of application software packages (e.g. workflow software, image analysis and enhancement software, 3D image reconstruction, etc.) is growing. Depending on the market segment/application domain in which systems are delivered, the computing resources (processing power, storage, network bandwidth) required for these application software packages will vary. This calls for a software architecture that enables scalable deployment scenarios to assure optimal system performance on an optimal system configuration (i.e., without over dimensioning systems with abundant computing resources)..Project goal including fit Roadmap(s): This a pre-study to explore the state-of-the-art/practice of methods, tools, concepts and technologies for creating such scalable software architectures and to evaluate this in industrial Proofs of Concept of TFS. The topics addressed in the project are relevant in view of needs and trends in the wider high-tech industry, like those found in the HTSM SE Roadmap: design for customer adaptations, design for system (of system) qualities, adaptivity and run-time optimization, resource planning and scheduling, exploiting hybrid computer platforms. They are relevant for the roadmap of ESI in view of the strong focus on optimized (Continuously Evolving) customer-specific (Series-of-One) systems that are to be integrated in customer-specific (Systems-of-Systems) workflows..Utilization: The results of this project will enable ESI to (i) refine their applied research roadmaps and (ii) disseminate the results to the Dutch high-tech industry. Since the project is done in close cooperation (and at location) with TFS, using their industrial proofs of concept, deployment will be an integral of the project (the ESI industry-as-lab approach). Generic results will be made available to the high-tech industry via dedicated consolidation, dissemination and competence development activities.
Aanvrager: Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk Onderzoek TNO

Projectbeschrijving: The goals of the project are twofold: First to visualize key system parameters of dynamically evolving systems, both at design time and run-time. Secondly to vertically integrate system engineering models into software engineering models and map functional and non-functional requirements on a component-based system in such a way that we can reason about the match between requirements and implementation. There is a clear fit with the HTSM Systems Engineering roadmap high-tech product  challenges (platform-based, evolvable, digitalization), methodology challenges (modelbased development, systems thinking, design for qualities, design for customer adaptations and also for architectures for data/AIintensive systems), and scientific challenges (languages for MBSE, design space exploration, systematic analysis of/design for key system values, integral security)
Aanvrager: Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk Onderzoek TNO

Projectbeschrijving: A high-tech system-of-systems test environment has two main design axes: the structure of the system-of-systems (SoS), and the tests. The connections and interactions between the individual systems, or components, of a SoS are increasingly complex. Using models to describe SoSs improves the flexibility and effectiveness of high-tech test environments. In the TheXel-2021 project a modelling approach based on domain specific languages (DSLs) is used to specify these models. A SoS' capabilities are often described in terms of features, where one feature may be realized by a set of components. Testing a feature can be sped up if only the functionality of the components for a particular feature are tested, called featurebased testing, instead of the complete functionality of a component. The project will develop a DSL allowing the modeling of the relation between features and component functionality. To establish the quality of tests, we will develop a DSL to express the coverage of a set of tests. This project adds an abstraction layer enabling the test engineer to express compositional test cases in terms of system applications. The TheXel-2021 project increases system dependability by improving test coverage and test efficiency. There is a clear fit with the HTSM Systems Engineering Roadmap technology challenges (system integration and test, model-based system design and engineering ), and scientific challenges (system dependability).
Aanvrager: Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk Onderzoek TNO

Projectbeschrijving: The Transposition 2021 project's goal is to finalize the proof-of-concept of the model-based methodology on scalable relearning of software component behavior by observing and inferring module interfaces on both provided and required interfaces. The focus will be on validating the most promising techniques: constructive model inference and interface behavior comparison, used to analyze changes in behavior for different system scenarios and profiles. Projectbeschrijving: Haemoglobin (Hb) concentration in blood is used for many applications in the medical field, e.g. for.anaemia diagnosis, to screen blood donors, and in transfusion guidance. The need to draw blood for.Hb concentration analysis is undesirable for several reasons, including discomfort to the patient, the.time required of medical personnel to draw and handle the samples, and the potential risk of.spreading blood-borne diseases through punctures of the skin. Furthermore, studies have.demonstrated a large variability in Hb measurements obtained from successive drops of fingerpick.blood, which may cause problems for clinical decision making..The eye provides a unique location in the human body with visual access to blood vessels. The blood.vessels in the retina are located very superficially, are optically well accessible, and thus provide a.unique access point for Hb concentration estimation due to the lack of thick overlying tissues present.elsewhere in the body. We will here investigate the feasibility of measuring Hb concentration noninvasively.in retinal vessels using a fundus camera that could ultimately become suitable for use in.primary care, to screen blood donors and in low resource settings. In this TKI project, we will address.the light transport in retinal tissue and use these results to experimentally investigate the feasibility.of the approach..One sponsor (Sanquinnovate) provides the required in cash and in kind contributions.

Projecttitel: HEMA3 - High Efficiency integrated Module for Active Antenna Array at Ka-band
Projectbeschrijving: The goal of the project is to research and demonstrate an innovative high efficiency integrated Active Antenna module for Ka-band HTSC terminals based on array antennas.  Currently the main-stream approach for Active Array Antenna terminals at these frequencies consists of implementing all RF functions on the silicon IC and using very complex substrates. Functionality of such architecture has been proven, but the thermal management and overall efficiency are considered to be insufficient. Our focus is in optimizing the performance of the radiator- Power Amplifier (PA) building block: Altum RF will contribute through the research and development of a state-of-the-art Ka-band GaN Power Amplifier and the manufacture of a proof-of-concept hardware demonstrator; TNO will contribute through the research and proof-of-concept design of the array antenna; the integrated antenna-PA module and the measurement of this module. The benefit will be in a more cost-effective solution for active array antennas due to better performance and higher efficiency. A follow-up step of this research (not in this project) will be the co-design of the antenna and PA for optimized performance. The success of this project will rely in a novel combination of expertise and heritage of the partners: the array antenna and MMIC expertise at TNO and the MMIC and packaging expertise at Altum RF. The research topics addressed within this project fit well with the Key Enabling Technology of Engineering and Fabrication and are in line with the objectives of the HTSM Roadmap Space. Moreover, the knowhow developed in the frame of the project will support the objectives prioritized by the NSO "Active array antenna roadmap" and the NSO "Communication Systems Roadmap - RF part".

Projecttitel: End-to-end performance telemetry applied to SXR in the Classroom
Projectbeschrijving: In the Programmable, Integrated Telemetry (PIT) research project in 2020 it was demonstrated how monitoring data can be       collected from multiple network domains. By correlating network telemetry with application telemetry and application-hosting       cloud telemetry an end-to-end telemetry system can be developed that enables end-to-end performance telemetry. Such       telemetry systems are essential for validating and improving the Quality of Experience (QoE) of real-time services. For       example, the successful introduction of Augmented and virtual reality (XR) services will require a satisfactory QoE for XR users.       As identified by members of SURF, XR in the classroom provides an opportunity for innovating educational services.       The objective of this project is to extend the network telemetry results from the PIT project by integrating telemetry       solutions that collect monitoring data from the multiple network domains with the measurements from the other XR service       components and cloud systems hosting XR applications. Further, the telemetry data will be correlated to user experienced       quality, such that the telemetry data can be used for diagnostic purposes and (ultimately) to be used to re-program the XR       (network) system in run-time for the selected metric.       The project uses the results of PIT project, as well as TNO's ERP SXR Integration Line demonstrator. SURF will use       the results for further exploration how end-to-end performance telemetry can improve the QoE for delivery of real-time services,       such as XR in the classroom. Also, this project results will be used by the TNO ERP SXR for enhancing the SXR platform with       advanced telemetry functionality which can further be used in the research on creating sense on togetherness in XR.

Projectbeschrijving: Security of digital communications and infrastructure is of paramount importance, also illustrated by      the impact of recent cyber-attacks of the University of Maastricht , NWO and Hogeschool van      Amsterdam, and EMA. The risk of cyber threats will increase even more with the expected arrival of      quantum computers within the next ~10-20 yrs, which will be able to crack most of the currently used      asymmetric cryptosystems for secure communication (e.g. RSA), due to fundamentally improved      computing capabilities exploiting quantum mechanical effects such as superposition and      entanglement. As a possible solution, new cryptographic techniques are proposed based on      mathematically hard problems, that are even challenging for a future quantum computer. However,      these cryptographic schemes will always have an important limitation, namely that they will remain      computationally, and not information-theoretically secure. This means that there will always be a risk      that in due time new quantum algorithms will be developed which will be able to crack these      encryption schemes in a limited time. As a promising alternative, Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is      an increasingly accepted means for future secure communication thanks to its capability to securely      distribute symmetric keys which can then serve as input to quantum-safe encryption protocols such      as one-time pad or Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). In a prior TKI project, GEOQKD, TNO and      Eutelsat designed a disruptive implementation of QKD from a satellite on a Geostationary orbit      (GEO), which resulted in a patent which is currently being filed. It concerns a hybrid configuration of      QKD in which the QKD system can either be used in 'untrusted' or 'trusted' mode, or in combination.      This allows for a tuneable security, meaning that the user can choose for ultimate security using the      'untrusted' mode only, or combine it with keys from the 'trusted' mode in which key material must      temporarily be stored on board of the satellite. In the current proposed project, we would like to build      forwards on the results from GEOQKD related to the implementation of a hybrid QKD configuration.      The research will in the short term allow us, and our partner Eutelsat, to understand and evaluate the      performance of the hybrid QKD service from a GEO stationary satellite with the aim of guaranteeing      safe and secure communications without the need for a costly Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite      constellation. In the long term, a global quantum-safe key distribution service could be realized, acting      as critical infrastructure for banks, governments, Defence and industry.

Also, interest in SEA L4 (safe) autonomous driving is shown by distribution centers, airports and large business areas. As it's is easier to get the safety in place in confined areas, a high level of automation can be implemented more easily and quickly. However, a safety concept suitable for use on public roads reaches deep into the vehicle's architecture. As rewriting software is very expensive, the research question is whether it is possible to construct an architecture (via vehicle control interfaces) with the proper growth pad towards future public road usage that enables real-life tests and experiments in confined areas...The aim of this project is to develop an initial concept definition of vehicle control interface (including low-level motion controllers) for road legal tractors such that they can easily be deployed for automated driving in confined areas as well as manually driven transport on public road. Projectbeschrijving: Particles cannot be tolerated in Semicon equipment, e.g. wafer scanners. With demands for increasingly smaller feature sizes requirements on particle number quantity and size become even more stringent/bottleneck. Gas flushing (countercurrent flow and cross flow flushing) is applied to keep particles away from delicate ultra clean optical components (reticles and mirrors), however degrading the required vacuum, or leading to undesired effects like gas expansion/compression thermal loads and pressure fluctuations. Particle and flow interaction at low pressure is less well understood than at continuum conditions, where for example gas-slip reduces the particle drag. For the design of efficient particle flushing strategies accurate quantification of these effects is essential. The goal of the project is quantifying low pressure neutral particle drag, to be used in design tools for particle flushing strategies in Semicon equipment.

Projecttitel: mcSLO - Retinal oximetry using multicolor Scanning Laser Ophthalmoscopy
Projectbeschrijving: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a medical condition in which damage occurs to the retina due to diabetes mellitus. DR is the result of damage to the small blood vessels and neurons of the retina. The earliest changes leading to diabetic retinopathy include narrowing of the retinal arteries associated with reduced retinal blood flow. Later, the basement membrane of the retinal blood vessels thickens, capillaries degenerate and lose cells, particularly pericytes and vascular smooth muscle cells. This leads to loss of blood flow and progressive ischemia, and microscopic aneurysms which appear as balloon-like structures jutting out from the capillary walls..Age Related Macular Degeneration (AMD) exists in two forms: dry AMD, characterized by degeneration of the macula pigment epithelium cells, (80-90% of cases), and wet AMD, characterized by abnormal blood vessel growth (10-20% of cases). Wet AMD progresses rapidly and accounts for 90% of the cases of legal blindness. The macula receives the highest blood flow of any tissue in the body when related to size, and anything that can reduce the rich blood supply can cause hypoxia, malfunction, and disease. Therefore, characterization of oxygen saturation as surrogate marker of hypoxia may be a suitable early diagnostic indicator of progression to wet AMD. The ability to predict transitions, especially to wet AMD, will enable treatment before irreversible vision loss has occurred...We will in this project combine OCT-angiography with multicolor SLO-based retinal oximetry to attempt to determine local blood distribution and oxygenation levels in retinal arteries and veins as small as 50 micrometers. The multimodal research device that will be developed will enable us to optimize the existing oximetry algorithms, where optimization will be based on Monte Carlo simulations that include the 3D location of the blood vessels extracted from the OCT-A scan. The performance of the system and algorithms will be validated on model eyes that should be developed for this specific purpose. Specifically, such a model eye should contain flow channels containing blood of controlled flow velocity and oxygen saturation. Clinical pilot studies of 10 DR patients, 10 AMD patients and 10 healthy volunteers will be performed to investigate if local variations in oxygenation between DR, AMD and healthy retinas can be distinguished using this multimodal approach.

Projecttitel: APP - Alliance for Privacy Preserving Detection of Financial Crime
Projectbeschrijving: Financial crime is a large world-wide challenge. In 2018, an estimated 5.8 trillion dollars (6.7% of global GDP)        worth of financial crime was perpetrated. International collaboration between banks is essential to keep up        with advanced money laundering strategies. However, just sharing client data for collaborative money        laundering detection is not desirable or even legal due to trust, confidentiality and regulations. In the previous        TKI HTSM research project MPC4AML we developed a methodology that enables collaborative money        laundering detection without disclosing the underlying (sensitive) data by making use of Multi-Party        Computation (MPC).        The goal of this joint research program is to extend the set of Proof-of-Concept software solutions for privacypreserving        collaborative detection of financial crime (DFC) and to develop pilots for one-time application of        privacy-preserving analysis on real production data to validate the developed technical solutions. Our goal is to        collaborate on the following topics:        - Moving from synthetic data to pilot experiments with real data to validate the results.        - Design synthetic data generator to obtain realistic financial data for testing algorithms and to get        academics involved and invested in developing DFC algorithms and technology.        - Develop larger set of algorithms for Anti-Money Laundering, Know Your Customer, fraud detection        and other forms of DFC.        This program seizes the societal relevance and strategic importance on privacy-by-design technologies, that        are applicable on large-scale international data. This enables to show the value of collaboration: expanding        and unifying all partners' knowledge about the data leading to improved quality of alerts that relate to        financial crime. By moving from the current Proof-of-Concept to establishing a pilot on operational data is the        potential start of a paradigm shift. We will further investigate how different privacy enhancing technologies        can effectively be combined to create more efficient solutions and eventually fight financial crime on        international scale.        The program consists of three tracks:        - Track 1 will investigate how privacy preserving technologies such as MPC, can be applied to already        existing or new detection algorithms for Know-Your-Customer (KYC), fraud detection or Anti-Money        Laundering (AML). One use case will be worked out into Proof-of-Concept.        - Track 2 will extend the previous work on Secure Risk Propagation for money laundering detection.        The previous research offers us a starting point for taking this use case a step further by performing a        pilot on operational data of multiple banks. This will enable us to answer research questions on a        technical, legal and organizational level. Next to researching use cases related to financial crime, we        would also like to extend the knowledge on privacy preserving technology in general.        - Track 3 will look into active security, synthetic data generation and the possibilities of an MPC        platform.        The results of program contribute to the main goal: to improve the effectiveness of detecting financial crime        by enabling national and international collaboration using privacy enhancing technologies.

AR is recognized as a promising technology also for advanced industrial applications. Projecttitel: FIP2.0 - Complex Fluids on Complex Substrates
Projectbeschrijving: Inkjet printing technologie wordt gekenmerkt door hoge productiviteit, voortdurende volumetrische miniaturisatie, en extreme reproduceerbaarheid. Ondanks de lange historie als een grafische reproductie techniek staat inkjet printing nog steeds in de frontlinie van high-tech fabricage technieken, aangedreven door voortdurende intensieve technologische ontwikkelingen. Inkjet printing is een sleuteltechnologie voor veel toepassingsgebieden, zoals het printen van zonnecellen, rapid prototyping, geprinte elektronica, en zelfs het printen van DNA en proteïnes. De volgende generatie van inkjet-printing technologieën is gebaseerd op vloeistoffen die zijn opgebouwd uit meerdere componenten en oplossingen met gefunctionaliseerde deeltjes, om zo een ongekende veelzijdigheid en controle van het printproces te bereiken. De huidige wetenschappelijke kennis van complexe vloeistoffen en van de interactie van dergelijke vloeistoffen met complexe substraten is echter nog incompleet. Het ComplexFS project richt zich op de ontwikkeling van modellen en simulatie technieken om het gedrag van complexe vloeistoffen, en de interactie daarvan met complexe substraten, te beschrijven. ComplexFS is onderdeel van de tweede tranche van het meerjarig onderzoeksprogramma Fundamental Fluid Dynamics Challenges in Inkjet Printing (FIP), waarin TU/e, Canon Production Printing, UT en UU intensief en langdurig samenwerken om de openstaande wetenschappelijke vraagstukken op het gebied van het gedrag van complexe vloeistoffen te beantwoorden en de leidende positie van Nederland op het gebied van inkjet-printing technologie te versterken. Het ComplexFS project is opgebouwd uit vier complementaire promotieprojecten en heeft een beoogde looptijd van 2021-2026.

Projecttitel: Mi-RAYS - Multi-mode high resolution automotive radar with dense analog to information converter arrays
Projectbeschrijving: High resolution mm-wave automotive radars transform cars into securely connected self-driving robots capable for cognitive perception of the environment, able to process information and act autonomously. This requires concepts that achieve much higher resolution, have smaller size, and create more information, compared to today's state of art 77 GHz radars. A paradigm shift is required moving to smaller mm-wave wavelengths to enable new ranging and sensing concepts. In this project, NXP and TU/e will develop novel 140 GHz radar antenna and frontend IC technology to achieve ultra-high range, angular and velocity resolution. This will enable high quality imaging radar, localization, mapping, and enhanced object classification capabilities. The specific objectives of this project are: to overcome radar system size limitations of today's 77 GHz sensors; to exploit heterogeneous and co-functional integration concepts in the front-ends such as dual 77 / 140 GHz waveguide launchers that greatly enrich and simplify the radar system; to design breakthrough performance building blocks such as transmitters with arbitrary waveform modulators that support orthogonality for very dense antenna arrays; to develop analog-to-information converters overcoming data rate explosion due to massive bandwidth and array sizes.

Projecttitel: PICOSTAR - Photonic Integrated COherence Scrambler Through phased Arrays
Projectbeschrijving: Optical sensors for metrology are essential in the semiconductor industry, for example to create highly accurate nanometer scale structures in integrated circuits. With the advent of extreme ultraviolet lithography, transistors of a few nanometers can now be made. This means that the sensors must also be able to provide information on the nanometer scale. Many of these sensors work with an optical broadband source, so-called white light. By extending this bandwidth further, to the ultraviolet and infrared, these sensors can be made more accurate. A promising source for this broadband light is a so-called supercontinuum laser. This is a pulsed laser, the bandwidth of which is increased by means of optical nonlinearities. Since these pulses are mutually coherent, this leads to problems with interference. Multiple optical spatial modes in the illumination system lead to a varying pattern in the illumination, leading to errors in the sensor. Interference from reflections in the system can also lead to errors. The question is therefore how both the spatial and temporal coherence of the light can be broken, so that the sensor can work more accurately. PICOSTAR's approach is to add a photonic integrated circuit, or an optical chip, to the laser output. This optical chip will be used as a so-called optical antenna array. By splitting the laser light over different waveguides on the chip, and then modulating the phase of the light in these waveguides separately, the temporal coherence is broken. At the output of the chip, these waveguides are recombined, with rapidly varying phase profiles. This leads to very rapidly varying illumination patterns, which are averaged out by the detector in the sensor to a uniform illumination, which also breaks the spatial coherence.
Partners: ASML Netherlands B.V., Technische Universiteit Eindhoven

Projecttitel: PISANO - Perinatal care Interventions, Sleep Apnea and New Opportunities for peri-operative monitoring
Projectbeschrijving: Demographic changes induce an ever-higher burden on the healthcare system. Early detection of complications and diseases and the determination of effective personalized treatments are essential to lower this burden, to prevent comorbidities, and to lower healthcare costs while simultaneously improving patient outcome and quality of life.  The PISANO project proposed here seeks to leverage technological advances in pathophysiological modeling, unobtrusive sensing, monitoring and artificial intelligence (AI) towards this end. A major thrust is on radical innovations towards widespread use of ultrasound (US) technology. Wearable US cuffs will enable continuous peri-operative monitoring to detect hemodynamic instabilities; AI algorithms will be developed to improve image quality and ease-of-use of US; and the effectiveness of IntraVascular US will be enhanced through AI algorithms trained on synthetic data from a physically accurate image simulator. For Obstructive Sleep Apnea patients, we will measure sleep parameters to enhance the effectiveness, personalization and adherence of positive airway pressure treatment, which currently suffers from low adherence. To improve the monitoring and risk management of pregnancies, novel wearable fetal monitoring technologies will be developed, capable e.g. of keeping track of fetal movements. The general approach in PISANO is to co-develop novel technological solutions in a controlled clinical environment, and to subsequently refine and validate them in extramural and at-home settings, immediately followed by deployment in the healthcare system with the aim to increase effectiveness at lower costs in combination with lower patient burden and higher patient quality of life.

Half the cost of a new charging station can be the cost of grid connection. This leads to a configuration using a local battery to reduce the peak power demands. This can be implemented either with an AC or DC coupling configuration. In this project we intend to concentrate on the latter DC coupling configuration due to lower losses and some novel technology elements.

Projecttitel: MALIOD - Machine Learning to improve Illumination Optics Design
Projectbeschrijving: In the last decade good progress has been made on solving inverse problems for illumination optics (given the source and target light distributions, calculate the lens/reflector surfaces at once). This type of technology is actively used in industry..However, the physics is not complete: aspects like Fresnel reflections, non-ideal sources, absorption and scattering are not taken into account. Modelling these is extremely difficult and therefore we propose to take an alternative route. This approach implies to use the inverse tools to generate a library of optical designs, to use advanced simulation technologies to incorporate the above effects and to use artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques to give a suggestion for the best design for a given source and target distribution. The goal of this research is to develop an algorithm that supports engineers in illumination optics design by selecting the most suitable optical architecture and design for the illumination task at hand.

Projecttitel: MIEP - MEMS materials in EUV-induced plasma
Projectbeschrijving: Micro scanning mirrors are tiny devices used for dynamic light modulation for numerous applications, such as fast optical switches (telecommunications), LIDAR sensors (automotive), and in vivo diagnostics (healthcare). Application of arrays of such devices in EUV lithography tools would bring obvious benefits in performance, yield and accuracy, increasing productivity and lowering cost. However, all the optical elements in the EUV scanner are exposed to EUV and EUV-induced hydrogen plasma, which is a very aggressive environment. The materials used to fabricate micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) must be able to remain functional in this complex environment of electrically and chemically active components and strong electric fields. They are also not allowed to contaminate the plasma, which would lead to deterioration of mirror surfaces and thereby to reduction of lifetime and availability. Thorough fundamental understanding of the interaction between EUV induced plasma and MEMS materials is needed to assess the feasibility of using these promising devices in a realistic scanner environment. In the MIEP project the behaviour of MEMS materials is analysed when exposed to different stressors: hydrogen plasma, EUV and heat. The goal is to understand and mitigate the risks posed by applying these materials in EUV scanners.

Projecttitel: CREW - Compressed Representations for Efficient Workflows
Projectbeschrijving: It covers large-scale data processing and supports collaborative workflows, related to manufacturing processes. Efficient access to all data targets velocity and "real-time performance"(2.7). The representation can be considered a new database architecture, tackling response times and interactive exploration (3.4.2). The work is T-shaped(3.5) with many application domains for example, 1D (gene analysis) and 3D (printing and compression/visualization). Collaborative workflows touch many other themes, such as "human assisted processing and visualization of big data"(smart cities), as interactions with large-scale city scans and recording of modifications by many users relates to democratizing planning or safety discussions.

Projecttitel: Electronics validation platform for QuTech demonstrator and experimental quantum science
Projectbeschrijving: is to develop a stand-alone validation platform allowing complete regression tests of software and firmware upgrades for existing instruments and the bring-up of new instruments for commercialization, without requiring down-time for QI-Starmon or scientific setups, and with which ZI and QuTech engineers can collaborate in person.  This effort is key to achieving the target of controlling the 17-qubit superconducting systems for use as NISQ devices in QI-Starmon (benefitting also the semiconducting backend of QI, which also uses ZI electronics) and targeted for quantum error correction in DiCarlo lab. This TKI grant fits within the objectives of the National Agenda Quantum Technologies, and contribute  to the strengthening of the Dutch quantum ecosystem by developing demonstrators, such as the QuTech Quantum Inspire platform.

Projecttitel: SAFER - Scientific Approach for developing a Fire safety Economics decision-making Roadmap
Projectbeschrijving: This project aims at developing a roadmap to complement insights gained from fire safety engineering calculations with insights from fire safety economic calculations. The general research question is the following: "How can a roadmap be scientifically developed such that economic information becomes part of the fire prevention decision-making process?"

Projecttitel: Advanced electronics for low-energy electron detectors
Projectbeschrijving: The goal of this project is to investigate and provide integrated solutions (ASIC) for the readout electronics of the sensor module for the next generation high-resolution and high-speed SEM. To achieve this goal: (i) new innovative circuit solutions and architectures will be investigated, using advanced CMOS production processes. The propose solutions should be able to sense very weak currents, as well as single electrons (electron-counting mode of operation) (ii) options will be considered for two different kind of electron detectors: PIN detectors and avalanche detectors (SPAD, SiPM, APD (iii) the possibility to integrate the readout electronics together with the electron detector in system-on-chip (SOC) or in system-in-package (SIP) will be studied, as well.

Projecttitel: AI techniques for automotive radar signal processing and SLAM
Projectbeschrijving: While AI algorithms are successfully used for optical image processing, their application to radar signals remain a major challenge due to different nature of radar signals. To achieve breakthrough in environment perception with radars, novel AI applications in the entire radar signal processing pipeline needs to be developed to fully utilize the unique modality of radar signals, which is unlike camera and lidars. Solutions for 3 critical radar signal processing challenges will be pursued: Direction of Arrival Estimation and Super resolution in azimuth;  Simultaneous Localization and Mapping of the environment; AI for tracking applications in autonomous driving.  The project goals will help move from situational awareness towards cooperative, reactive, adaptive and predictive perception of environment around automotive vehicles.

Projecttitel: DRASTIC WBC - Digital tRAnSmiTter ICs for WideBand Com
Projectbeschrijving: The development of SG communication equipment is addressing the ever-growing societal demand for more and faster data access, anywhere, anytime. However, the current SG system prototypes show that this SG functionality will come at a significant financial and environmental (CO2 ) foot print. The aim of this project is to lower cost level, as well as, the energy consumption of these systems. This will be done by replacing the analogue TX lineups, which are the most power hungry components, by highly integrated fully digital solutions, so that these systems can be strongly simplified and save on real estate cost, as well as, operating cost. As such, this project addresses both societal and environmental needs. On the economic level, Dutch industry e.g. Ampleon, and NXP belong to the largest in volume component suppliers for these SG systems. So progression in TX design knowledge, IP and training of new scientist in this research direction will help to keep the Netherlands at the frontline. While Nokia networks is in volume among the top three set makers of the world.
Partners: Ampleon Coöperatief U.A., Nokia Solutions and Networks Nederland

Projectbeschrijving: Detection of Heavy Metal Ions and Organic Compounds in Waste Water Using Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy - The wastewater needs to be treated to remove chemical contaminants before it can be discharged into the environment. Detection and quantification of organic and inorganic compounds in drained water is a key to assess the need and the type of water treatment for a specific end-use. Conventional pollution detection techniques are often expensive and not practical for onsite real-time monitoring. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is an electrochemical technique possessing great potential in providing detailed information about water composition by measuring the dependence of the AC potentials frequency. EIS has been implemented on various fundamental processes, i.e., adsorption/film formation, rate of charge transfer, ion exchange, diffusion, etc., indicating its potential for detection of the water composition.

Projecttitel: NOCAD - Mass saving of wing structures by using new design tools for commercial aircraft
Projectbeschrijving: The aim of the project is to increase the efficiency of the use of composites which will lead to significantly lighter structures. The challenge is that the design space of the airframe structure becomes too large to be searched efficiently using detailed stress models. The proposed approach is a multi-fidelity approach which combines lower-fidelity stick models, still capturing the essential structural dynamics, with more detailed structural solvers able to resolve the local structural effects such as structural stability. The combination of aerodynamics, structures and flight dynamics leads to relatively computationally expensive models.  Both the extended design space and the computational modelling cost challenges will be solved in the proposed project. The design space can, therefore, be searched in an efficient manner, increasing the chances to find the optimum low-weight design.

Projecttitel: MEMS-based optics for high-resolution electron microscopy
Projectbeschrijving: We propose to design and construct MEMS-based electron microscope components such as aberration correctors and beam-splitters for high-resolution microscopy (Roadmaps Advanced Instrumentation & Nanotechnology). We will study the electron optics performance of designed and fabricated components both experimentally and via computer simulations, including study of the interaction of energetic electrons with the micron- and nanoscale patterned features that form the functional units in the MEMS-components (Roadmap Nanotechnology).

Projecttitel: Metrology, physically correct modeling and full surface specification
Projectbeschrijving: The goal is to develop physically correct modeling of the impact on optical image quality of surface profile imperfections over a large range of spatial frequencies. There are known problems with these models in the mid spatial frequency domain were calculation results are inaccurate. Moreover, it is an unsolved problem how to correctly combine results from two different models (for low and high spatial frequencies respectively). In addition to these modeling issues there are also significant challenges in specifying surface tolerances such that it can be measured in a meaningful way.

Projecttitel: Quasi-Optical MIMO Antennas for Line of Sight Wireless Links at H-band
Projectbeschrijving: Wireless communication will use the H-band (220-325GHz) with antenna MIMO architectures in the near future . Integrated technology at such frequencies has problems to generate power,  amplifiers are non-linear, and introduces high levels of noise. In this project, we study the use of electrically large apertures to reach energy efficient wireless links. Link distances within a few 100 meters can be effectively in the near-field and therefore the energy can be focalized leading to negligible propagation spreading losses. The great advantage of a near-field link, besides the need of very low level transmitted powers, is the large spatial multiplexing capability.

Koppert Biological Systems and Canopy Guard will test the e-noses on commercially relevant use cases with disruptive business potential and high societal impact (e.g. stop deforestation due to replacing infected plantations).

Projecttitel: DRASTIC WBC II - Digital tRAnSmiTter ICs for WideBand Com
Projectbeschrijving: Digital Transmitters (DTX) that provide direct conversion of the digital baseband data to RF power will be developed. The proposed direct massive digital control of tiny gate-segments in the RF output stage(s) allows perfect waveform shaping and device activation. These techniques directly addresses the needs of future (wireless) mMIMO base stations. By eliminating completely the need for analogue TX chain(s), almost a doubling of the average system efficiency is expected.  This project aims for the development of these new electronic devices and their application in a new generation of 5G mMIMO base station demonstrators, which will be jointly developed by the TU Delft, NOKIA and Ampleon.
Partners: Ampleon Coöperatief U.A., Nokia Solutions and Networks Nederland

Projecttitel: F-Minis - Miniaturized flow control components for integrated microfluidics
Projectbeschrijving: The goal is to develop a generic methodology and technology that enables the design and implementation of a portable application specific integrated microfluidic (ASIMs) system (See Figure). The two major steps to be taken to realize our vision are (1) developing a library of miniature flow control components, and (2) system integration. Therefore, we aim to work on the following challenges: a) Novel liquid flow-rate controller, 2) establish characterization methods for flow-control components, 3) investigate methods to fabricate a monolithic platform with integrated fluid and electrical layers with standardized connectors. 4) Implement a demonstrator. Projecttitel: MEGABeam - Metamaterial and Origami-based Beam Flexure for High-tech Precision Mechanisms
Projectbeschrijving: The aim of our research is to enable the design of origami-inspired flexure that utilize their internal creases and micro features (metamaterial-based) to achieve a spatially curved shape with a desired extreme anisotropic stiffness properties and large deflection, an artistic impression is shown in the picture. This project will contribute to two main HTSM roadmaps, including high-tech materials (Inc. designer functional metamaterials, and sustainable materials domains) and semiconductor manufacturing equipment (by contributing on lighter and energy efficient position stages that are able to achieve higher throughput).

Projecttitel: Miniature Low Power Hybrid Temperature sensors for Biomedical and IoT Applications
Projectbeschrijving: The main goal of the project is to realize hybrid temperature sensors that will combine multiple temperature sensing principle to simultaneously achieve small size, low power, high power efficiency and low-cost calibration. This will require the development of innovative readout architectures, the use of power-efficient continuous-time readout techniques and the use of advanced chip-scale packaging technology. The resulting sensors will be well suited for use in biomedical applications, and so the proposed research fits well within the priority area Healthy living and prevention of the HTSM Healthcare roadmap. The sensors can also be used in industrial and scientific instrumentation and as such, this research also fits well within the Electronics R&D roadmap 2.0.

Projecttitel: Understanding and mitigating mining-induced and climate-induced degradation of masonry
Projectbeschrijving: The aim is to develop and validate multi-scale models for masonry damage, and subsequently integrate these models into probabilistic frameworks for forecasting fragility and vulnerability of building stock with respect to ground movements. Nonlinear finite element models will be developed starting from the brick/joint micro scale all the way up to the large structural scale. Particular focus will be placed on splitting and crushing of calcium-silicate masonry and the performance of that masonry subjected to restrained shrinkage, under cumulative action by settlement  and earthquake-induced ground movements. In-plane walls will be tested in the lab with digital image correlation for validating the models. Innovative approaches to upgrade the masonry with bed-joint reinforcement or fibre-reinforced plasters will be studied.

Projecttitel: c-COOL - clay - CO2-Loading for Negative Emission Technologies and long term safe CO2 storage
Projectbeschrijving: The goal of the project is to explore and demonstrate the fundamental scientific basis of c-COOL technology and to identify optimum nano-materials and process conditions that will allow to judge the technological and economic potential of the approach. If successful, c-COOL can become a serious contender as a technology  to mitigate the worst consequences of climate change.

The scientific goal of the program is to create insight into unresolved issues in the current inkjet process and to improve and extend the functionality of the inkjet printing process to meet future requirements. The program combines experimental, numerical, and theoretical approaches and the objectives are at the core of the HTSM printing roadmap.

Projecttitel: INSPEXT - In-Situ Pellicle Exposure and Transmission
Projectbeschrijving: The goal of the project is to enable EUV exposure and in-situ transmission measurements at a synchrotron facility, enabling: Strong acceleration of pellicle materials development by time-resolved, direct observation of EUV- and plasma-driven degradation of existing and novel pellicle materials Deeper understanding of EUV-driven surface degradation processes, allowing improved modelling and scaling laws predicting pellicle lifetime Observation of laterally resolved degradation effects, comparing directly EUV-exposed areas to neighboring spots only effectively separating EUV-photon driven processes from secondary thermal / plasma degradation processes.

Projecttitel: NociTune - Neurophysiological biomarkers for early diagnostics and personalized treatment of chronic pain syndromes
Projectbeschrijving: The goal of this project is to further develop a new concept toward mechanism based markers for individual characterization of nociceptive dysfunction predictive for patients responses to treatment.
Partners: Centre for Human Drug Research (CHDR), NociTRACK B.V., Saluda Medical Netherlands B.V., Stichting Sint Antonius Ziekenhuis

Projecttitel: SPLASH - Systems and Portfolio development and Architecting using Systems engineering by Humans
Projectbeschrijving: In this research project ASML and the UT will research how to factor in the above mentioned aspects while increasing the state of the art  performance of the equipment, using a systems engineering approach on technological and organizational level. The central objective for  this challenging research project is to enable system architects in making founded and communicateable trade-offs spanning the entire lifecycle and as part of product portfolio, despite missing, incomplete and inaccurate information.

Projecttitel: The effectivity of hard chrome plating in cold rolling
Projectbeschrijving: This project will aim at unravelling the fundamental behaviour governing the complex physical, mechanical and chemical interactions of chrome-plating in cold rolling processes to enable future solutions for greener, more sustainable production

Projecttitel: ACTUATOR - Advancing Core Technologies by Unified Activities on Talent, Organization, and Research
Projectbeschrijving: As part of ACTUATOR, three R&D-projects have been defined with a strong focus on VDL ETG's core industry: semiconductor applications. The goal of the first project "Miniature superconducting actuators" is to realize a compact but powerful and low-dissipation voice-coil type actuator specifically designed for the manipulation of objects in cryogenic environments, e.g. mirrors in space and Big Science applications. The goal of the second project "3D deposition of magnetic structures" is to develop optimized nano-sheet buffered superconducting films on 3D functional substrates, building on the results of the first project. The goal of the third project "Research on Hydrogen-INduced Outgassing" (RHINO) is to enable the direct 'on-site and on-surface' detection of contamination for large steel or aluminum vacuum chamber components and to correlate such measurements to the contamination rate of EUVL optics.

Projecttitel: Innovative health monitoring for circular steel infrastructure - HiTMaT-25K2
Projectbeschrijving: Teneinde rond 2030 een duurzame en 50% circulaire economie te bereiken zijn vele technologische, organisatorische, institutionele en sociaaleconomische aanpassingen nodig. Grote stalen infrastructurele werken zoals bruggen beginnen hun "end-of-life cycle" te bereiken. In plaats van het geheel opnieuw construeren van dergelijke werken, beoogt het voorstel de ontwikkeling van nieuwe tools waarmee de gezondheid van het materiaal snel en precies kan worden gemonitord, en onderhoudscycli beter kunnen worden voorzien. https://www.hollandhightech.nl/innovative-health-monitoring-methods-boost-durability-steel-infrastructure

Projecttitel: PATIENCE2 - Patient-centric healthcare through nomadic sensing
Projectbeschrijving: The PATIENCE 2 project addressed three aspects which jointly contribute to the aim of instantiating a more open and novel ICT infrastructure for storing and processing patient data, where process stakeholders like institutes, equipment manufacturers and the patients themselves will have controlled access to that data and use it for a smooth and data-driven treatment. The first aspect is fast catheter detection in ultrasound imaging for interventions. Novel powerful catheter detection algorithms are being evaluated in a real-time experimental setting in order to translate these algorithms to a real-time system setup that enables a thorough practical evaluation of the catheter detection. The second aspect concerns a remote patient monitoring kit for clinical studies. Such outpatient monitoring kit comprises connectivity for monitoring devices, a telecommunications hub, and cloud software services. The kit is intended to be used during clinical studies and is being enhanced and matured with respect to automation and usability while fully respecting privacy. Thirdly, telerehibalitation of heart failure patients following acute decompensation is investigated to see if personalized telerehabilitation in recently hospitalized congestive heart failure (CHF) patients improves their physical function when compared to usual care. The program will be tailored based on remote monitoring of physical capacity, lifestyle behaviour and vital parameters while exploiting and evaluating parts of the outpatient monitoring kit mentioned before.

Projecttitel: Roboconnect - A robotic solution for live cable splicing
Projectbeschrijving: How can robotic technology play a role and have an impact on making these connections in a safe, manual labour saving and reliable manner. Making a connection with the currently used sleeve adapter (mof) in both the low and middle voltage net requires a large number of complicated manual actions such as removing the grounding shield (splicing), removing diverse insulation layers,('aanpellen'), measuring, dimensioning, cutting into the inner layers, etc. Both nets have different dimensions and cable types and use completely different systems, methods, components and tools for making connections.

Aanvrager: Stichting Koninklijk Nederlands Lucht- en Ruimtevaartcentrum

Projecttitel: Innovative Research of Multi-channel integrated diagnostic system in new Nuclear Fusion environment - Phase 3
Projectbeschrijving: The goal of this project is to research innovative technologies in specific nuclear fusion optical diagnostics areas. These include research of key optical diagnostic components; RF plasma cleaning technology inside the vacuum vessel, built-in calibration and alignment systems for continuous and reliable operation, and multi-channel optical instruments for plasma diagnostics. These technologies are applicable to most of the modern fusion facilities and are applicable to other markets as well involving harsh and complex environments. An important future diagnostic subsystem of the experimental nuclear fusion reactor ITER (Cadarache, France) is the Visible Spectroscopy Reference System (VSRS). As a main partner in an international consortium, TNO has the opportunity to research and design this particular subsystem. The front part of the system will operate in the extreme ITER vacuum and plasma environment. This means that during the design and engineering phase, a number of specific design challenges have to be faced to cope with the extreme environment for which no current solution exists. To bring the VSRS system development project in reach for TNO and partners, a TKI project is envisaged including an envisaged key development partner Advanced Space Technologies S.A. (AST) in Leidschendam. The Dutch Institute for Fundamental Energy Research (DIFFER) in Eindhoven supports the research from scientific point of view. In the course of the following development projects other Dutch contributors are foreseen e.g. Chromodynamics BV in Eindhoven and DRE Engineering B.V. in Noordwijk to prepare for these technological challenges. The technology research will create knowledge essential to bring TNO and the technology research partners in a position to offer the VSRS system to ITER with competitive technical maturity and reduced risks. The knowledge developed, and researched solutions will also be applicable in the core design processes that TNO and partners use in their Aerospace and Big Science projects, including future fusion facilities, such as DEMO, JT60-SA and DTT.
Aanvrager: Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk Onderzoek TNO

Projectbeschrijving: The application and utilization of atomized liquids is very diverse; in modern society almost every industry and household use some form of sprays. For example, liquid atomization is a well-known method for targeted drug delivery to the lung. As the inhalation route becomes more attractive for delivery of different types of drugs, besides those used for traditional asthma therapy, liquid atomization faces several challenges. To make best use of their ability to target specific areas of the lung, control in drop size is needed to increase efficacy. But also for paint and agricultural spraying, home and personal care products and foods sprays are omnipresent. For all of these applications the drop size and its distribution have to be controlled, which is at the heart of this proposal..We will develop new methodologies for the controlled atomization of liquids in collaboration with Medspray, an SME that sells nozzle technology to, amongst others, the pharmaceutical industry. Medspray is a fast growing company with currently 40 employees, and will have an estimated 60 employees by the end of this year. has developed a new cleanroom technology for manufacturing ultra-precise nozzles. Besides the controlled mass manufacturing of precision nozzles with the aid of semiconductor technology, the second important focus of Medspray is control over spray formation and performance. The main challenges we will address in the proposal are therefore to achieve versatility in generating micron and submicron droplets, ability to obtain narrow droplet-size distributions, working in a wide range of liquid viscosities and densities, ability to achieve high atomization doses suitable for pharmaceutical and biological materials, and a focus on environmental friendliness by spraying without the need of using propellants..From the fundamental side, there is an increasing scientific interest in and understanding of atomization, with research aiming to relate the properties of the atomized liquids to the drop size (distribution) under different conditions, such as the atomization method used and the use of formulations with different rheological properties. Recent advances in spraying and atomization technologies exercised in various fields have shown that a spray with a narrow drop-size distribution, or even a monodisperse spray, may be advantageous for many applications. Sprays with monodisperse droplets with a controlled trajectory and with micron to sub-micron sizes are however difficult to generate.
Partners: Medspray Technology & Manufacturing, Nederlandse organisatie voor wetenschappelijk onderzoek (NWO)

Projecttitel: SPARSITY - Using data from sparse measurements for predictive maintenance
Projectbeschrijving: Vehicles, manufacturing and printing equipment, consumer and medical devices, robots, wind turbines: they are examples of systems that could benefit from Predictive Analytics (PA). For instance, PA can leverage data science to improve service life through predictive maintenance and to build better ones via predictive design. An outstanding challenge for PA is the need of large amounts of data to develop, identify and validate algorithms. One way to overcome data scarcity is via synthetic data generation from so called Digital Twins (DT), that is dynamical mathematical models that are used in lieu of the physical system, even before it is built. Anyway, DT models development still need data. We plan to solve this conundrum by extending modelling and identification methodologies in order to cope with a particular kind of data scarcity: data sparsity. We will target cases were data is not continuously available over time, and fragmented over a large population of similar devices. This is relevant for mass-produced systems where practical reasons prevent data to be collected, transmitted and processed continuously for the entire population. This novel approach will be validated in an industrial Proof of Concept for the diagnosis and prognosis of real automotive components.

High-speed ADCs are key components of modern radio and radar systems. However, the drive  to carry out more and more of the associated signal processing in the digital domain, i.e. after the ADC, puts increasingly stringent demands on ADC performance. The main goal of this project is to develop new architectures for high-speed ADCs in advanced CMOS processes, which should achieve wide BW (100s of MHz) without compromising their linearity and resolution (noise), while still consuming reasonable amounts (< 1W) of power. The project will be carried out by researchers from the TU Delft and from NXP Semiconductors.

Projecttitel: ACACIA - Advancing Cancer care And Cardiac care through Interpretable AI
Projectbeschrijving: Cardiac diseases and cancer are among the world's leading causes of death. The ACACIA project aims to advance cancer and cardiac care with Artificial Intelligence (AI), taking a patient-centered and physician-centered approach to address unresolved challenges that hamper adoption of AI in clinical practice. For cancer, early detection, timely and accurate diagnosis and staging, and subsequent selection of the appropriate treatment for each patient are critical factors to improve patient outcomes. Diagnostic imaging plays an integral role in many phases of a patient's care path. The project will build on the recent developments of AI technology to better support image analysis, achieve earlier detection and better characterization of cancer and improve monitoring of response to treatment. It will shape optimal physician-AI collaboration and develop tools and methods for bringing AI to clinical practice and evaluate actual use, trust, and experience with AI. Cardiac patients recovering from surgery in the Intensive Care Unit are at significant risk of shock, infections, and sepsis. In addition, medical ICU staff is spending a considerable amount of time in bookkeeping and patient handover. AI-based medical predictive models are capable of detecting risk of deterioration of these patients in an earlier stage than in current practice. The resulting AI-based clinical decision support tools, in combination with workflow support and user-centered visualizations, will enable significant improvement of ICU performance and patient care.
Partners: Philips Electronics Nederland B.V., Stichting Catharina Ziekenhuis

Projecttitel: Auto-AR - Automated Situated Design of Augmented Hearing Reality Algorithms
Projectbeschrijving: Hearing aid (HA) clients need a personalized and acoustic scene-dependent audio processing algorithm. Therefore, HA algorithms should preferably be designed automatically (i.e., without engineers in the loop) and in-the-field when the environmental conditions and personal expectations can be measured, i.e., under "situated" conditions. Brains provide an inspiring example for automated situated algorithm design. After all, brains design algorithms for speech and object recognition, for locomotion, etc., through situated interactions between the brain and its environment without engineers in the loop. Over the past decade, a large body of theoretical neuroscience work, covered by the umbrella term "the Free Energy Principle" (FEP), has revealed the underlying physical principles of the brain's automated algorithm design method. The central challenge in this project is to transfer FEP-based design from an academic neuroscientific interest to a robust and practical engineering method, in particular in the context of situated HA design. In this project we will develop a FE minimizing agent that is capable automated situated design of an algorithm that can attenuate or enhance any of the constituent source signals in an acoustic mixture. Moreover, the project will develop an open-source engineering toolbox that can be utilized to specify FE minimizing agents for alternative applications.

Projecttitel: RAISE - Robust AI for SafE (radar) signal processing
Projectbeschrijving: The RAISE project aims to develop AI technologies that can strongly advance the robustness, safety and general performance of car radars, as well as the robustness and performance of adaptive multichannel filters as used in digital radio and hearing aids. Moreover, RAISE will explore AI techniques that can help to strongly improve the efficiency of the IC design and validation process. To these ends RAISE involves a close collaboration between key AI experts of TU/e with key industrial IC design, engineering and application experts. This collaboration will enable the project to develop synergistic combinations of data driven and model-based approaches, thus supporting a shift of the performance-efficiency-robustness boundary.

Projectbeschrijving: Een cruciale uitdaging voor hedendaagse supply chain-netwerken wordt vertegenwoordigd door hun veerkracht, bedoeld om het vermogen de bedrijfscontinuïteit te waarborgen in aanwezigheid van ontwrichtende gebeurtenissen. Gezien de hoge onderlinge afhankelijkheden tussen knooppunten binnen een netwerk, strategieën om de impact van verstoringen te verminderen, moeten in overweging worden genomen niet slechts één bedrijf, maar het hele netwerk. Echter, de ontwikkeling van strategieën om het netwerk te verbeteren veerkracht kampt met grote moeilijkheden. Een van hen is een belangrijke factor die vaak in de literatuur naar voren wordt gebracht, namelijk het ontbreken van transparantie in de keten. Inderdaad, meestal zijn verschillende partners in een SC zich alleen bewust van hun eigen functie/producten binnen de keten, terwijl een overzicht van de totale keten, met bijbehorende afhankelijkheden tussen de knooppunten ontbreekt. Dit zorgt vaak voor veel onzekerheid bij de bedrijven als het gaat om het reageren op verstoringen. Dit project wil dit probleem aanpakken door nieuwe methodologieën en tools te ontwikkelen om bedrijven in staat te stellen hun supply chain-netwerken te visualiseren en te onderzoeken hoe gerelateerde processen met elkaar verbonden zijn. Het visualiseren van het netwerk zal leiden tot a) het verbeteren van het netwerk transparantie, en b) het ondersteunen van beslissingen via zowel financiële als operationele acties om te herstellen van opgetreden storingen. Dit netwerk zal kwantitatieve analyse mogelijk maken over hoe verstoringen zich voortplanten door het netwerk, dat op zijn beurt de ontwikkeling mogelijk zal maken van systemen voor vroegtijdige detectie van verstoringen die gericht zijn op tijdig bedrijven op de hoogte stellen wanneer een storing in het netwerk hun processen waarschijnlijk zal beïnvloeden. Deze doelen zijn gekoppeld aan de volgende innovatiethema's van Dinalog: Supply Chain Management; Data gedreven logistiek; ICT & Informatievoorziening; en Douane en Handel.

Het niet integreren van de productie- en transportschema's leidt tot overmatige productie en vervoerskosten. Bovendien leidt het tot extra onnodige CO2-uitstoot van zowel productie als vervoer. Om dit veelvoorkomende praktische probleem aan te pakken, richt dit project zich op de volgende onderzoeksdoelen: 1. De ontwikkeling van modellen en oplossingsmethoden voor geïntegreerde productie en transport planning die efficiënt, schaalbaar en robuust is tegen de alomtegenwoordigheid van onzekerheid in de processen. 2. Het ontwerpen en ontwikkelen van een Proof-of-Concept (PoC) planningstool voor geïntegreerde productie en transportplanning, gevalideerd in de mengvoederindustrie als use case. 3. De oprichting van een nieuwe Community of Practice, bestaande uit vertegenwoordigers van de academische wereld en verschillende industriële toepassingsdomeinen, geconfronteerd met het probleem van de integratie van productie en transport schema's.
