Projecttitel: Towards osteoarthritis fingerprinting – combining imaging biomarkers and multi-organ-on-chip technology for improved in vitro models
Projectbeschrijving: Osteoarthritis (OA) affects circa 300 million people globally, being the main cause of mobility associated disability. This degenerative disease affects all tissues of the synovial joints, yet its trigger is largely unknown. Current in vitro models are too simplistic, failing to reproduce critical inter-tissue interactions. Furthermore, animal models of OA rarely reflect human aetiology, thus lack translational power. Since none of the currently available models truly recapitulate the complexity of the human disease, there is an urgent unmet need for predictive, human, multi-tissue in vitro joint models that mimic key features of the moving joint, including mechanical stress and/or inflammation. To this end, we will develop a micro-engineered biomimetic model (organs-on-chips) that recapitulates key interactions between two joint tissues: cartilage and synovium. A modular multi-organ-on-a-chip set-up will be established, using mechanically actuated microfluidic platforms, a cartilage-on-chip and a synovium-on-chip unit, to emulate multi-axial joint movement, connected via microfluidic channels mirroring blood vessels and intra-articular space. A toolbox of bioluminescent markers will be developed for real-time analysis of inflammatory, remodelling and mechano-transduction read-outs. The success of the herein proposed OA-BioDetectChips modular platform will be assured by the synergy between the academic and industrial partners, with proven experience in interdisciplinary work, at the intersection between (micro-) tissue engineering, biomaterials, microfluidics, non-invasive molecular imaging and cell biology. This new model will accelerate drug target and biomarker identification, their validation and subsequent clinical translation to offer urgently needed solutions for the 1.4 million Dutch patients affected by AO. Ultimately, we expect to develop an innovative, modular and translatable OA measurement model with high predictability for humans, while substantially reducing, or even replacing, animal experimentation.
Partners: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC), Percuros B.V., Stichting Proefdiervrij, chrn on-chip biotechnologies B.V.

Projecttitel: Drug disposition On-a-Chip: a multi-organ-on-chip model tailored to mimic ADME/PK in vitro
Projectbeschrijving: Each year, tens of thousands of compounds are studied by the pharmaceutical industry. Lack of efficacy and safety issues are the most common reason for drug failure during development (>90% in expensive clinical phase studies). Drug disposition is tested by studying drugs’ pharmacokinetics (PK), which is very different between laboratory animals and human beings. Based on US-FDA and NC3R data, it is estimated that 0.2-1.5 million animals yearly are used by the pharmaceutical industry for PK-testing. Currently available and applied in vitro, cell-line based models have limitations in predicting human ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion) properties, diminishing their predictive value. The necessity for improved preclinical models to predict drug disposition and efficacy is therefore widely recognized. Here, we propose an innovative ‘Drug Disposition-On-a-Chip’ (DD-OoC) by physiologically linking the most relevant organs associated with drug disposition. This innovative modular system will have: 1) human cells, 2) in vitro 3D-polarized organs involved in oral exposure, 3) physiologically relevant connected organs, and 4) a tight cellular barrier between the compartments. Functional parameters (including endogenous functions, drug transport and metabolism) of each individual DD-OoC organ will be identified. The model will be standardized further by the implementation of an automated system that allows for automatic cell culturing and imaging, and sampling of the various compartments for compound concentration analysis. Eventually, the models’ performance will be tested and validated with a selection of model compounds and drugs, for which species-specific ADME/PK is known. Our platform will be the first to showcase a multi-Organ-on-a-Chip focusing on PK determined by the concerted action of ADME-relevant organs, supporting rapid integration in the drug discovery phase of the pharmaceutical development pipeline.

Projectbeschrijving: In de Westerse nemen leeftijd- en leefstijl-gerelateerde ziekten, zoals diabetes, hart- en.vaatziekten en nierziekten drastisch toe. Onderzoek is nodig om hier effectieve.therapieën voor te ontwikkelen. Hiervoor is veel onderzoek nodig. Wat dit onderzoek.complex maakt is dat in dergelijke ziekten verschillende organen elkaar negatief kunnen.beïnvloeden. Zo kan diabetes leiden tot chronische nierschade, en is het bekend dat.chronische nierschade een belangrijke risicofactor is voor het ontwikkelen van hartfalen..Om ziektemechanismen en effecten van mogelijke behandelingen in deze systemische.interacties te onderzoeken lijkt gebruik van diermodellen onontkoombaar. Omdat.dierproeven duur zijn, veel tijd kosten, ethische bezwaren met zich meebrengen, en ze.zeker niet altijd de menselijke situatie correct nabootsen, wordt er hard gewerkt aan.alternatieven voor dierproeven..Dankzij nieuwe ontwikkelingen waardoor menselijke organen beter nagebootst kunnen.worden in het lab, zoals 3D-kweekmethoden en de organoïdentechnologie, gecombineerd.met technologieën op het gebied van miniatuur circulatiesystemen is het mogelijk.geworden om interacties tussen verschillende (zieke of gezonde) menselijke organen in.het lab na te bootsen. In de MOC modellen zullen we nier- leveren.pancreasorganoïden, 3D-gekweekte hartcellen uit adulte, geïnduceerde stamcellen,.vetcellen en endotheelcellen, die de relevante weefsels en organen in deze ziekten.representeren, combineren en de gezonde en zieke situaties in het lab nabootsen..Gegevens uit deze experimenten zullen in samenwerking met onderzoekers van Certara,.experts in het ontwikkelen van computermodellen, worden gekoppeld aan beschikbare.biologische en patiëntengegevens om zo de voorspellende waarde van de MOC.experimenten te onderzoeken. Projecttitel: Innovative Oxidative stress and Neuronal damage biomarker Selection to Enhance.diagnostic Test accuracy in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
Projectbeschrijving: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) is a devastating neurological disease leading to.death within on average three years. ALS can occur at any adult age and is highly.variable in its clinical presentation. This complicates the diagnosis of ALS, leading a.diagnostic delay of 12-15 months and a misdiagnosis rate of 10%. Advances in the.diagnostic process are vital to timely initiate multidisciplinary care and improve quality of.life, as effective treatments to slow progression are lacking..Objective.The aim of this project is to evaluate new diagnostic strategies using innovative markers.of oxidative stress and axonal damage in order to provide a diagnosis earlier and reduce.diagnostic delay. The overall target is to contribute in the prevention of adverse events,.improve self-management and deliver better prospects for finding a cure..Study design.This project concerns a multidisciplinary consortium between the UMC Utrecht and.Treeway B.V. to combine clinical and statistical expertise with biomarker proficiency in.order to address the urgent need for better diagnostic tools collaboratively. Using.prospective population-based registries and biobanks, we will determine a unique set of.biomarkers comprising malondialdehyde, 8-hydroxy-2’-deoxyguanosine, IL-6 and.neurofilaments. Biomarker data will be matched with high-dimensional clinical.information, including MRI, cognitive and electrophysiological information. State-of-theart.statistical modelling techniques are used to assess the biomarker’s expedience..Anticipated social and economic impact.Approximately 60,000 people are living with ALS in Europe and each year 20,000 people.die from this progressive, fatal disease. Projecttitel: Comparison of two mandibular advancement devices in mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) patients
Projectbeschrijving: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is characterized by repetitive obstructions of the upper airway that are often related to oxygen desaturations and arousals from sleep. The prevalence of OSA varies from 9% to 38% in the adult population. Excessive daytime sleepiness and fatigue, lack of concentration, and snoring are frequently reported complaints. Furthermore, patients with untreated OSA are at increased risk of impaired quality of life, hypertension, stroke, heart failure, diabetes, and involvement in car accidents. Therefore, ineffective treatment of OSA has severe consequences and is associated with enormous costs, both for the individual and for society..Currently, mandibular advancement devices (MADs) are commonly prescribed for the treatment of OSA patients. The rationale behind the efficacy of MADs is that advancement of the mandible and tongue improves upper airway patency during sleep. There is a large variety of commercially available MADs, all with different design features. However, there is limited evidence on the influence of MAD design on the effects of this therapy in OSA patients..This study focuses on effective treatment of OSA by comparing ResMed Narval CC® (ResMed, Lyon, France) and SomnoDent Flex® (SomnoMed, Sydney, Australia) MADs in OSA patients. The main differences in design between these MADs are: 1. the size, weight, and material, which could influence the preference of patients and their adherence to the therapy; and 2.the couple-mechanism between upper and lower splints, which could result in differences in the appliances’ effects on OSA..Therefore, the aims of the study are to compare these MADs on the outcome measures: 1. preference; 2. adherence; 3. side-effects; 4. clinical performance; 5. costs; and 6. therapy success. Based on these outcomes, the evidence for the efficacy of the ResMed Narval CC®-MAD will grow, and the design of the ResMed Narval CC®-MAD will be improved to make its position in the current market stronger.

Projecttitel: Exploiting senescence for the treatment of cancer
Projectbeschrijving: Cancer remains difficult to treat, especially when disease is advanced. Combinations of different cancer drugs are used to suppress development of resistance, but such therapeutic approaches are often limited by toxicity. We have recently developed a radically different approach to cancer therapy which is not based on combinations of drugs, but rather on the sequential treatment with drugs, thereby avoiding drug combination toxicity. First, cells are induced to stop dividing and also acquire a major new vulnerability that is subsequently targeted by a second drug that selectively kills cells with the acquired vulnerability. To accomplish this, we take advantage of the notion that a cellular senescence response can be triggered in advanced cancers. Such senescent cancer cells have dramatic changes in gene expression and metabolism that might be exploited for their eradication. As part of an ERC advanced grant, we have validated functional genomics technology to identify genes whose suppression results in a senescence response in cancer cells. We have also validated similar CRISPR-based technology to find which genes, when suppressed, selectively kill senescent cancer cells. Using an animal model of liver cancer, we have delivered proof of concept that induction of senescence, followed by treatment with an agent that specifically kills senescent cancer cells, leads to dramatic responses. We have dubbed this novel therapy the “one-two punch” approach: the first therapy to induce senescence in cancer cells, the subsequent therapy to eradicate the senescent cells. Here, we will perform genome scale genetic screens in four major cancer types to identify novel genes whose suppression induces senescence or kill senescent cancer cells. After validation, these targets will serve as starting point for future development of innovative cancer therapies. The social and economic impact of fundamentally new cancer therapies in four major cancer types is significant.

Projecttitel: Intestinal Yeasts associated with Inflammatory Bowel Disease and Irritable Bowel Syndrome
Projectbeschrijving: Recent investigations have pointed towards a prominent role of fungi, more specifically the yeasts Candida albicans and Saccharomyces cerevisiae, in healthy and diseased gut, especially Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) and Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (IBD). Studies suggested that fungal dysbiosis is linked to IBD due to an enrichment of Candida and a decrease of Saccharomyces yeasts, whereas increased C. albicans and S. cerevisiae populations seem to play a role in IBS..We formulated three hypotheses:.- Yeast population sizes of C. albicans and S. cerevisiae in the gut correlate with severity of IBS and IBD..- Genetic and phenotypic differences occur among C. albicans and S. cerevisiae populations in patients with IBD, IBS and healthy individuals that correlate with virulence attributes and immune interactions..- Essential plant oils and antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) impact the growth of gut-derived yeasts and may have potential as modulators of gut inhabiting yeast populations and adhesion to gut epithelial cells, and may improve gut health..These hypotheses will be tested in two work packages: WP1, Isolation, identification, and genotyping by microsatellite analysis of yeasts from patients with CD, UC, IBD-IBS, IBS and healthy volunteers; WP2, Phenotyping of yeast isolates from WP1 including virulence and immune interactions, adhesion to gut epithelial cells, and the effect of food grade plant oils and peptides on this adhesion..YBD/S may potentially result in [probiotic] leads that could improve the quality of life of the many people suffering from the chronic gut disorders IBS and IBD through probiotic or prebiotic interactions.

Projecttitel: Development and validation of the next generation of Organoid medium.
Projectbeschrijving: To date, academic and commercial research groups use a home-made recipe when working with Organoid Technology. Organoids require a very rich and complex culture media, which allows for a lot of variety in recipes. The different components and reagents can be obtained from different suppliers, resulting in differences in stability and activity, causing differences in results and effectiveness between the different research groups, but also between researchers within groups. Therefore, it is important to develop a standardised Organoid medium recipe, available for all research groups. Hubrecht Organoid Technology (HUB) is specialised in Organoid Technology, as the proprietary Organoid Technology was developed by Prof. Dr. Hans Clevers at the Hubrecht Institute. The technology is patented by the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) and the license has been granted exclusively to HUB. HUB wants to develop a standard Organoid medium, that increases the worldwide implementation of the Organoid Technology by producing Organoid medium that supports reproducibility and robustness of the technology. HUB is partnering with Stem Cell Technologies (SCT), a biotech company, for the development of standardised Organoid medium. In this project, HUB and SCT will jointly probe the viability of standardised Organoid medium and to demonstrate it, the consortium will develop Organoid medium for several Organoid models. To this end, HUB will test and further develop the recipes together with SCT, so that they meet HUB’s high standards. When the development is successful, the HUB and SCT provide an improved and a new range of Organoid medium, similar in use compared to the culture media for “regular” cell cultures. The speed at which diseases can be investigated with- and drugs can be tested on - Organoid Technology will accelerate, due to the increased reproducibility and robustness. Moreover, a standardised medium will reduce the costs within research groups (academic and commercial).

Projecttitel: De novo cohort; The Personalized Parkinson Project
Projectbeschrijving: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most prevalent degenerative brain disease. Recent work has clarified that accumulation of misfolded alpha-synuclein plays a critical role in the pathophysiology underlying the relentless progression of PD. This recognition has opened up new possibilities for developing interventions that directly target this process of alpha-synuclein accumulation, and thereby potentially slow down or even arrest disease progression. The recent failures of disease-modifying interventions will be explained by the negative outcomes of clinical trials where the tested compounds were in fact effective, but that the current clinical scales are not sensitive enough to detect genuine effects on the underlying disease process. ..For example in the Parkinson field, the MDS-UPDRS scale remains the gold standard to document the outcomes in clinical trials for Parkinson’s disease (PD). However, there are increasing concerns about the validity and reliability of such clinical rating scales, for a variety of reasons: the scoring system is subjective, and is subject to greater variability; the measures are taken episodically, for example once or twice a year; the assessments are typically done within the hospital, where particularly patients with Parkinson's disease perform paradoxically very well (a phenomenon termed kinesia paradoxa); and many events that take place only sporadically cannot be captured by this episodic in-house assessments, such as falls or gradually progressive declines in physical activity. There is therefore an urgent need for development of objective outcome measures that can be obtained longitudinally and unobtrusively while patients perform in their own natural home environment...Digital biomarkers may be able to overcome the limitations of the MDS-UPDRS, as they continuously collects real-time data, during the patient’s day to day activities. In this study we are interested in developing algorithms to track progression of bradykinetic gait, tremor, and autonomic dysfunction (the latter being derived from e.g. skin conductance and changes in heart rate variability). These considerations have motivated us to start a prospective, longitudinal, single-center cohort study: the Personalized Parkinson Project de novo cohort (PPP de novo). The PPP de novo cohort consists of 144 patients with de novo (i.e., newly diagnosed and previously untreated) Parkinson’s disease. The observation in the earliest course of the disease is highly relevant for the development of disease modifying interventions, which are likely to have the biggest potential in the earliest phases of the disease, when the loss of substantia nigra cells is minimal. In particular, we will deploy the PPP de novo cohort for the development of digital biomarkers that could serve as a surrogate or possibly even a primary outcome in future clinical trials of disease-modifying interventions.

Projecttitel: An hiPSC-based fluorescent reporter imaging platform for drug discovery to combat polycystic kidney disease
Projectbeschrijving: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is a critical chronic disease that limits patients to actively participate in society. The disease is initiated at an early life stage and leads finally to renal failure at the age of ~60, thereafter patients will continuously require renal dialysis and ultimately kidney transplantation. The current challenge is to develop targeted drugs or combinatorial treatments that could prevent the initiation of cyst formation or overall disease progression. ADPKD disease model systems that integrate biomarkers for PKD disease initiation and progression, allowing advanced drug discovery, are currently lacking..Objective: The aim of this project is to establish ADPKD models with integrated biomarkers for disease initiation and progression, that can ultimately be used for imaging-based drug discovery..Design: We will use bioinformatics approaches to uncover relevant disease biomarkers based on signalling networks that trigger disease onset and progression. We will use genetically engineered human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC) carrying a PKD1 mutation that can be differentiated to kidney organoids. Wild-type and PKD1 mutant hiPSC cells will be genetically modified to express fluorescent protein markers of disease triggering and progression. These hiPSC reporters will be differentiated into renal epithelial cells as well as kidney organoids and evaluated for implementation in advanced microscopy settings to derive temporal quantitative information on disease biomarker activation..Social and economic impact: we anticipate that these test systems will be critical for the identification of ADPKD targeted drugs. Improved therapeutic modalities for ADPKD patients will have an important impact on their participation in society for a prolonged period. In addition, successful prophylactic or therapeutic intervention will limit renal dialysis and the need for renal transplantation, thereby likely improving quality of life at significantly reduced health care costs.

Projecttitel: Translation of high-throughput genetics from inbred dogs.to identify mutations involved in complex genetic diseases in humans
Projectbeschrijving: The majority of chronic diseases in man have a hereditary background. Hereditary diseases can be classified as rare or common. In common diseases, multiple genetic defects each with a small effect, predispose for disease. In contrast, a limited number of genetic defects with large biological effects are usually involved in the aetiology of rare diseases. Although studies to clarify the aetiology of hereditary diseases are undertaken at an increasing scale, genetic heterogeneity and a variable disease presentation, often hamper genetic studies in humans..Populations of inbred dogs harbour hereditary diseases with high frequency. Close resemblance of disease presentation in dogs and man, conservation of the mammalian genome and the genetic architecture of inbred dog populations, make an excellent animal model for identification of genetic mutations relevant to man...To accelerate genetic research of human hereditary chronic diseases we aim to pinpoint causal candidate genes by translation of results from canine studies...Genetic and phenotypic data from canine and human genome-wide association studies, will be compared using an automated pipeline in a high-throughput setting. As a proof of concept we will study fibrosarcoma (a rare disease) and ectopic ureters (a common disease) in humans and dogs...The ultimate purpose is to elucidate disease aetiology of human hereditary diseases, using a One Health approach. This will pave the way for follow-up studies to improve diagnostics, prognostics and therapeutics in healthcare. Eventually improving the wellbeing of the patients, genetic counselling and healthcare costs..As a by-catch, dogs will benefit from implementation of new DNA tests in breeding strategies leading to a decrease in disease burden of hereditary diseases

Projecttitel: Systematic assessment of microRNA-132 therapeutic targeting in Alzheimer’s disease
Projectbeschrijving: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) affects millions of people worldwide and cannot currently been prevented, slowed down or cured. AD is viewed as a complex multisystemic and multicellular failure to maintain brain homeostasis in affected individuals and its heterogeneous nature poses great challenges to the development of effective therapeutics. microRNAs (miRNAs) are endogenous noncoding RNA species regulating homeostasis in all biological processes and cell types. The pleiotropy of miRNA biology makes them attractive candidates for the treatment of multifactorial diseases, such as AD, as they can potently target multiple RNAs in distinct molecular networks and pathways that converge onto disease pathogenesis. microRNA-132 (miR-132), a potent neuroimmune regulator, is robustly downregulated in the AD patient brain and its deficiency has been functionally linked to amyloid deposition, TAU hyperphosphorylation and memory decline –the main pathological features of AD- in both human and rodents. Despite accumulating evidence pointing towards the functional relevance of miR-132 in AD, the potential on- and off-target toxicity of miR-132, inherent to the miRNA multi-targeting nature, remains largely unknown. Therefore, the translational potential of miR-132 as a drug target cannot currently be predicted..We propose the systematic, unbiased, genome-wide mechanistic investigation of the complex miR-132 regulatory effects in AD-relevant models and the assessment of miR-132 supplementation as a potential therapeutic strategy in AD. Our explorative multi-arm study will employ a series of orthogonal approaches in human and mouse systems to investigate potential on and off-target toxicity and associated molecular mechanims of miR-132-dependent regulation in AD, and obtain a mechanistic proof-of-concept regarding the functional impact and safety of such a strategy in the treatment of AD. The outcomes of the current study will generate essential knowledge for assessment of the therapeutic potential of miR-132, critically inform drug discovery programs and minimize the risk of failure in drug development and clinical applications.

Projecttitel: Porous Titanium Cages for Spine Fixation
Projectbeschrijving: Back pain is worldwide in the top 5 causes of invalidity. An often used strategy is removal the intervertebral disc and replace this for an interbody fusion device (IFD). The IFD is placed to boost bone formation in order to fuse the vertebrae without intervertebral height loss. Most used IFDs are made of polyetheretherketone (PEEK), however this material has serious drawbacks in terms of safety and efficacy. A broad range of IFDs have been developed during the past seventy years, but no guaranteed solution has been accomplished..We investigate efficacy of newly developed 3D printed porous IFDs made of porous Titanium-6 Aluminum-4 Vanadium (Ti6Al4V). This titanium Alloy is known to be a superior material for bone formation and implant-bone anchorage compared to PEEK. However, solid Titanium implants too stiff relative to the surrounding vertebral bodies hampering bone fixation and subsequently risk of subsidence of the implants..With the development of 3D metal printing in the past decade it is now possible to make porous Titanium implants. These implants are expected to have superior fusion rates to PEEK devices due to the material properties and compatibility. Furthermore, the pores are thought to enhance bone formation as blood vessels can form within the pores and bone remodelling cells are stimulated due to the porous structure of the device leading to firm fixation without subsidence..A comparative animal study was recently performed by ISCA in collaboration with UMC Utrecht to study the effectiveness of two different shapes of porous titanium alloy IFDs and compared to a similar shaped PEEK implant. In the current project we will analyse and evaluate further details on how these implants differ in terms of histological, biomechanical and radiological performance, with the goal to further optimize spinal interbody fusion devices.

Projecttitel: Machine learning To Enhance teMPoral cOding for cochleAr impLants
Projectbeschrijving: The World Health Organisation estimates over 5% of the world’s population have disabling hearing loss. Electrical inner ear prostheses (cochlear implants, CIs) have become the standard of care for those who lose their hearing, enabling them to regain a large part of their communication abilities and to continue participating in and contributing to society. CIs also greatly ease the development of spoken language for deaf children, removing barriers that could otherwise seriously limit their education, employment and ability to fully integrate into society. Several CI limitations are largely attributable to their very limited delivery of temporal fine structure (TFS) information..TEMPORAL combines computational modelling, state-of-the-art Machine Learning techniques and patient testing, to develop a new speech coding strategy which allows for better neural encoding of TFS. This will lead to improved perception of music and tonal languages, improve speech understanding in (fluctuating) noise and enhance directional hearing, with either two CIs or a CI and a contralateral hearing aid (bimodal hearing)..Task1 will extend the Leiden computational model of the electrically implanted cochlea with an artificial speech processor and add natural and bilateral hearing to it. This will generate auditory nerve spike train datasets for several conditions. Using these datasets, Task2 will tune the configurable parameters of the CIs to better approximate the spike trains that normally transmit the information to the brain. It will use nonlinear multi-objective optimization through evolutionary algorithms and develop suitable loss functions for spike trains and noise handling. Appropriate machine learning and cross-validation techniques will assure generalizability of the results. Task3 will focus on subjective testing in CI-users and normal hearing subjects to validate the outcomes of the other two tasks. Initially, this will produce normative data for the model and Machine Learning system, thereafter the novel speech coding algorithms will be validated in patients.

Projecttitel: Speeding up MRI with AI: fast MRI applications in prostate cancer
Projectbeschrijving: MRI systems are widely used for the diagnosis of various diseases or for more novel applications like guiding minimal invasive therapeutic interventions. In the era of personalized medicine, medical imaging is the driving force behind these so -called patient- tailored management approaches. Advantages of MRI are being able to detect the disease while at the same time guiding therapies, which enables maximum disease treatment coverage while keeping unwanted side effects to a minimum..With current MRI systems, diagnostic multiparametric-MRI (mpMRI) examination of the prostate can be performed in approximately 40 minutes or in case of an MRI guided therapeutic intervention in 1-2 hours. In order for healthcare systems to be able to handle the vastly increasing number of patients who require a diagnostic or interventional procedure, new technology is required to reduce scan time without compromising image quality..In this project we will be investigating speeding up MRI in prostate cancer (PCa) diagnosis and interventions. PCa will serve as a proof of concept disease, with future expansion possibilities to other (clinical) MRI applications. National and European guidelines have recently changed and recommend mpMRI as first-line diagnostic work up in all patients suspected of PCa. MRI is also expected to be more intensively used for surveillance in the setting of a watchful waiting strategy, in order to avoid overtreatment of PCa. Consequently, the number of MRI scans and associated cumulative costs will substantially increase..In this project, called “FastMRI-AI”, we will develop new artificial intelligence (AI) techniques that will make MRI for the diagnosis and interventions in PCa targeted, and therefore faster and more accurate. Innovative harmoniously operating AI techniques will be developed for this purpose: detection, reconstruction, and steering AI (which will target disease and interventional instruments on raw, low resolution,

Projecttitel: A personalized medicine approach for Alzheimer’s disease
Projectbeschrijving: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is among this century’s major healthcare challenges. It gradually robs individuals of their cognitive.capabilities, with dementia as its final stage. In the Netherlands almost 300,000 individuals suffer from dementia, mostly the AD.type. This number rises to more than half a million by 2040. There is no curative treatment for AD yet. Care targets the.dementia stage, often with compromised quality of life. ABOARD envisions a future with individualized prevention ecompassing.tailored combinations of lifestyle and disease modifying interventions. This implies that the key to stop AD lies in the.pre-dementia stages, realizing that one size does not fit all. Most importantly, the patient needs to be at the steering wheel. To.achieve this, we need all ABOARD! The mission of ABOARD is to jumpstart Personalized Medicine for AD by preparing for and investing in effective and patient-orchestrated diagnosis, prediction, and prevention of dementia. The mission is realized by a.strong multi-sectoral and multidisciplinary consortium, with 32 partners spanning the entire translational value chain. The.project is executed in five interconnected work packages: ABOARD (i) improves timely and molecular diagnosis, including.clinical evaluation of blood-based biomarkers and polygenic risk scores, (ii) develops individualized risk predictions that use.patient reported outcomes and translates this to the national level, (iii) pilots primary prevention strategies and prepares for.secondary prevention strategies, (iv) engages elderly (at risk of) AD throughout all aspects of health and disease management,.and (v) develops and implements recommendations and (e)-health tools to support patients/care partners and professionals. At.the close of the project, ABOARD has paved the way for a personalized medicine approach for AD. Patients and care partners.are empowered and more actively engaged in the management of their health and disease, and strategies for diagnosis,.prediction and prevention of AD have improved.

Projecttitel: Restoring 24-hour substrate rhythmicity to improve glycemic.control by timing of lifestyle factors
Projectbeschrijving: Recently, our 24-hour culture has been identified as another lifestyle factor that can cause type 2 diabetes (T2D). Technological.and societal advances, such as artificial lighting and digital screens – leading to light exposure that is too dim during the day.and too bright during the evening –, shift work, time zone transfers, variable sleep timing and round-the-clock food availability.disrupt our intrinsic and evolutionarily preserved 24-hour rhythms resulting in a desynchronization between light cues and.behavior cues to our circadian system. This mistiming of cues, also referred to as circadian misalignment is now thought to be a.major contributor to the current metabolic health crisis with increasing rates of obesity and T2D..To be prepared for alternating periods of day and night, feeding and fasting, and activity and recovery, the body contains a.biological clock that sets the circadian rhythm. This somatic circadian system is composed of a central master clock in the.hypothalamus and a series of subordinate clocks in virtually all other tissues. Whereas the central clock is primarily entrained.by bright light exposure, the rhythms in peripheral tissues and immune cells are primarily synchronized by behavioural.Zeitgebers such as food intake, temperature, sleep and physical activity. Consequently, the two clock systems can.desynchronize when cues derived from these behavioral Zeitgebers are not aligned to the environmental light/dark cycle..Our consortium found complete lack of rhythmicity of energy substrate oxidation, muscle mitochondrial function, plasma free.fatty acid levels, and of muscle and adipose tissue expression of major peripheral molecular clock genes in humans.predisposed to diabetes and/or patients with diabetes. On the basis of these preliminary data we hypothesize that appropriate.timing of behavioural interventions to enhance daily rhythmicity of the circadian timing system holds great promise to improve.metabolic health and glucose homeostasis and may be a novel strategy in the prevention and treatment of T2D..OBJECTIVES: The proposed Dutch-Canadian research consortium objectives are to: 1) elucidate the mechanisms of the effect.of timed life style interventions on metabolic health and body weight regulation in subjects at high risk of T2D; 2) determine the.relevance of differentially timed lifestyle factors throughout the 24h cycle for the development and progression of T2D; and 3).from all these data develop more effective lifestyle interventions to prevent and reverse T2D..PROPOSED RESEARCH APPROACHES: To reach these objectives, we propose 3 complementary and integrated work.packages (WP) that build on the expertise and track record of our international team in integrative physiology, epidemiology.and clinical trials. We will also leverage the expertise of our team in engagement of patient partners, training & mentoring of.next generation of scientists, and in development of large successful collaborative scientific networks. WP 1 proposes proof of.concept mechanistic studies in animals and humans with tracer, molecular imaging, and deep metabolic phenotyping to assess.the effects of timed lifestyle interventions on muscle, adipose tissue, brain and immune functions in pre-diabetes. WP 2 will.determine the impact of timing of lifestyle factors on the development and progression of T2D in longitudinal Dutch and.Canadian population-based and T2D patient cohorts (eg. The NEO study, the Hoorn studies, the Canadian Longitudinal Study.on Aging, Synergie Study and consolidated observation and interventional cardiometabolic imaging cohorts at Laval University,.and the multi-omics DIRECT studies). WP 3 will design pragmatic trial interventions based on results from WP 1 and 2 and on.the experiential expertise of patient partners, to test whether timed lifestyle interventions improve glycemic control in T2D in.regular care. International training programs in diabetes research and patient engagement will be established for trainees,.scientists and patient partners in collaboration with Diabetes Action Canada, the CIHR SPOR Network on diabetes, the.Cardiometabolic health, Diabetes and Obesity Network of the FRQS, and with the Dutch Diabetes Foundation..IMPACT: The proposed consortium will regroup some of the world best experts in integrative physiology, epidemiology, lifestyle.interventions, patient engagement, and scientific networking to optimize lifestyle interventions based on circadian misalignment.to prevent T2D, train the future generation of health researchers in the field, and develop patient partners’ engagement at the.international level.

Projectbeschrijving: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs, plastic particles < 5 mm) are increasingly found in our environment and our food, however we.know very little about how they are formed and their potential human health risks. This lack of knowledge forms an important.barrier to developing and implementing solutions to minimize the potential adverse health impacts of MNPs. Research on.MNPs is therefore of high priority in the Dutch Knowledge and Innovation Agenda 2020-2023. In the past year, the Netherlands.Organisation for Health Research and Development (ZonMw) funded several ‘breakthrough’ projects of one year duration to.research the most urgent knowledge gaps in the field of MNPs and human health. In addition, ZonMW will soon release the.national Knowledge Agenda on Microplastics and Health, which outlines the major research gaps in this field. The overarching goal of this project is to build on the momentum gained in the ZonMW breakthrough projects and work towards.a long-term public-private-partnership (PPP) that will ultimately form the Dutch National Research Infrastructure on MNPs and.Health, using the ZonMW Knowledge Agenda on Microplastics and Health as a basis. Our project, aptly entitled.“MOMENTUM,” integrates and accelerates the most promising research developments from fourteen ZonMw breakthrough.projects. In co-creation with private sector organisations and in consultation with key stakeholders from academia, government,.industry and citizen organisations, the research conducted in MOMENTUM aims to unravel the human health effects of MNPs.and to propose solutions to minimize their potential health impact. MOMENTUM expands on the ground-breaking research of.the breakthrough projects by further investigation of the potential human health risks following MNP exposure. In particular,.approaches will be developed to measure internal human exposure and further elucidate the kinetics of MNPs crossing internal.barriers of the lung, intestine, brain and placenta. We will also continue our novel research on unravelling the immunological.hazards of exposure to plastic particles and MNP-associated pathogens. We will go beyond the current ZonMw breakthrough.projects by increasing knowledge on the formation and characterisation of MNPs, and by developing a roadmap to.comprehensive risk assessment of MNPs. The innovations in MOMENTUM will form the basis for solution sets to minimize.potential health risks, and a long-term R&D strategy lasting beyond the three year duration of the project..MOMENTUM seeks to inspire the academic and medical world, government, and industry to develop new understanding of the.MNP pollution problem. MOMENTUM brings together researchers from eight Dutch universities and medical centres, four.research organisations and fourteen international partners from small, medium and large private enterprises. The MOMENTUM.consortium has expertise in a wide range of disciplines, including polymer and analytical chemistry, exposome sciences,.materials sciences, toxicology, immunology, medical sciences, virology, microbiology, bioengineering, environmental sciences,.and risk assessment, ensuring an original, interdisciplinary mix of researchers who will work together for the first time to tackle.this challenge. This will create synergism that will fuel both the fundamental research and the evidence that can be translated.towards the benefit of society.
Partners: Aimplas, American Chemistry Council, Antea Nederland B.V., Avantium Support B.V., BASF Nederland B.V., Borm Nanoconsult B.V., Bruker Nederland B.V., CytoSMART Technologies B.V., Da Vinci Laboratory Solutions B.V., KWR Water B.V., Lyondell Chemie (POSM) B.V., Malvern Panalytical B.V., Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk onderzoek TNO, Open Universiteit, Plastics Europe, Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu (RIVM), Rijksuniversiteit Groningen, SiMPLInext SA, Stichting Deltares, Stichting VU, Universitair Medisch Centrum Utrecht, Universiteit Maastricht, Universiteit Twente, VITROCELL Systems GmbH, WESSLING GmbH, Wageningen Universiteit/ Wageningen University

Projecttitel: A garment-integrated artificial intelligence-based sensor system for early detection of stress in people with impaired cognition
Projectbeschrijving: Care costs for people with dementia and people with intellectual disabilities are rapidly increasing. With the.anticipated growth of long-term care clients and decline in labor force, it will be difficult to maintain the quality.level of care and support. Cognitively impaired clients are vulnerable to stress. Their caregivers face the daily.challenge to identify and regulate their client’s stress and emotional state, based on non-verbal cues. A delay in.recognition of stress can result in challenging behavior, such as aggression or agitation. Challenging behavior.has negative consequences for quality of life, makes client care and support difficult, and the burden on.caregivers results in higher than average work-place absenteeism and staff turnover. Developing aids that.increase the quality of care, while also reducing the burden on caregivers, is critical..We are developing a mood-sensing system that provides caregivers with early signs of client stress, allowing.caregivers to mitigate the causes of stress before the client becomes agitated or violent. The mood-sensing.system combines a suite of sensors in a garment, with a cloud-based communications system, and a smart.algorithm, to detect early signs of stress in the client. Caregivers can use the device to prevent the build-up of.stress, but to also provide a more pleasant and enjoyable environment for the client. This will enhance the client’s.quality of life, reduce the burden on caregivers, and reduce costs.
Partners: Mentech Innovation B.V., Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk onderzoek TNO, Prinsenstichting, Stichting 's Heeren Loo Zorggroep, Stichting Fontys, Stichting Katholieke Universiteit Brabant, Stichting Saxion, Stichting Severinus, Technische Universiteit Eindhoven

Projectbeschrijving: This project is to show and transfer a virtual connected home-based facilitated self-managed toolkit (CTK) in MPV status to.enhance functional status and wellbeing and to change lifestyle behaviour before major elective surgery (Fit4surgery)..Monitoring will be based on data collected by a comfortable, intuitive and seamless device that measures vitals including sleep.and stress. The CTK toolkit is an MPV with AI-based continuous remote cardiac monitoring solution includes a wearable,.non-invasive medical device, AI-based analytic platform, system of smart notification and dashboard for healthcare.professionals with access to real-time information. NAAST (1st line) and RUMC (2nd line) provide layered monitoring and.support during the pre-habilitation period (2-4 weeks)..Fit4surgery is a relatively new trend in health care, with little or only general insights in the economic advantages. This applies.even more for the next level; on-line Fit4surgery coaching and monitoring. In this project we will provide insights on the health.care economics of the project in comparison to the current in-house Fit4surgery program of RUMC. On a national level,.Fit4surgery is not yet implemented in all hospitals. A cost-saving solution like CTK for pre-habilitation, is expected to support a.wide, enhanced and sustainable implementation of the program, corresponding with the quadruple aims in healthcare and.nationwide prevention programs.

Projecttitel: WavyTunes: Reduction of the demand of care for (female).patients with ischemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries.(INOCA) by introducing a stress-reducing program
Projectbeschrijving: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) is the leading cause of death globally, taking an estimated 17.9 million lives (31% of all deaths).each year. For Europe, IHD causes 877,000 deaths (20%) among women and 862,000 (19%) among men. In women, ischemia.with non-obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA) dominates over obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). INOCA with.coronary vascular dysfunction is the main cause of IHD in women, especially in the age group 40-70 years, twice as often as in.men. Psychosocial distress is a major contributor to INOCA, for which adequate support is currently lacking. Cardiac.rehabilitation programs are mainly focused on physical exercise in obstructive CAD and not on stress reduction in INOCA. This.project aims to examine the efficacy of a stress-reducing program with the WavyTunes smartphone-app, using biofeedback to.adapt for individual needs with Radboudumc, 4 collaborating hospitals, Fontys University, Wavy Assistant and Harteraad. 250.female patients with established INOCA will participate. Patients will serve as their own controls in a cross-over study design, 4 weeks placebo and 4 weeks treatment. The goal is to provide a significant treatment option for this large, but neglected patient.group, lowering healthcare costs from €2.500 to €1.300 per patient (48%).
Partners: Academisch Ziekenhuis Maastricht, Stichting Catharina Ziekenhuis, Stichting Elisabeth-TweeSteden Ziekenhuis, Stichting Fontys, Stichting Harteraad, Stichting Viecuri, Medisch Centrum voor Noord-Limburg., Wavy Assistant B.V.

Projecttitel: MOVITA: Wearable technology to optimize prognostic evaluation and rehabilitation of gait behaviour in orthopaedic patients.
Projectbeschrijving: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) imposes a substantial burden on individuals and the health care system. Total.knee arthroplasty (TKA) is indicated to treat end-stage OA, but tailoring postoperative treatment is.hampered by a lack of objective assessment tools to monitor recovery. This results in ineffective.identification and care of poor-recovering patients, and excessive care of well-recovering patients..Objective assessment and visualization of daily-life physical behaviour and gait quality using.new wearable technology will facilitate effectiveness in prognostics and treatment of TKA.patients, minimizing required care and optimizing patient satisfaction..MOVITA (Move, Visualize, Tailor) will be a product to remotely assess, store, and visualize an OA.patient’s daily-life physical behaviour to monitor progression without costly hospital visits. Scientifically.validated algorithms based on wearable technology will be professionalized (module 1) and integrated.in a cloud-based platform with an attractive user-interface (module 2) co-created with end-users. Field.tests will reveal potential pitfalls and unforeseen requirements, further supporting the iterative.developmental process. The resultant minimal viable product allows orthopaedic surgeons and.physiotherapists to remotely assess and visualize clinical endpoints, enabling tailormade.postoperative treatment. Business case development in collaboration with stakeholders will ensure.uptake of MOVITA as an effective, affordable and beneficial medical device.
Partners: McRoberts B.V., Moveshelf Labs B.V., Noordwest Ziekenhuisgroep, Stichting Sint Maartenskliniek

Projecttitel: Precision Orthotics in Stroke, MS and CP
Projectbeschrijving: Plantarflexor spasticity in combination with dorsiflexor paresis cause equinus or equinovarus foot.affecting safe mobility. Conventional ankle-foot orthoses (AFOs) are stiff, and support mobility by.attaining foot clearance during swing, but at the cost of ankle motion, push off during gait, and.activities requiring a mobile ankle, like dressing and car-driving..The NWO-TTW NeuroCIMT-project ‘Stiffness as Needed’ developed a novel negative stiffness.AFO, called Hermes, to compensate for the spastic ankle joint stiffness, enabling the available.dorsiflexor muscles to regain control..As a sequel, “Show and Transfer I" will bring the design from a generic, though tuneable, research.prototype TRL4 to a personalized demonstrator prototype for home use TRL6. At the expense of.complexity and weight, the TRL4-prototype allows tuning to a range of patient’s needs. For home.use, the hinge should be redesigned for safety and durability (covering rotating parts) and should.accommodate individual patients’ needs using personalized torque-angle characteristics..With cross-sectional patient studies in lab setting currently underway, a “Validate and Transfer II”.enables longitudinal studies with home use..Improved ankle mobility reduces complications of spastic paresis (e.g., contractures, high energy.expenditure), allows renewed muscular control, and secondarily lowers the limitations in activities,.enhancing quality of life.
Partners: Basalt Den Haag, InteSpring B.V., Leids Universitair Medisch Centrum (Lumc), OIM Noordwijkerhout B.V.

Projectbeschrijving: De komende decennia zullen overgewicht en fysieke inactiviteit leiden tot een toename van stofwisselingsziektes zoals diabetes mellitus, en zal de druk op de gezondheidszorg meestijgen. Zelfmanagement bij diabetes kan complicaties en ziekenhuisopnames voorkomen. Ook een actieve leefstijl kan fysieke conditie en fysiologie processen verbeteren en het ontstaan van metabole complicaties bij diabetes en obesitas voorkomen. Er is derhalve vraag naar sensoren die het metabolisme kunnen monitoren en een actieve levensstijl kunnen ondersteunen.Binnen dit project wordt een nanosensor doorontwikkeld, die continue acetonuitscheiding via de huid meten. Als restproduct van vetverbranding kan aceton gebruikt worden om het vetmetabolisme te monitoren. Het monitoren van vetmetabolisme is van groot belang bij patiënten met obesitas en/ofdiabetes om te voorkomen dat ze respectievelijk metabole stoornissen of ketoacidose ontwikkelen.Door deze sensor worden professionals ondersteund met een accurate maat voor vetmetabolisme.Tegelijkertijd worden mensen met obesitas gemotiveerd om een actieve levensstijl te onderhouden.De sensor zit momenteel in fase TRL4 en kan verschillende concentraties aceton in vitro meten. De technologie wordt doorontwikkeld tot een minimal-viable-product (MVP). De doelen van dit project zijn 1; de sensor tot MVP te ontwikkelen (TRL4-TRL6); 2; relaties tussen fysieke activiteit en acetonuitscheiding onderzoeken; 3; de toepassing bij de gebruikersgroep evalueren.
Partners: Academisch Ziekenhuis Groningen, GEEN RECHTSPERSOON, All round Technology (ART), GEEN RECHTSPERSOON, LioniX International, Medisch Spectrum Twente, Stichting Quality Assurance E-health

Projecttitel: ADJUST: A stiffness adjustable ankle-foot-orthosis for efficient.human-in-the-loop orthosis selection
Projectbeschrijving: Ankle-foot-orthoses (AFOs) enable people with muscle weakness due to neuromuscular diseases to prevent falls by providing.stability (walk more safely) and to increase their walking radius by lowering walking energy cost (walk more efficiently). We.have demonstrated that the effectiveness of AFOs to augment walking can be greatly improved, when the stiffness is.individually optimized. The experimental modular TRL4 prototype AFO we developed and validated, requires the exchange of.various stiffnesses to determine the optimal (i.e. most efficient) stiffness. This is a lengthy and labor-intensive procedure with.high patient-burden. In this project, we propose to design a novel wearable AFO of which the stiffness can be altered in.real-time. This allows for a rapid optimization procedure in one session, as the outcome, energy cost, can be continuously.measured while changing the stiffness (human-in-the-loop-optimization). Currently, this is only possible with comprehensive.high-cost equipment. As a Minimal Viable Product, we aim for a dedicated low-cost wearable model, enabling stiffness.optimization in a large range of clinical practices. We expect that use of our stiffness adjustable AFO will dramatically shorten.the optimization procedure (1.5 hours instead of 8, and in 1 hospital visit instead of two), thereby saving personnel time and.healthcare costs and it will considerably lower patient-burden. Furthermore, precisely selecting the individual optimal stiffness.will lead to a more effective treatment in terms of reducing gait problems and improving physical functioning during daily life.
Partners: OIM Noordwijkerhout B.V., Stichting Reade, Technische Universiteit Delft

Projecttitel: Decreased deployment of medical resources by applying the.one-stop breath analyser in vulnerable patients with chronic.diseases.one-stop breath analyser in vulnerable patients with chronic.diseases
Projectbeschrijving: Early diagnosis of chronic diseases is crucial to improve treatment and prognosis, e.g. chronic lung disease, cancer, chronic.kidney or liver disease in children and elderly. Non-invasive analysis of exhaled breath has shown potential for improved.diagnosis and management of chronic diseases. In this project, we focus on a one-stop diagnostic solution, especially for.vulnerable patients with chronic diseases by solving critical existing problems of commercial breath tests. As a start, the clinical.application is children (1-4 years) suspected of asthma. Our TRL4 lab prototype exists of carbon nanotube sensors performing.in a highly controlled environmental box and being processed by dedicated algorithms. In the demonstration phase, a TRL6.prototype is developed with a focus on achieving the required sensitivity by dedicated functionalization of the carbon nanotube.sensors and intelligent data processing to determine the complex breath profiles. Moreover, we focus on ease of breathing and.feasibility during the test by mimicking canine nasal airflow. In the validate phase, the TRL6 is evaluated by our clinical.consortium partners according to the Medical Device Directive. As the market for one-stop breath analyzers will grow a staggering 30% in the coming decade, a competitive position is expected. In the transfer phase, we target IP protection and a.solid market entrance strategy
