Projecttitel: Act4AgrMotion - Reliable actuators for aggressive motion conditions
Projectbeschrijving: Linear electromagnetic actuators constitute one of the core components of high-tech motion systems. These actuators are fed by power cables which are moving with the stage. Increasing demands on motion profiles increases the excitation forces on the power cables and the supplied power which requires to increase the diameters of the cables. This is not sustainable. Increasing the supply voltage (up to 2 kV and higher) allows to break this trend, but this requires improved electrical insulation of the actuators. Therefore, the research objective of this project is to derive and investigate methods that breach the relation between high-voltage and force density in linear actuators.....The actuator design is such that is capable to withstand the applied voltage by the choice of insulation materials and by the thickness of these materials. However, increasing this thickness reduces the volume available for the conductors, limiting the force density of the actuator. Next to that, the insulators are also directly in the thermal cooling path from the actuator coils to a water-cooled body, which means that increasing the thickness reduces the cooling performance of the actuator. An additional research objective of this project that requires attention in this context are partial discharges and the failure mechanisms related to it, which become increasingly critical as operating voltages increase.

Projecttitel: AMBER - AdvanceMents in BEhavioral autonomy for medical Robotics
Projectbeschrijving: The new generation of image guided therapy robots will see more autonomy in mutual positioning between different parts of the system which poses challenges with respect to position accuracy but creates opportunities for smoother and higher-level interaction between the user (i.e., the physician) and the system..Traditionally, physicians interact with image guided therapy robots controlling them by means of a joystick which provides low level inputs in terms of velocity and direction of movements. This type of robot control for strictly non-surgery related movements (i.e., homing) is time consuming and not intuitive for the end-users. Advancing the behavioural autonomy of such systems for non-surgery related movements would reduce the workload on medical personnel in a time with heavy workforce shortages. It would also enhance the clinical workflow reducing treatment time and decreasing expenses.  .AMBER will advance the state-of-the-art of behavioral autonomy of medical robots by endowing them with advanced autonomous reasoning abilities safeguarding safety throughout the process.

Projecttitel: COMARIC - Continuous Management of Architecture-Implementation Conformance
Projectbeschrijving: Softwareontwikkelprojecten lopen tegen een grens aan van moeilijk te beheersen complexiteit.  Om overzicht te maken, en te houden, worden architectuur-representaties van het systeem gemaakt. Echter, het is moeilijk om de architectuur van het systeem en de implementatie 'in de pas' te laten lopen. Hierdoor verliest de architectuur zijn waarde als hulpmiddel voor 1) het beheersen van de complexiteit, 2) het analyseren van het systeem, en 3) het plannen van de bouw en uitbreiding van het systeem..Dit project beoogt een methode en software tool te ontwikkelen waarmee de architectuur en de implementatie wel 'in de pas blijven lopen'. Hiervoor zal het project standaarden en guidelines ontwikkelen voor her modelleren van zowel de architectuur en de implementatie van software systemen. Op basis van deze modellen, wordt een dashboard gemaakt die rapporteert waar architectuur en implementatie uit de pas lopen, zodat developers & architecten hierop actie kunnen nemen om dit te repareren.

Projecttitel: DACCLET - Dynamics of air entrapment in cooling circuits for lithographic exposure tools
Projectbeschrijving: In lithographic machines, hundreds of liters of water are pumped to various components every minute to cool them. The down side of this high cooling flow is that vibrations and waves are generated at pumps, bends and manifolds which deteriorate the dynamic performance and accuracy of the machine. .To make things worse, during service actions (scheduled or unscheduled) the water-cooling system often has to be stopped and the cooling infrastructure (tubing, pumps, ducts) has to be drained and refilled, which introduces air entrapment in the cooling circuits. The presence of air significantly changes the dynamics of the cooling circuit, which makes it rather unpredictable and varying over time, and potentially causing more vibrational waves. .This study aims to come up with reliable physical and conceptual physics-based and data-based machine learning tools to predict air entrapment risk and expected time to reach air free operation. On the basis of these modeling tools, mitigation strategies will be developed to limit both the air entrapment risk and the propagation of vibrational waves.

Projecttitel: DAISPP - Design, Data and AI in Servitizing Professional Printing
Projectbeschrijving: Canon Production Printing (CPP), formally Océ, is a leading multinational manufacturer of professional printing products and services, which are used by a variety of customers in different domains. In addition to supporting diverse businesses, CPP solutions are also used in varied ways and workflows, at different scales and process integrations. Even between two similar types of customers there might be considerable differences in how they organize their work, both in terms of company and operator level. The core challenges in this context are (1) to better understand customers and customer workflows through collecting and analysing interaction flows and contextual data, and (2) to help customers get more value from the CPP solutions by means of better workflow integration, AI-supported personalization and advanced analytics. To address these challenges, the CPP design and R&D teams focus on two clusters of research questions: (1) targets insights on how users compose their UI ecosystem based on the applications provided within the Pigment Design System, and (2) how different users utilize printers and software in their workflows. We will pursue a multi-stage approach to answer the research questions: from contextual and functional collection and analysis of rich data to optimized UI ecosystems and workflows. Methodologically, we will rely foremost on data-supported ethnography, data-enabled design, and research-through-design, and leverage CPP's data platform and analytics expertise. From within EAISI, we will work with advanced AI to steer real-time data collection, product and UI adaptation and the modelling of workflows. This collaboration between design and R&D team at CPP and researchers from Industrial Design (TU/e) aim for concrete outcomes that integrate with CPP product development, enable new design research capabilities and lead to insights into data-enabled product development methodologies and tools.

Projecttitel: HiVECAF - Highly Versatile Efficient & Compact Active Filters
Projectbeschrijving: Active filters are devices that are based on power electronics and are used in a variety of installations to eliminate unwanted and disturbing harmonics, preventing them from polluting the grid. As the grid is evolving towards a more decentralized structure that involves the increased use of distributed generation and the deployment of the associated power converters that are necessary to accommodate it and control it, the problem of polluting harmonics is expected to intensify. Therefore, the use of active filters will become more widespread and critical to the proper operation of the grid. ..Active filters today are based on traditional IGBT-based Power Electronics technology, utilizing well-established circuit topologies and control techniques. The developments based on these traditional choices have reached their limit in terms of efficiency, compactness and capabilities in terms of the elimination of harmonics. On the other hand, the use of Wide Band-Gap (WBG) semiconductors offers an increased switching frequency that not only allows for more compact designs, but also offers higher control bandwidths. The results of the combination of this feature with advanced control techniques have not been fully explored - let alone exploited..The HiVECAF project will focus on the deployment of WBG technologies, namely SiC and GaN, and advanced control techniques (such as Model Predicitve Control) in the field of active filtering.

High-tech motion and mechatronic systems are becoming increasingly complex to meet ever increasing market demands on quality and versatility of system performance. In particular, model uncertainty and system variations arise from more and different sources. For instance, due to cost aspects, which play an increasingly prominent role in system design for some companies, companies are investigating the use of low-cost system components, for sensing, actuation, bearings, computational platforms, etc. Such cost-driven design decisions typically lead to non-ideal (and hard-to-model and uncertain) component behaviour, such as nonlinear sensor characteristics, computational delays, and complex behaviour of mechanical system components that add to the overall large complexity of high-tech systems..These growing complexity, uncertainty and cost aspects put under pressure the performance and reliability of purely physics-based modelling strategies and purely model-based control design strategies for high-performance motion and mechatronic systems. Therefore, we propose in this project a novel design approach that complements model-based design with state-of-the-art data-based learning techniques. Particularly challenging will be the question on how to exploit the immense potential of large amounts of data on real-life performance of high-tech systems in the field made available by recent developments on sensing and communication technologies.
Partners: ASM, Canon Nederland N.V., Thermo Fisher Scientific

Projecttitel: MATTER - Maintenance Assistant for Time-bound Troubleshooting and Event Resolution
Projectbeschrijving: High-tech systems require ever increasing levels of competence from field engineers and technical support staff. Effectively sharing knowledge between engineers and providing first-time-right (FTR) advice from the pool of available knowledge requires insights from system design, past experience and diverse data sources such as sensors, logs, alarms and warnings. To remain at the front of challenges, thinking assistants that can combine this knowledge securely and work in successful partnership with field engineers and technical support staff are required..The objective of the Marel Thinking Assistant project is to develop a holistic approach to supporting field engineer and technical support staff decision making when diagnosing and intervening in complex systems. This means accurately diagnosing critical events that are happening now or in the near future, assessing the root causes of these and identifying possible interventions (and their risks) to ameliorate the issues that have been identified. Human experience and skills are important to achieving successful outcomes and will be assisted by AI-based knowledge systems. This is in line with the HTSM roadmap Smart Industry..To remain competitive and to maintain the high-levels of uptime and performance of complex system, a "first time right (FTR)" approach is necessary for field engineers and technical support staff. Expert thinking assistants that grow with the engineer and their knowledge and share important lessons across the company based on complex multi-dimensional sources will make service engineer jobs less stressful, more rewarding and will help high complexity system suppliers to provide their customers with better operational outcomes.

Projecttitel: MoPlaMo - Modular Planar Motor for semicon applications
Projectbeschrijving: The Modular Planar Motor project research magnetically planar motors for accurate positioning in semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The goal is to make a significant step in accuracy in planar motors with moving magnets and stationary coils. The research in magnetic design will explore inverse optimization techniques to synthesize planar motor structures instead of applying classical forward models to improve the motor performance and the modeling of all interactions between coils and magnets in the motor. Further optimal integration of the motor and the wafer chuck is studies to deal with the large internal stresses and the highly position dependent forces that occur inside these motors. Metrology concepts are researched with improved angle tolerance. Included in this study is the metrology system to fulfill the requirements on measurement uncertainty for large range movements in multiple degrees of freedom.

The RAIDAR project aims to develop AI technologies that can strongly advance the perceptive capabilities, noise immunity and security of radar systems. To these ends RAIDAR involves a close collaboration between key AI and security experts of TU/e with key industrial IC design, engineering and application experts. This collaboration will enable the project to develop synergistic combinations of data driven and model-based approaches, thus supporting a shift of the performance-robustness-security boundary.

Projecttitel: Semi-XOM - Smart Exposure, Metrology and Inspection through neXtgen Opto-Mechatronics
Projectbeschrijving: Nowadays, many high tech products, machines and scientific instruments are based on Optics, which is enabled by high-end Mechatronics. Striking examples are mobile phones, production and inspection equipment for ICs, and (space) telescopes and laser interferometer gravitational-wave observatories (LIGOs) respectively. The critical steps for both optical lithography and inspection, which are driving advanced applications such as AI (artificial intelligence), HPC (high performance computing), and autonomous driving, are dependent on accurately positioning of high-end optics, including the object (mask) and the image plane (wafer). .The goal of the SEMI-XOM project is to provide breakthrough technology steps, tailored to the long term needs and in line with the Electronics and Semiconductor Equipment Roadmaps for lithography and inspection. Four PhD projects on experimental design are defined, in which proof of concept of groundbreaking hardware will being realized and experimentally verified. In view of the broad Opto-Mechatronics scope of the program, multiple supporting MSc assignments are envisioned for the coming years..Through a very strong focus on integral System-based Design, which was built up at the Control Systems Technology group at the Eindhoven University of Technology over the last two decades, the ecosystem of high tech industries in the Netherlands, is considered to substantiate a unique proposition through joint academic research in the area of Opto-Mechatronics, which allows for further gain in competitive advantage in human capital and technology in the Netherlands. Results from academic research will contribute to improved and up-to-date training of engineers at BSc and MSc level, compatible to modern industry standards.

The SimplifAI project contributes to the existing ICAI lab, the KPN-JADS Responsible AI lab, and aims at developing methods that simplify deep learning algorithms in order to facilitate transparency and robustness. Overparameterization is at the core of the success of deep learning algorithms. Both Convolutional Neural Networks and Transformer architectures have been shown to benefit from an abundance of free parameters. Although over-parameterization is beneficial to the training and subsequent generalisation performance of deep learning algorithms, it gives rise to three main problems: (1) lack of transparency of the trained network, (2) lack of robustness to adversarial attacks, and (3) waste of resources due to excessive training times. These problems can be mitigated by reducing the number of parameters, which can be done by creating shallower models while preserving the performance. Simplification can also be achieved by imposing constraints on the learning algorithm and deep-learning architecture to prevent exploitations of attributes related to gender, race, religion, age and their covariates. SimplifAI's goal is to develop, evaluate, and validate simplified versions of existing over-parameterized deep learning algorithms (e.g., ResNet, BERT). The resulting simplified algorithms will be evaluated in terms of transparency (To what extent can we understand how the algorithm arrives at decisions and to what extent it adheres to the principle of fairness?), robustness (How sensitive is the algorithm to adversarial attacks?), and resource consumption (How much energy is required for training and running the algorithm?). A set of guidelines will be defined to identify the most suitable simplification methods and metrics to apply in practice. The project goals address the Artificial Intelligence (AI) and autonomous systems topic of the KIA ICT roadmap. For KPN to maintain an (inter)national leading position as ICT systems and Telecom provider it wants to be at the forefront of creating responsible AI solutions. Developing methods for Fairness Quantification is crucial in ensuring that its solutions will not have disparate impact to certain groups based on attributes like but not limited to gender, race, religion, colour, age, and their covariates.

Projecttitel: ThermOpt - Hybrid modelling and sensor/actuator layout optimization for thermal control in lithography
Projectbeschrijving: In wafer scanners used in the semiconductor industry, an increasing number of thermal control loops has been introduced to limit the undesired effects due to thermal disturbances on positioning performance. Advanced thermal control solutions will become even more important for future machines, as - on the one hand - the thermal disturbances in the machine will increase further and - on the other hand -performance objectives will become more stringent...To support future system designs, including hardware design, sensor and actuator layout and thermal control solutions, two key challenges arise: "How to construct computationally tractable and accurate dynamic models of the thermo-mechanical systems?" and "How to optimize thermal sensor and actuator layout in support of thermal control?" Therefore, the main objectives of this project are:..- To develop a hybrid (i.e., combined physics- and data-based) modelling approach for thermo-mechanical dynamics resulting in computationally tractable and accurate models. In this scope, this proposal aims to investigate the role of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN's) in combination with fast and efficient training algorithms...- To develop a control-aware optimization approach for thermal sensor and actuator layout in support of thermal control, while coping with complexifying aspects related to nonlinearities in the thermal dynamics and robustness requirements following from practical ASML use cases. Both in the modelling and optimization aspects, the development of AI-based methodologies is foreseen...The scientific results of the project will be validated by application to a practically representative set of use case scenarios.

Projecttitel: TOWR - Towards Open World Robotics Research Program
Projectbeschrijving: The TOWR project will bring robotics to the next level by providing an ability for individual robots to empathise with other robots and their abilities to perform such tasks, allowing pools of robots to perform tasks when individual robots are unavailable.

De telecommunicatie sector is constant aan het innoveren voor onze digitale samenleving van de toekomst. Er ligt nu een immense kans in het ontwikkelen van de volgende generatie kunstmatige intelligentie: één die een evolutie is van onze klassieke data-only aanpak; één die een geïntegreerde data-mens-machine aanpak neemt. Wij gaan geavanceerde nieuwe kunstmatige intelligentie ontwikkelen, die ons zal helpen om nog beter beslissingen te nemen binnen complexe KPN systemen waarin onzekerheid een uitdagende rol speelt. Onze nieuwe algoritmen zullen bijvoorbeeld inkomende verzoeken bij callcenters efficiënt kunnen toewijzen aan medewerkers wiens expertises en ervaringen onderling verschillen, en mogelijk zelfs veranderen over de tijd..Concreet mikt dit voorstel op het realiseren van doorbraken in de ontwikkeling van reinforcement learning technieken wanneer deze worden toegepast op grote, hoog-dimensionele data sets die onderliggende verborgen structuren hebben. Wij gaan dit doen door de allernieuwste methodes binnen de toegepaste kansrekening te combineren: wij gaan load-balancing algoritmen en wachtrijtheorie, als ook clustering algoritmen en multi-arm bandietproblemen, wiskundig combineren met Markov beslissingsproblemen. Deze geïntegreerde aanpakken zijn grotendeels onbekend terrein, en voortgang zal van grote waarde zijn in zowel wetenschappelijk als praktisch opzicht. Door middel van zorgvuldig ontwikkelde, wiskunde-gebaseerde methoden voor dimensionaliteitreductie zullen wij in staat zijn om nieuwe leeralgoritmen te ontwerpen die niet alleen exponentieel sneller zijn, maar ook bewijsbaar de best mogelijke.

Projecttitel: ViPERS - Virtual Product Engineering for Reliability and Safety
Projectbeschrijving: Decarbonization of heat and power has led to a large interest in hydrogen as a medium to store and transport energy, and as a source of direct heat, replacing natural gas in industry and households. Bosch Thermotechnology is focusing on hydrogen technologies for domestic appliances, with a hydrogen research center planned for 2022-2025 in Deventer. TU Eindhoven and Bosch have identified the need for an open digital platform for virtual product development that combines accurate and fast physics models to smart design tools. Novel aspects are the treatment of the system at different levels: detailed physics models at the lowest level and reduced order digital twin models using machine learning approaches at the system level. Smart and accurate approaches to investigate the safety, reliability and lifetime of components and systems are the key challenges..The goal is to develop an open platform for virtual product development of appliances for the heat and power industry, with in this project a focus on reliability and safety aspects of domestic hydrogen applications. Development and implementation of novel models for safety and functional assessment in design optimization software at component and system level. Implementation and assessment of machine learning methods in a smart setup for analysis of components and appliances in the development phase as well as development of novel robust and reliable smart sensing and control system for next generation hydrogen appliances.

Projecttitel: DDLC - Defect Driven Local Charging - Study & control of particles in a small vacuum gap with a high electric field
Projectbeschrijving: To meet the international Technology Roadmap for Semiconductors (ITRS), future ASML machines require improved performance in terms of overlay, focus and throughput. Currently defectivity (particles) in the vacuum clamping gap needed for electrostatic clamping of wafers and/or reticles affects the overlay performance and the effect is expected to further deteriorate performance when moving to increased throughput. To further minimize overlay impact and secure a technology roadmap it is needed to understand, control and optimize how particles behave in the clamping gap. This can be done for example by immobilizing the particles and/or minimize their trapping and emission of charge or maybe even to actively remove them, e.g. by an electrostatic pickup means, after their location has been identified from scanner and/or metrology data..The ultimate goal is to understand the behaviour of realistic (size & shape) conducting and dielectric particles in typical clamping gaps under relevant conditions, to optimize the geometry and (both) surfaces to minimize the impact of particles on the performance, to improve understanding and improve the performance of today's particle removal methods and to propose, specify and develop an in-situ tool to remove such particles..The specific goal for the PhD in this project is (a) Study the behaviour of particles in a gap using first principles, numerical models and experimental verification. This includes effects like field emission, secondary emission, polarization, microdischarges, electron induced outgassing and charge (de)trapping. (b) Specify, develop, manufacture and test improved configurations, incl. surfaces, possible treatments and cleaning methods to optimize the behaviour of particles in a gap with a high electric field.

Projecttitel: H2PSI - Understanding H2 plasma surface interaction
Projectbeschrijving: Plasmas form a real enabler in the semiconductor industry and they lie at the base of many nanotechnologies applied for the manufacturing of electronic integrated circuits and other devices. This is part of both the trends within "More Moore" (miniaturization of devices) and "More than Moore" (functional diversification). Traditionally plasmas have been used to etch and deposit materials through methods such as reactive ion etching and plasma-enhanced deposition and as such plasma systems have been omnipresent in semiconductor fabs already for half a century. Yet the importance of plasma steps and plasma surface interaction is still growing tremendously as many of the steps involved in these atomic-scale methods and in the processing of the nanoscale materials are plasma-based..The goal of the project is to measure the species on surfaces exposed to an (EUV-induced) H2 plasma, providing an understanding to degradation mechanisms, and offering the possibility to explore solution paths. The highly detailed insight into the H2 plasma surface interaction will also generate generic insight that is beneficial for other fields of technology with the domains of the semiconductor, photonic and renewable energy industries.

Projecttitel: Metalenses - Multi-element metalenses for improved matching and chromatic correction
Projectbeschrijving: Metalenses are nanostructured planar surfaces that can act like conventional lenses. They promise to be a disruptive technology in optics that could replace bulky refractive lenses in many applications. A conventional lens introduces a phase delay to a plane wave that depends on position. The phase control of the waves interacting with metalenses is provided by scattering with nanoparticles that are judiciously positioned on the surface and is controlled by varying dimensions, shape, orientation and/or material of the nanoparticles over the surface. The increase of degrees of freedom for the design of metalenses compared to conventional lenses and their planar structure are the reasons for the myriad of possibilities that these nanostructured surfaces offer. In this project we will investigate the benefits that metalenses offer to optical metrology in semiconductor manufacturing. They potentially have smaller as-made aberration variation than conventional lenses due to better-controlled manufacturing, improved lens-to-lens matching, and unconventional forms of (chromatic) aberration correction. They offer an unconventional optical design freedom. These characteristics make metalenses ideal candidates for the realization of achromatic systems with improved performance that can be used for imaging or metrology. .The project goals include design, simulation and characterization of metalens design and aberration theory for multi-element planar metalenses or hybrid lenses for high-end imaging. Study of (apo)chromatic aberration correction and field aberrations using broadband imaging interferometry. Determine how the design of metalenses impacts transmission..It also includes manufacturing sensitivity and wavefront shaping: Study of metalens aberration sensitivity to lithographic processes using scanning scatterometry and correlated microscopies. Explore the limits for aberration correction in metalenses by designing adaptative systems. Reach aberration levels of a few tens of milliwaves RMS in the visible.

With increasing cyber crime and the advent of quantum computing, data that is secured with today's standard cryptographic methods is increasingly under threat. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is a technology that distributes a data encryption key by using quantum effects in such a way that it is secure against wiretapping-attacks. With this, QKD helps to protect data from attacks today and in the future and is believed to play an essential role in securing networks with high-value data, such as critical infrastructure, governmental, and financial data. QuTech as one of the globally leading institutes in quantum technology has been working on the development of a specific QKD-based system, called MDI-QKD (measurement device independent QKD) for a number of years. Such a system offers a range of advantages in security and cost-efficiency when building larger networks, compared to existing point-to-point QKD.

Projecttitel: Wide Band Phased Arrays - Toward Extreme Efficiency Ultra Wide band, Wide Angle Scanning
Projectbeschrijving: The Tera Hertz Sensing (TS) Group has been leading the state of the art of ultra-wide band phased arrays for over a decade. Recently this  competitive advantage is recognize by many international companies that directly support this work with a continuous influx of third money stream. Most recently Thales France, has signed a contract with the TS group to develop a novel phased array antenna for their next generation airborne radar for fighter jets. The specific problems they would like to be addressed is the use of wide angle scanning and two frequency bandwidths of operations..The purpose of this project is to gain insigth into the physics borne limitations of phased arrays used for multibeam scenarios. Virtually all multi-beam phased arrays previously developed in military architectures operate in relatively narrow frequency ranges (with relative bandwidths measured in tens of percent). However the maximum number of beams that can be supported by multi-beam antennas is not well defined when the antennas operate over wide frequency ranges. Specifically when a multi-beam array is supposed to operate on a BW 1 to 3, as it will be the case for all next generation phased arrays to be covering the bands up to 100 GHz, all the existing rules of thumbs lose applicability.  This project will addresss this challenges to allow the TS group to face this next generation array challenges.

Projecttitel: Broadband Ptychography and Wavelength-Diversity for SXR
Projectbeschrijving: Whereas throughput of monochromatic ptychography as a metrology solution may be limited in terms of the available photon flux, broadband ptychography could lead to a significant improvement in terms of acquisition time. However, the superimposed contributions from multiple harmonics of the high-harmonic source (HHG) to the far-field diffraction patterns needs to be unscrambled via specifically devised signal processing as is now being investigated in scaled experiments with visible light at LINX. The signal processing is based on the concept of automatic differentiation. Secondly, broadband ptychography would require a new optics design for the illumination branch, i.e. different multilayer mirrors are needed to select more harmonics of the HHG source.

Projecttitel: Neuromorphic smart sensing for low-latency motion segmentation and analysis
Projectbeschrijving: Exploiting the finegrained temporal dynamics captured by neuromorphic image sensors is difficult. Indeed, offloading computation to the cloud loses the latency advantage of such sensors, conventional CPU/GPU architectures are ill-matched for spike-based event-driven processing, .and current neuromorphic hardware does not allow for a robust microsecond-latency processing within power budgets suitable for near-sensor edge intelligence...The goal of this project is to fill this gap in three steps by:.1) designing microsecond-latency neuromorphic hardware for near-sensor intelligence by leveraging the principle of digital in-memory computation,.2) developing a framework for mapping emerging neuromorphic/AI algorithms to the proposed hardware architecture,.3) demonstrating the resulting neuromorphic hardware/algorithm stack on a motion-segmentation and analysis use case.

In state-of-the-art positionerings-systemen voor halfgeleiderfabricage en andere opto-mechatronische toepassingen zijn veel kritische mechanische componenten onderdeel van een regellus om het vereiste dynamische gedrag te bereiken. Dit vereist dat een effectieve computer-ondersteunde ontwerpmethode integraal de prestaties van het gehele geregelde systeem beschouwd, inclusief de invloed van verstoringen op nauwkeurigheid en stabiliteit. Verder is het zeer gewenst het potentieel van integratie van dempende materialen in de componenten te kunnen benutten, aangezien dit beperkingen door ongewenste vibraties sterk kan reduceren.

Projecttitel: BioXolo - Next-generation volumetric printing of living matter
Projectbeschrijving: We here propose to pioneer clinically-scalable Xolographic bioprinting of large living organs with similar intrinsic resolution and functions as observed in native tissues. As concrete proof-of-principle, we will engineer fully vascularized bone tissue for treatment of large bone-defects, which represent ~5-10% of bone-fractures, causes permanent disability, and costs $9.2 billion/year in global-healthcare.

Our proposal consists of two parts. The first part focusses on using adaptive techniques to design photonic processors which are more robust to fabrication errors, as well as better strategies for programming those processors. This proposal will therefore help keep and strengthen the competitive advantage we have just built up with large-scale photonic processors. In the second part we will carry out a proof-of-principle experiment using a custom-built enhanced processor. The idea is to make a random-number generator with our photonic processor seeded remotely in such a way that it can be verified that the numbers are produced by quantum interference and hence are truly random. Although now generally accepted, this would exploit what Einstein believed could not be true: "God doesn't play dice".

Om een volgende stap te kunnen maken is het nodig om meer fundamentele kennis te hebben van de relatie tussen de coating structuur, de chemische samenstelling en het gedrag van de coating. - Met de resultaten uit dit project worden design regels voor het ontwikkelen van een nieuwe coating gegenereerd. Projecttitel: DiRAc - Distributed High-Resolution Automotive Radar for Autonomous and Secure Mobility
Projectbeschrijving: Advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) are transforming cars into securely-connected, highly-autonomous vehicles sensing the environment and making adequate decisions in a huge number of traffic conditions. Key components are radar transceivers measuring the range, angle, and velocity of objects around the vehicle. The penetration of radars into urban scenarios requires extremely high angular resolution to separate pedestrians, bicycles, etc. Angular resolution is a challenge for single mm-wave radars of limited aperture size. We will therefore pursue a distributed, synchronized network of small aperture radar sensors in this research project.  It deals with high-resolution imaging of the environment using a moving platform, wideband mm-wave signals, and multiple distributed MIMO radars with a small number of antennas. Solutions for four critical radar architectural and signal processing challenges will be pursued: Imaging topology, waveform and radar synchronization, 360 degrees image focusing, and bistatic signaling. The work proposed in this program is to be executed by two PhDs, one concentrating on IC design aspects and the other on radar signal processing. Both disciplines are crucial for the next steps in distributed radar system development and successful introduction into the automotive marketplace.

ASML's EUV lithography scanner is the cutting edge tool that enables writing the smallest features on the latest generation chips for everything from 5G to mobile phone processors and AI chips for self-driving cars. One of the most sensitive components of the whole lithography process is the mask, also called 'Reticle' in EUV lithography. The reticle is the master pattern that is replicated on every chip being printed. This reticle needs to be protected from particles landing on it at all cost, as a particle of even a few nm on the mask would be replicated as a printing error on every single chip passing through the scanner.

Projecttitel: Fundaments of a Construction Logistics Control Tower (CLCT) 2023

CLCT's beloven grote voordelen te bieden (20% in kilometers en ongeveer 15% in BKG-emissies) door aanzienlijke verbeteringen in de samenwerking met belanghebbenden en informatie-uitwisseling, maar ontbreken nog in de bouwsector. Het onderzoeksproject onderzoekt de functionele vereisten voor CLCT's van alle betrokken belanghebbenden en de beschikbare gegevensbronnen en ontwikkelt een conceptueel en functioneel ontwerp voor CLCT's. In het project worden de state-of-the-art technologieën en standaarden die relevant zijn voor de bouw en logistiek onderzocht en gebruikt als basis voor het ontwerp. Het onderzoek zal zich richten op twee soorten CLCT's, met name: 1) CLCT voor individuele, op projecten gebaseerde toeleveringsketens; 2) CLCT voor verkeersstromen in gebieden.

Projecttitel: PLATO (Platforms and digital transformation in logistics)
Projectbeschrijving: Digitization is transforming the logistics function, and digital platforms accelerate this transformation, while being closely linked to another major transformation: the greening of transport and logistics. Digital green policies are crucial to meet the Green Deal ambitions, as recognized by RLI . Therefore, the logistics sector has to embrace this digital transformation in order to become sustainable, add value , remain competitive, and create resilience capabilities to cope with disruptive forces. This project aids the sector to embrace the digital transformation, recognize the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats of platformisation and act accordingly. Previous research highlighted the disruptive potential of platformisation in logistics  and the pace of digital transformation demands for a quick and adequate response in logistics. However, the previous research also identified reluctance and difficulties to articulate this adequate response in platform implementation, corporate digital policies, and business process redesign. This project aims to help the sector to formulate such an adequate response to platformisation and digital transformation. In the project, we address two matters: (1) the logistics function is facing platformisation, which is an irreversible and (potentially) disruptive development; and (2) platformisation has potential to radically improve the logistics function also in terms of sustainability performance. Question is whether benefits as in (2) can be achieved while avoiding unintended consequences as in (1). This calls for a proper understanding of value adding services for the users and providers of the logistics function, the shippers, freight forwarders, and LSPs, and provide logistic ecosystem orchestrators with the measures to manage the disruptive character of platformisation in their communities.

Projecttitel: Aberration correction for digital holography imaging and metrology of semiconductor devices
Projectbeschrijving: Overlay metrology measures pattern placement between two layers in a semiconductor chip. The continuous shrinking of device dimensions drives the need to explore novel optical overlay metrology concepts that can address many of the existing metrology challenges. We present a compact dark-field digital holographic microscope that uses only a single imaging lens. Our microscope offers several features that are beneficial for overlay metrology, like a large wavelength range. However, imaging with a single lens results in highly aberrated images. In this work, we present an aberration calibration and correction method using nano-sized point scatterers on a silicon substrate. Computational imaging techniques are used to recover the full wavefront error, and we use this to correct for the lens aberrations. We present measured data to verify the calibration method and we discuss potential calibration error sources that must be considered. A comparison with a ZEMAX calculation is also presented to evaluate the performance of the presented method.

Projecttitel: 3DHybCrete - Towards circular Netherlands: Turning waste to resource through 3D printed Hybrid Concrete Structures
Projectbeschrijving: Urgent ideas are needed to reduce the waste stream from construction sector, save earth’s natural resources and provide CO2 neutral construction. Although promising, the crushing of old concrete and creating recycled aggregate that can be reused as raw material for new concrete impairs its long-term properties and durability. Hybrid concrete systems with high-performance materials and new manufacturing technology are the future. The project will develop a novel system in which the shell, “important” zone in the structure (i.e. critical for durability), is made by newly developed high-quality 3D-Printed Strain Hardening Cementitious Composite, SHCC, with recycled fine aggregates (3DP/Re-SHCC), whereas low quality recycled aggregate concrete is used as “low” demanding infill. The major challenge is defining the relations between (i) long-term structural behaviour and durability of the hybrid system made from recycled materials and (ii) the fundamental mechanisms on a lower level, related to time-dependent material behaviour, printability and interfaces (i.e. between printed layers in the material, and between shell and infill in the hybrid structure). In this position, your key research objectives will be to:  correlate the 3DP/Re-SHCC mix designs to printability (i.e. pumpability, extrudability, buildability), and correlate 3DP/Re-SHCC hardened properties (strength, ductility, anisotropy) to its mix design, printing parameters and interfaces between the layers of the circular material  unravel the influence of structural interfaces and coupled hygro-mechanical processes between the 3DP/Re-SHCC shell and the recycled aggregatge concrete infill on the long-term structural behaviour and durability of the hybrid system. This position is funded by TKI HTSM and supported by several industrial partners. The project is embedded in a cross-departmental collaboration within the faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences (CiTG), including the Department of Engineering Structures (ES) and the Department of Mechanics, Materials, Management and Design (3MD).

Projecttitel: Strong and tough: Green Meets Circular
Projectbeschrijving: Many  plastics  materials  are  quite strong and stiff (relatively  high value  for tensile  strength and modulus) ,  but are characterized  by relatively low toughness and impact properties in general.  This dichotomy is very well known and typical of polymer science.  It is also known, at least for commercially relevant plastic materials, that an increase  in strength and stiffness  often  results  in decreased  toughness  and vice  versa.  Additionally, in the  last  few  decades  the need  to find  an optimum between  these  two extremes  of mechanical  behavior has  become  even  more relevant  as  plastics derived  from biomass  have  been  trying to replace  oil-derived  ones.  Several  strategies  are  available  to increase  toughness,  the most popular one being the use of rubber (particles)  dispersed into the matrix polymer.In this project we aim at using recycled rubber (e.g. car tires) derived from the recently patented process by the University of Groningen in order to endow (green) plastic with the necessary  impact properties. As the recycling process is new and being commercially implemented “ as we speak”, the corresponding recycled rubber streams (never accessible so far) constitute a relevant novelty of this project.
