Projecttitel: CODED: COntrolled DElivery of Drugs in glioblastoma
Projectbeschrijving: In this project, we aim to develop an adhesive hemostatic hydrogel glue that allows for a localized, controlled release of encapsulated therapeutics intracranially, circumventing the poor passage of compounds across the blood-brain-barrier. By using drugs that have been clinically proven in other indications, the project has a balanced risk-profile and a rapid route towards clinical translation. We combine clinical experience with innovative academic research on experimental matrices, invented in an existing collaboration between the UMC Utrecht and SentryX. .The approach is based on a (natural) polymer hydrogel glue, SNX-51, that adheres to the cavity wall after brain surgery and prevents bleeding. This glue is empowered by loading it with therapeutics, dexamethasone initially. After surgery and during radiotherapy, high doses of systemic dexamethasone are administered to prevent brain swelling. By incorporating dexamethasone into the glue, controlled local release can inhibit inflammation while avoiding systemic adverse effects. Another approach, investigated to a limited extent in glioblastoma, is the addition of radiosensitizers to the radiation schedule, where controlled release can ensure optimal synergy with radiotherapy. Local depots could also clear the way for chemotherapeutics that are unable to cross the blood-brain-barrier, including biologicals. The loaded glue will be designed, synthesized and tested for local drug release in advanced in-vitro/ex vivo brain models to prepare an Investigator’s Brochure for veterinary patients for proof-of-concept..This project addresses a large unmet need for a patient group that has missed out on advances in the cancer field in recent decades....Doelen.WP1. The aim of this subproject is to define the critical characteristics of SNX-51 that:.• Provide optimal adhesive properties.• Effectuate good hemostatic activity.• Enable drug encapsulation..WP2. .The aim of this WP is to develop local treatment support with controlled release for prolonged periods of time of therapeutics. We will initially focus on dexamethasone for anti-edema formation...WP3.The aim of this WP is herapeutic testing in advanced in vitro/ex vivo models of glioblastoma....

Projecttitel: Target characterizationwith MRI/PET for MRI-guided radiotherapy of metastatic disease
Projectbeschrijving: Over 20.000 cancer patients present with metastasized disease in The Netherlands yearly. Traditonally, only systemic therapies are used for metastasized disease. However, the Elekta Unity MR-linac enables precise stereotactic irradiation of multiple small metastases, by combining an MRI scanner with a linear accelerator. The addition of local treatment for (poly)metastatic disease is a paradigm shift in the treatment of metastatic cancer. However, highly detailed information about the target sites is crucial for precise planning of the radiation delivery. Therefore, we are developing a 1.5T wide bore MRI/PET system designed specifically for radiotherapy planning. This system aims to combine two benefits, that cannot be achieved by acquiring the MRI and PET images separately: 1) The MRI scanner allows for the characterization of motion by 3D MRI motion tracking. This is crucial for the detection of small tumour volumes and the successful dose planning of moving targets. 2) The PET scanner acquires functional information of the pathophysiology of the target site. This gives information about the aggressiveness and treatment response of the tumor. The goal of this project is to develop MRI motion tracking techniques to constantly track 3D motion (with >3 Hz and 3 mm resolution). The obtained MRI-based motion information throughout the exam is then used to correct PET images that would otherwise be blurred by motion, enabling the acquisition of high-quality PET images. Feasibility will be shown in a clinical pilot study on 10 adult patients. The proposed research builds on our track record of fast MR-based 3D motion estimation for MR guided radiotherapy. Besides the clinical breakthrough for metastasized cancer patients this new MRI/PET system will position the Philips/Elekta alliance as the major company in this new field of image guided radiotherapy.

Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a frequent, dose-limiting, and debilitating side effect of anti-cancer drugs (e.g. oxaliplatin) that may not resolve after therapy discontinuation. Currently, no effective treatment, either prophylactic or on demand, is available for CIPN. This project is a first step to a possible solution of this huge unmet medical need.

Projecttitel: Integrated fluorescence- and radioguidance during PSMA-targeted prostate cancer surgery
Projectbeschrijving: Prostate cancer is the 5th most common cancer in The Netherlands (10% of cancers in men) with yearly more than 10,000 new patients and more than 2,500 prostate cancer-related deaths. Upon initial diagnosis, most patients will initially undergo (robot-assisted) surgical removal of the primary tumor, so-called prostatectomy. Of the estimate 2500-3000 annual prostatectomies in the Netherlands, about 25% show irradical resection and about 20% require extended pelvic lymph node dissections (ePLND; Briganti score > 5%). These limitations create a demand for surgical guidance technologies that help increase the surgical accuracy, reduce the number of complications and reduce the need for additional follow-up treatments, such as prolonged hormonal therapy, radiation therapy, and/or salvage surgery. Over the last decade, PSMA-PET has radically improved preoperative staging of patients and creates a surgical roadmap, thus creating a new paradigm in prostate cancer care. We now aim to effectively translate the preoperative roadmap to the surgical field using a hybrid PSMA tracer that not only facilitates intraoperative fluorescence- and radio-guidance, but that can also be navigated upon using a modified DROP-IN gamma probe. To realize our mission to radically advance PSMA-targeted surgery, we will pursue three main objectives: 1) Create a clinical grade kit formulation of our hybrid PSMA tracer (99mTc-EuK-(SO3)Cy5-mas3), 2) Develop clinically compatible navigation options for our DROP-IN gamma probe technology, and 3) Implement both technologies during a first-in-human trial.

Projecttitel: Development of a tool box for ubiquitin metalloproteases.
Projectbeschrijving: Ubiquitine is een klein regulerend eiwit dat in bijna alle weefsels voorkomt. Het volgen van.signalering door ubiquitine is belangrijk om te begrijpen hoe cruciale cellulaire processen.werken. Een klasse enzymen dat betrokken is bij de regulatie van ubiquitine zijn de.zogenaamde metalloDUBs. Vanwege hun belangrijke rol in de regulatie van vele.biologische processen, worden zij gezien als potentiële aanknopingspunten voor.medicijnontwikkeling. Er is echter een groot tekort aan effectieve reagentia voor onderzoek.aan metalloDUBs. De ontwikkeling hiervan is achtergebleven door de relatief complexe.werking van metalloDUBs. Ons onderzoeksplan heeft als doel om met behulp van recent.ontwikkelde chemie dit te verhelpen en twee klasse reagentia te ontwikkelen om.metalloDUBs te herkennen en karakteriseren. De eerste klasse reagentia is gebaseerd op.een uniek ontwerp dat het mogelijk maakt om actieve metalloDUBs heel sterk te binden,.en zo de identificatie van (nieuwe) metalloDUBs mogelijk te maken. De tweede klasse.reagentia stelt ons in staat om metalloDUB activiteit te meten in zogenaamde assay.formaat; dit is van belang voor medicijnontwikkeling en het bestuderen van de rol die.mutaties in metalloDUBs spelen in ziekten. Samenvattend, de reagentia die wij willen.ontwikkelen zullen helpen bij het bevorderen van onze kennis van metalloDUBs wat.uiteindelijk een belangrijke rol zal spelen in het ontwikkelen van nieuwe medicijnen.biomarkers.

Projecttitel: Towards novel innovative enterovirus vaccine approaches
Projectbeschrijving: De groep van enterovirussen bevat belangrijke ziekteverwekkers voor mens en dier. Hieronder vallen het bekende poliovirus: de veroorzaker van polio, rhinovirus: wat onder andere verkoudheid veroorzaakt, en ook opkomende virussen zoals enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) wat een belangrijke oorzaak is van hand-voet-mond ziekte (HVMZ) en ook ernstige neurologische complicaties en zelfs verlamming kan veroorzaken. HVMZ kan daarnaast ook worden veroorzaakt door groep A coxsackievirussen (CV-A), zoals CV-A16, CV-A10 en CV-A6. HVMZ is met name in Azië een groot probleem, met jaarlijks honderden slachtoffers in China, maar ook in Europa (o.a. Spanje en Frankrijk) en de Verenigde Staten zijn de laatste jaren uitbraken geweest geassocieerd met neurologische symptomen. Hierdoor is er een grote behoefte aan een multivalent HVMZ vaccin gericht tegen EV-A71 en deze CV-A virussen.  ..Vaccins wekken een immuunrespons op zonder mensen ziek te maken en beschermen tegen een latere infectie en ziekte. In dit project willen wij onderzoeken of we nieuwe generatie van enterovirus vaccin kandidaten kunnen ontwikkelen. Omdat sommige CV-A virussen, waaronder CV-A10 en CV-A6, heel moeilijk vermenigvuldigen op gekweekte cellen, gaan we stukjes van deze virussen aan de buitenkant van andere virussen toevoegen. Dit worden ook wel chimere virussen genoemd. Wij zullen chimere EV-A71 en CA-A16 virussen maken die stukjes van CV-A10 of CV-A6 aan hun buitenkant bevatten, zodat tegen meerdere virussen tegelijkertijd een immuun response wordt opgewekt. Met deze aanpak kan de moeizame vermenigvuldiging van CV-A10 of CV-A6 op cellijnen worden omzeild. Deze strategie kan de basis vormen voor een multivalent HVM vaccin en zal binnen het project worden getest in diermodellen voor hun eigenschap om een goede immuunrespons op te wekken...De uitkomsten van dit project kunnen worden doorontwikkeld voor nieuwe HVMZ vaccins. De toepassing van deze nieuwe technologieën is breed en kan ook worden gebruikt voor verbeterde vaccins tegen andere enterovirussen en rhinovirussen.

Projecttitel: Precision treatments In moNogenic ePilepsies:.Observational regIstry and N-of-1 Trial recommendations
Projectbeschrijving: Uit recent DNA-onderzoek weten we dat in een kwart van de ernstige kinderepilepsieën de oorzaak een verandering (mutatie) is van één enkel gen. In deze zogenaamde monogenetische epilepsieën ligt een precisiebehandeling voor de hand. In zo’n behandeling wordt heel specifiek ingegrepen op de specifieke gevolgen van die gen-verandering. Omdat het echter om zulke zeldzame ziektevormen gaat, is het niet mogelijk om deze precisiehandelingen te onderzoeken in een klassieke klinische studie (een zgn. gerandomiseerde trial). De weinige kinderen met zo’n aandoening tonen ook nog eens veel variatie in hun ziektebeeld..Om een behandeling empirisch te onderzoeken is een veelbelovende, maar nog relatief onbekende, studieopzet de n-is-1 studie. In zo’n studie functioneert één kind – de enige (proef)persoon in de studie – als zijn eigen controle. Dit kan door de behandeling in opeenvolgende periodes afwisselend wel of niet te geven..Echter, er zijn momenteel geen specifieke richtlijnen voor de methodiek, geen softwareprogramma’s, voor dergelijke n-is-1 studies..TKI-LSH (Match) PPP Allowance application form 2021.8.PINPOINT wil hierin voorzien. We hebben daarvoor een unieke samenwerking opgezet tussen het nationale referentiecentrum voor zeldzame epilepsieën, twee internationaal gerenommeerde vakgroepen verbonden aan Nederlandse universiteiten, en een toonaangevende industriële partner op het gebied van digitale gezondheidsinnovaties toegespitst op neurologische aandoeningen..Als consortium gaan we een methodologisch kader ontwikkelen dat helemaal is toegespitst op de n-is-1 behandeling van monogene epilepsieën. We zullen patiënt-gecentreerde uitkomstmaten ontwikkelen en in een app opnemen, en gebruiksvriendelijke en open-source software ontwikkelen voor n-is-1 studie s..Met deze aanpak verbeteren we de geïndividualiseerde zorg voor patiënten met zeldzame monogene epilepsieën in een groot Europees netwerk van epilepsiecentra. Tegelijkertijd verwachten we dat de te ontwikkelen software en methodiek voor n-is-1 studies ook kan worden toegepast bij andere zeldzame ziektebeelden.

Projecttitel: NudgeMe: Digital Nudges for Healthy Food Choice: Empirical, Ethical and Design Perspectives On Personalised Digital Nudging Techniques
Projectbeschrijving: Keuzeomgevingen beïnvloeden gezondheidsgedrag via nudges. Momenteel zijn supermarkten ingericht als een omgeving die vooral ongezonde voedselkeuzes stimuleert en dit belemmert de preventie en het zelfmanagement van chronische ziekten zoals Type 2 Diabetes. In dit project wordt gekeken naar de empirische, ethische en technologische perspectieven die relevant zijn bij het ontwerpen van gepersonaliseerde nudges ter bevordering van de gezondheid, en meer specifiek het bevorderen van gezonde voedselkeuzes..Het empirische doel is om te onderzoeken via welke mechanismen personalisatie de effecten van nudging kan versterken en de rol van transparantie hierin. We onderzoeken dit in de context van een innovatieve digitale nudge, namelijk de Just-In-Time nudge. Verder zullen de effecten in het veld worden getest bij Type 2 Diabetes patiënten, voor wie een suikerarm dieet cruciaal is..Het ethische doel is om een genuanceerd normatief kader te genereren voor gepersonaliseerde digitale nudges op het gebied van gezondheidsbevordering. Transparantie en acceptatie spelen een cruciale rol in de ethische evaluatie van nudges. We gaan onderzoeken in welke mate het gepersonaliseerde en digitale karakter van nudges kan bijdragen aan het wegnemen van morele bezwaren die gezondheidsbevorderende nudges mogelijk oproepen..Het technologische doel is het bepalen van de (technologische) uitdagingen en kansen van personalisatie in mobiele technologie en de interactie daarvan met de fysieke keuzeomgeving, d.w.z. de supermarkt. Dit heeft betrekking op de mogelijke effecten van het implementeren van de nudges op de ‘user-flow’ binnen de applicatie en de gebruikerservaring..Dit project is innovatief zowel in zijn focus (gepersonaliseerde, digitale nudges) als zijn mixed-methods benadering, waarbij gebruik wordt gemaakt van gecontroleerde labstudies en een veldstudie in combinatie met ethische analyses en design-gerelateerd onderzoek. De resultaten kunnen worden gebruikt voor het ontwikkelen van een ondersteunende preventieve omgeving die gezonde consumenten in staat stelt gezondere voedingskeuzes te maken en die zelfmanagement bij patiënten met chronische ziekten bevordert.

Projecttitel: Understanding the interplay between materials and surface technology for the prevention of biofilm formation and orthopedic infections (EMILIO = Understanding intErplay Material bacterIaL orthopaedic InfectiOns)
Projectbeschrijving: Infection of medical devices is a devastating and very costly complication that usually requires multiple surgeries and considerable pharmaceutical intervention to promote healing. With the rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance to antibiotics, technologies that prevent an infection by prohibiting bacterial attachment to implant materials are crucial.This fundamental research project will commence by investigating two antimicrobial properties with or without external release for specific medical device implant related materials. The application process for Cobalt-Chromium, Titanium alloy, UHMWPE, and PEEK will be investigated and optimized. Antimicrobial properties will be tested using in vitro screening models according to ISO 22196. Safety will be assessed accoding to ISO 10993. Thereafter, coupon level characterization will be performed, including determination of biocompatibility and safety of the coating components in vitro and in vivo, including understanding the coupled interaction between substrates/anti-infective technology with respective biofilms using advanced imaging. An animal study utilizing the antimicrobial technologies will be started in the second year. The studies will aim to assess in vivo biological safety (including osteointegration), and antimicrobial experimental proof of concept for material-specific technologies. Upon successful completion of the project, selected technologies will be further tested with large animal models to obtain technology concept validation in the lab and work towards clinical implementation. Depending on the material system and applications, the clinical study timeframe for these technologies could be 2-3 years after project end.

Projecttitel: Exploration of smart implantable electromagnetic sensor technology for surgical navigation - ISSA (Implantable Sensors for Surgical Applications)
Projectbeschrijving: Background: Surgery is the main treatment for most solid cancers. However, in 20-25%.of patients undergoing surgery, tumor tissue is not completely removed or too much.healthy tissue is damaged, leading to long-term morbidity. The main reason for these.failures is that during surgery tumor boundaries are often difficult to identify by eye or.touch. To tackle these shortcomings, Bcon Medical is developing a surgical navigation.system that is based on a detailed CT or MR 3D roadmap in which surgical instruments.are tracked by electro-magnetic sensors. The system is using wired surface sensors on.the body and able to locate fixed tumors with mm accuracy..Objective: To acquire new knowledge and underlying foundations with regard to.wireless implantable sensor technology. Such sensors could be implanted near the.tumor enabling continuous tumor tracking and navigation in, non-fixed, mobile.tumors, which may change position due to surgical manipulation (liver, rectum,.prostate, lung). This guides the surgeon to find the correct resection planes..Design: We will research smart wireless electromagnetic implantable sensors equipped.with microelectronics in combination with a mobile sensing receiver unit (repeater) that,.in combination, is able to give precise 3D information of the tumor position and of.surgical instruments. The design of the new wireless system allows a seamless.integration with the wired system, currently developed by Bcon Medical..Social impact/economic impact: It is estimated that using implantable sensors for.surgical navigation can improve patient outcome in over 170.000 surgical procedures per.year (EU, USA). When assuming a 20% reduction in local recurrence due to more radical.resections, already a cost saving can be obtained of 300M€/yr for rectal cancer and.240M€/yr for prostate cancer.

Projecttitel: HEalth ReseArch - Cancer Living labs - setting up an Ecosystem of trust (Secure and Sovereign) - HERACLES
Projectbeschrijving: The yearly number of people diagnosed with cancer is increasing. In 2019, 800.000 people in the Netherlands are living with cancer. They experience a high disease burden and lower societal participation due to cancer (treatments). The aim of this project is to reduce the impact of cancer by retrieving novel insights into peoples’ health journey, which can only be gained through joint analysis of data (clinical, patient, epidemiology, quality, research) stored at different organizations. These insights bring real-world evidence to shared decision making in health and personalized prevention, treatment and support in clinical practice and in society..To achieve such data insights, parties in the health and technology domain join forces to create an innovative, sustainable, privacy-preserving and scalable data infrastructure built on trust. This infrastructure, the Health Data Space, enables stakeholders to request data insights by privacy-preserving analyses on the participating data sources. Serving the principles of the Personal Health Train, sensitive data is only reused for specific purposes. The data infrastructure will be generic, interoperable and scalable, thus applicable to other areas..We will demonstrate the possible impact of the Health Data Space through two use cases: ovarian and lung cancer. The ovarian cancer use case focuses on extending survival by insights in patterns of cancer recurrence and its treatments (new therapies). The lung cancer use case focuses on optimizing diagnostics to improve the care pathway and personalized decision making in health. For both cases, current data sets and linkage procedures are insufficient and not future-proof, due to challenges in trust, privacy and administration..The HERACLES methodology is holistic, taking governance, ethical, legal and societal conditions into account, and links to other initiatives. This will impact peoples’ health and participation, the quality of care and create a trustworthy data ecosystem centered around people with (chronic) conditions.

Projecttitel: ReconVac: Elucidating Immune Responses to Glycoconjugate Vaccines
Projectbeschrijving: Antibiotic resistance (AMR) is a major threat to the effective treatment of serious bacterial infections. 50% to 90% AMR in current Escherichia coli (E.coli) strains and an estimated 10 million yearly deaths in 2050 sketch a dramatic scenario. Vaccination is a far less resistance-prone treatment of bacterial infections, advantageously avoiding severe symptoms or even any infection entirely. However, vaccination is limited to prevention and by bacterial (strain) specificity. Bacterial polysaccharides (BPS) are well-established targets of protective immune responses. However, glycoconjugate vaccines (GCVs) generally induce longer, T-cell dependent immune responses, resulting in improved memory B-cell formation and opsonophagocytosis. Beyond these observations, immune responses to glycoconjugate vaccines are poorly understood which limits rational design..We aim to elucidate the antibody-mediated immune response to GCVs exemplarily on E.coli O-polysaccharides (O-PS). Quality and quantity of antibodies heavily determine the efficacy of the immune response, including functional pathways and effector cells. Diversity of antibody isotypes, glycoforms and affinity variants may explain opsonophagocytosis differences. Therefore, we will characterize anti-O-PS antibodies and B cell receptors and correlate the findings with opsonophagocytic and antigen-binding assays. We focus on antibody-mediated responses for the greater knowledge gap, compared to cellular responses. Differential results from various presentations and formulations of O-PS, will yield hallmarks of a favorable immune response and ways to achieve it..The project will thus provide fundamental knowledge on anti-BPS antibodies which will improve rational design of GCVs. Our results will contribute to improving vaccines against extraintestinal pathogenic E.coli (ExPEC) infections being developed at Janssen. Efficacious ExPEC vaccination of risk groups, can prevent millions of E.coli infections and billions of annual healthcare cost. Translation to other anti-bacterial vaccines, could prevent millions of bacteremia episodes and 100,000s of deaths..Thus, our investigation is an important step towards addressing patient needs and to managing the looming antibiotic resistance crisis.

Projecttitel: LYDEA: LY75, in DEpth And beyond
Projectbeschrijving: Background.Cutaneous melanoma is the most aggressive form of skin cancer, accounting for 80% of skin cancer-related deaths. There is a clear clinical need to improve the identification of aggressive melanoma lesions at diagnosis. This will enable personalized disease management (prevention of under- and overtreatment) and improve quality of life and prognosis of patients. Cancer-associated molecular alterations have been recognized as biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis prediction. Molecular profiling of melanoma in our laboratory (using a workflow combining methyl-binding domain, RNA-sequencing and Infinium 450k arrays) identified LY75 methylation as independent predictor of poor melanoma prognosis. We have patented this finding and have started a spin-off company named MLA Diagnostics to translate and develop this biomarker..Objective.Although the biomarker performance of LY75 is promising and cost-effective (early HTA analysis MLA Diagnostics), we hypothesize that complementary biomarkers will improve the performance of the LY75 test. In addition, it has not been explored whether LY75 could serve as a prognostic marker in other tumor types. The objective of this project is 1) to perform a biomarker search focusing on LY75 complementary melanoma markers and 2) to investigate the biomarker potential of LY75 in other cancer types..Design.Our laboratory at Maastricht University has a successful track record in identification and translation of cancer DNA methylation markers (Koch et al., 2018). In this project we will 1) use this expertise to in silico identify LY75 complementary melanoma markers, 2) in silico study the biomarker potential of LY75 in other cancer types, 3) validate the newly identified biomarkers and 4) perform health technology assessment analysis of the new biomarker(panels)..Social and economic impact.If successful, this project will improve the identification of aggressive cancer lesions, thereby enabling personalized treatment (prevention of under-and overtreatment), increase the quality of life of patients and possibly increase the survival of cancer patients. Economically, it wil reduce health care costs and support MLA Diagnostics in becoming a leading molecular diagnostics company.

Projecttitel: BTK-Msign: Identifying a functional lymphocyte signature for more personalized therapy with Bruton’s tyrosine kinase inhibitors in multiple sclerosis
Projectbeschrijving: Background.Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a devastating chronic inflammatory disease of the central nervous system, which cannot be aduately controlled or prevented. B cells play a fundamental role in MS, likely by interacting with T cells as initial event. Our group recently identified several B- and T-cell subsets that are associated with MS activity. Their development seems to be guided by B cell-intrinsic Bruton’s tyrosine kinase (BTK), which is an emerging therapeutic target in MS..Hypothesis and aim.We hypothesize that high BTK activity in B cells can be used to expose a B and T cell-based signature for MS. Such a disease signature can tell whether lymphocytes are prone to enter the brain and cause local inflammation. By identifying and combining the functional profiles of brain-homing B and T cells, we aim to generate a tool to better predict the clinical course and response to treatment in early MS..Study design.To identify B-cell genes, markers and subsets associated with BTK activity, we will analyze memory B cells with high and low phospho-BTK of treatment-naive MS patients and healthy controls using bulk RNA-sequencing and innonative spectral cytometry (>30 markers/cell). Identified B-cell clusters will be studied for interaction with TFH-like cells and their capacity to infiltrate the CNS (ex vivo and in vitro). Evobrutinib will be used to suppress BTK activity in vitro. A brain-homing B- and T-cell profile will be revealed by using blood, CSF and brain tissues of unique clinical MS cohorts..Social and economic impact.The results of this study will meet the urgent need for improved prognostification and more personalized treatment of MS. The identification of an MS signature based on the functional profiles of B and T cells will not only increase cost-effectiveness, but also avoid unnecessary and sometimes severe side-effects of B cell-directed therapies.

Projecttitel: CARDIOIDS: Comparative testing of human cARDiac organOIDs with animal models of inherited heart diseaSe
Projectbeschrijving: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a rare genetic cardiac disease characterized by.the progressive substitution of the myocardium with fibro-fatty tissue, ventricular.tachycardia and sudden death, the latter being often its sole manifestation. ACM is.classified as the second most common cause of sudden death in the young and may.account for 22% of arrhythmias or heart failure among athletes. To date, several.underlying gene mutations have been discovered of which PKP2 mutations are most.commonly found in ACM patients in North America and Europe. However, disease.mechanisms underlying ACM are extremely variable, hampering the development of novel.therapies..Development of human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) technology has been a.revolution in all areas of research, allowing us to culture any cell type of interest, including.human cardiomyocytes (CMs), in which pathogenic mechanisms of diseases may be fully.investigated. 2D-iPSC-based models allowed us to overcome the major limitations linked.to investigation on animal models and non-cardiac primary cells. This field now moves.toward the application of 3D-based differentiation protocols, enhancing the potential of.iPSC-based platforms for both cardiac disease modelling and drug screening purposes..At Maastricht University, a state-of-the-art engineered heart muscle platform using iPSC.technology was recently established. 2D-hiPSC-CMs are cultured from reprogrammed skin.fibroblasts from a patients carrying a PKP2 p.Arg79X mutation. Together with a unique.ACM mouse model that harbors the same knock-in mutation, unique 2D in vitro and in vivo.models have been established that mimic the ACM phenotype. Based on these foundations,.the CARDIOIDS collaborative project was defined with the aim to generate 3D cardiac.organoids and evaluate their functionality and predictive behaviour in comparison with the.existing models carrying the same PKP2 p.Arg79X mutation and clinical data. These three.dimensional cardiac organoids are expected to become a superior drug screening tool.supporting the development of new treatments for ACM.

Projecttitel: Generation of a human skeletal muscle-on-chip model containing extracellular matrix-producing fibroadipogenic progenitors and electrical impedance sensing
Projectbeschrijving: A major problem in developing therapies for neuromuscular disorders is the limited availability and translatability of current human model systems for preclinical research. To overcome this limitation, we recently developed a muscle-on-chip model using myogenic progenitors (MPs) generated from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). The muscle-on-chip model consists of a chip that contains pure muscle cells grown within an artificial extracellular matrix (ECM) in a 3D culture. It allows contractile force measurements, a readout commonly used in the clinic. Here, we aim to improve our 3D tissue engineered skeletal muscles (3D TESMs) to include fibroadipogenic progenitors (FAPs), which together with myogenic cells are responsible for generating the ECM in muscle tissue in vivo. FAPs and the ECM have essential roles in muscle fiber development, maturation, and regeneration, transmission of contractile force, and in providing mechanical integrity. In muscle disease, FAPs are responsible for fibrosis and fatty replacement. To monitor the changes in the composition and architecture of the 3D TESMs in a longitudinal, noninvasive manner, we will include electrical impedance as readout. We will compare electrical impedance with cell biological and biochemical analyses to monitor changes in fiber type maturation and the composition and organization of the ECM. The impact on contractile force of the 3D TESMs will be assessed in parallel. We will apply the improved muscle-on-chip model to the skeletal muscle disorders facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) and Pompe disease to assess the influence of FAPs on disease progression, muscle pathology, fibrosis, and fatty replacement. We expect that this device will also be relevant for other neuromuscular disorders as it will provide a tool to study basic disease mechanisms and will aid in the development and testing of treatment options.
Partners: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC), Optics11 B.V.

Projecttitel: IMAGINE: Innovations for the manufacturing and marketing of fully personalised food products
Projectbeschrijving: The main objective of the consortium project IMAGINE is to deliver personalised food products into consumers’ .daily life by connecting personal data and digital food manufacturing technology, thus allowing consumers to be .and/or perform at their best. IMAGINE will first identify drivers and barriers of consumer acceptance and .perceived added value of the personalised foods, as well as user requirements for the technology platform from .4 user groups (military, sport, patients and care personnel). IMAGINE will develop a vending-machine-type .Flexible Food Manufacturing Platform based on a digitally controlled 3D printing process. This will enable on.demand production of fully personalised food products, based on a personalised nutrition advice platform. The .IMAGINE technology will empower consumers, providing them with control over food properties and nutritional .content, in order to motivate them to choose healthier foods and to comply to a healthier diet on the long term..The value of the technology will be demonstrated in two field labs. As example of medical-care applications, .personalised products will be created in a rehabilitation centre for COPD patients. Due to a large clinical diversity.within this patient group, personalised foods can contribute to better recovery and reversal of the variable .comorbidities of COPD patients. In a field lab in a military setting, personalised foods will be provided to improve .physical performance, vigilance, and/or physiological recovery of military personnel. .IMAGINE brings together TNO’s and WFBR’s scientific expertise on health, personalised nutrition, consumer .behaviour, industrial innovation, and food science, with a consortium of renowned industrial partners in medical .and personalised nutrition, food products and food processing, as well as the stakeholders in the military and .care domain. Together, we set out to create, test, and demonstrate this first-of-its-kind technology to allow .consumers to select and manufacture the food products that fit with their individual bodies’ requirements, and .to form an ecosystem to implement and commercialise the outcomes of this project.

Projecttitel: Seaweed to slow down the aging of the vasculature: a nutritious.approach to battle dementia and vascular aging
Projectbeschrijving: In this project we will provide proof-of-principle that seaweeds that are eligible for sustainable agriculture can be used to produce healthy and safe food and are a source of molecules to protect against dysfunction of blood vessels and against dementia caused by aging. To do so, we will study the effect of seaweed--contained food on vascular aging and dementia. In addition, we will study effects, compare lipophilic molecules in seaweed species and test their effect on nuclear receptors, which have been implicated in protection against aging, vascular dysfunction and dementia. With these studies we hope to strengthen our portfolio and supplement that of Topsector, and thus increase the chances to set up a viable industry to produce novel health care products based on sustainable seaweed agriculture in the Netherlands.
Aanvrager: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC)

Projecttitel: It takes guts to BBB: Using sustainable omega-3 rich oils to improve gut-brain health
Projectbeschrijving: The goal of this research is to improve the market perspective of sustainable omega-3 rich oils, such as algae and krill oil, by demonstrating their health benefits. We will investigate the bioavailability/bioaccessibility and health benefits of different omega-3 oils in order to bring out their health benefits. The oils will be investigated within in vitro and in vivo gut immune and brain models to link bioavailability to bioactivity properties and confirm health aspects as seen for fish PUFAs.
Partners: Danone Global Research & Innovation Center B.V., Fermentalg, Microalgas Oleas de Mexico, Stichting Wageningen Research, Universiteit Utrecht

Projectbeschrijving: It was recently discovered for some dietary fats that specific gut microbes can transform them into biologically active molecules, benefitting host immunity and metabolic health. This project will explore the potential of fats and oils to act as a modulator of the gut microbiome and its link with human health.
Partners: AAK Netherlands B.V., Academisch Ziekenhuis Groningen, Ausnutria B.V., Bioiberica, Cargill R&D Centre, Fuji Europe Africa B.V., Nederlandse Maag Lever Darm Stichting, Nimble Science, Novozymes Berlin GmbH, Upfield Research and Development B.V.

Projecttitel: Platform for characterisation of cellular system dynamics for tissue disease stageing and programming for repair.CELLSYSTEMICS
Projectbeschrijving: The integrity of biological tissues is actively maintained by cells. Applicable knowledge about how cells do this is of crucial importance to stage tissue disease and to develop preventive treatment. The core challenge is to tackle the complexity of the cell’s system of interrelated mechanisms. This requires a structured identification framework and an efficient integration of measurement technologies. CELLSYSTEMICS will develop these in the clinical context of ascending aortic aneurysm. (1) We will use patient-specific tissue and blood samples to generate robust disease and naive smooth muscle cell lines, as well as tissue matrix. (2) In parallel, we will develop a new platform integrating high-resolution stretch, indentation, and microscopy measurements. The platform will enable a uniquely comprehensive characterisation of cell mechanobiology at the intra-, inter-cell, as well as cell-matrix levels. (3) Our core approach will be to contrast human stemcell-derived naive cells with disease cells, reconstructing a patient’s specific disease history step-by-step. Taken together, CELLSYSTEMICS is excellently positioned to reveal fundamentals of tissue integrity – in patients, without animal involvement.
Partners: BioSPX B.V., Confocal.nl B.V., HCM-Medical B.V., Optics11 B.V., STEMCELL Technologies Canada Inc., Technische Universiteit Eindhoven

Projecttitel: Burgerkennis in de buurt. Ervaringskennis als basis voor een ecologie van gezondheid en participatie
Projectbeschrijving: In Nederland wenden we ons bij lichamelijke en geestelijke problemen tot professionals. Het vermogen van professionals om te helpen bij levensontwrichtende ervaringen is echter beperkt: zorgbehoeften overschrijden ruimschoots professionele middelen. Veel diagnoses werken bovendien beperkend: ze overbenadadrukken symptomen hetgeen medicaliserende effecten heeft en doen geen recht aan bronnen van veerkracht van mensen zelf. Diagnoses werken ook vaak stigmatiserend, genereren schaamte en hinderen participatie in de maatschappij. Veel praktische ervaringskennis van burgers om elkaar te helpen wordt daarentegen te weinig benut. Binnen de geestelijke gezondheidszorg en in sommige medische specialismen spelen ervaringsdeskundigen cq patiëntenkennis wel een rol, maar de ontwikkeling van deze burgerkennis wordt beperkt door institutionele, professionele en burocratische doelen, werkwijzen en grenzen. We gaan buiten de instituties in geheel nieuwe, niet professionele settingen onderzoek doen om op basis van Burgerkennis een aanzet te geven tot een fundamanteel nieuwe paradigma en een nieuwe taal over gezondheid, veerkracht en participatie..Daartoe organiseren we twee laagdrempelige, gastvrije buurtontmoetingsplekken in Maastricht-West waar mensen steun kunnen vinden bij levensvragen en in de omgang met ontwrichtende ervaringen die gezondheid en veerkracht ondermijnen (bijv. verlies, armoede, ziekte, slaapproblemen, mantel-zorgen). Deze ontmoetingsplekken zijn gesitueerd in een drukbezochte kinder- en zorgboerderij en in een winkelcentrum. Op deze plekken bieden ervaringsdeskundigen en buurtvrijwilligers werkvormen aan zoals levensverhaal workshops, herstelwerkgroepen, de mensenbieb, film- en gesprekavonden, maar buurtbewoners kunnen ook zelf werkvormen initieren. Door middel van een overdraagbare ‘strippenkaart’ (fysiek en digitaal) worden nieuwe verbindingen voor steun in de buurten gestimuleerd. Een burgeronderzoeker onderzoekt de impact van deze werkwijzen met behulp van kwalitatieve methoden: analyse van veldwerk (observaties, conversaties), dagboekjes, interviews. De bevindingen worden regelmatige besproken met de ervaringsdeskundigen, vrijwilligers, en consortium partners om tot een gedeelde interpretatie te komen..Deze Burgerkennis impliceert nieuwe empirische voorbeelden van alledaagse ervaringen met gezondheid die leiden tot een fundamenteel nieuwe theorie en nieuwe concepten van/over Gezondheid, Veerkracht en Participatie

Projecttitel: Doorleven ondanks de schaduw van de dood: Participatie in de maatschappij, ervaringen, wensen en behoeften van mensen die nog jarenlang leven met ongeneeslijke kanker.
Projectbeschrijving: Dit projectidee is ontstaan door burgerinitiatieven van auteurs en doorlevers Daniëlle Hermans en Jannie Oskam. Doorlevers zijn mensen met ongeneeslijke kanker, die dankzij nieuwe medische behandelingen, langer leven. Een mooie ontwikkeling die tegelijkertijd grote uitdagingen met zich meebrengt. Vanuit praktijkervaringen van zorgprofessionals en de ervaringsverhalen van doorlevers zelf weten we dat doorlevers op zoek zijn naar hoe ze een balans kunnen vinden tussen doorleven enerzijds en rekening houden met de onvermijdelijke afloop, het overlijden, anderzijds. Leven met grote onzekerheid wordt als lastiger ervaren dan leven met een heldere, doch slechte prognose. Voor de omgeving en voor zorgverleners is deze worsteling soms moeilijk te begrijpen; ja, iemand leeft nog, en dat is geweldig, maar doorleven met een onbetrouwbaar lichaam en grote onzekerheid over het verloop is heel moeilijk en vraagt veel veerkracht. Veel mensen die ongeneeslijk ziek zijn vinden het ook belangrijk om te kunnen blijven participeren in de maatschappij. Hoewel werkgevers en collega’s veel begrip tonen voor de ziekte en het ziekteverlof, lijken patiënten die terug willen keren naar werk niet te voldoen aan de verwachtingen van hun omgeving. Werken en ongeneeslijk ziek zijn worden gezien als tegenstrijdig. Vanuit praktijkervaringen is bekend dat sommige bedrijfsartsen het lastig vinden werknemers te begeleiden, zeker als ze niet zijn ziek gemeld..Dit zijn enkele uitdagingen en taboes, waar doorlevers mee te maken hebben. Omdat het een relatief nieuw fenomeen betreft – immers kanker was decennialang of beter worden, of doodgaan - is vooralsnog onbekend wat de beste ondersteuning is voor mensen die doorleven met ongeneeslijke kanker. Dit project wil de ervaringen, wensen en behoeften van doorlevers inventariseren en uitdiepen, in relatie tot 1) naasten, 2) zorgverleners en 3) werkgevers. Vervolgens willen we de opgedane kennis vertalen naar praktische tools om doorlevers beter te kunnen ondersteunen.

Projecttitel: DIGNIC: DIGITAL PERSONALIZED AFTERCARE FOLLOWING AN ADMISSION IN THE INTENSIVE CARE UNIT
