Projecttitel: AI-based kunstinterventies ten behoeve van nabuurschap voor mensen met dementie
Projectbeschrijving: Sociale contacten en ontmoetingen in de buurt zijn van belang voor de mensen die er wonen. Het stimuleert ook de samenredzaamheid van buurtbewoners en in het bijzonder mensen met beginnende dementie. Artificial intelligence kunstwerken zijn rijk aan interactie en bevorderen sociaal contact, maar in de praktijk ontstaan vaak veel dilemma's waar democratische participatie op het spel staat. Het project ‘It takes a village to grow old’ benadrukt het belang om samen met  de burgers te werken aan een dementievriendelijke buurt. Het  doel  is om samen met de Vondel/Helmersbuurt in Amsterdam onderzoek te doen naar AI-kunstobjecten in de openbare ruimte om ontmoetingen tussen mensen (met en zonder dementie) in de wijk te stimuleren. Het project speelt in op de behoefte van mensen met dementie om thuis te blijven wonen in de wijk waar ze zich prettig en veilig voelen. Ook de evaluatie wordt gezamenlijk uitgevoerd waarbij gekeken wordt naar wat het effect van de AI-kunstinterventies op de sociale interactie in de wijk is. In het project wordt zodoende zowel de ervaringskennis van burgers (met dementie) als de professionele kennis (zorg en welzijn, AI en kunst), en de academische kennis (burgerparticipatie, AI en slimme woonomgeving) gebruikt voor het inrichten van ontmoetingsplekken in deze buurt. In het project willen we in de praktijk leren hoe participatiewerken aan een dementievriendelijke buurt vorm krijgt tussen alle deelnemers. Uitgangspunt is dat dit proces op zich al meerwaarde heeft voor interactie in de wijk. Het project verkent daarmee de dynamiek tussen AI-kunstinterventies, place-making en sociale gezondheid uitgaande van de citizens science benadering. Het onderzoek leidt tot: 1) (ontwerp)principes voor sociale interactie tussen buurtbewoners (met dementie), 2) inzicht in socio-spatio-techno factoren van AI-kunstinterventies, 3) strategieën om samen met burgers de openbare ruimte in te richten zodat publieke familiariteit en ervaren nabuurschap bevorderd wordt en 4) waarden inclusief de ethiek van het participatief ontwerpen.

Projecttitel: De Kwekerij: een Leidse proeftuin voor een nieuwe aanpak van diabetes type 2 door burgers via leefstijl en peercoaching
Projectbeschrijving: Stichting Je Leefstijl Als Medicijn is een burgerinitiatief met een online community van mensen met diabetes type 2 die elkaar ondersteunen bij een gezonde leefstijl. Hier bundelen zij hun kracht met Stichting Vitality club, een burgerinitiatief van mensen door het hele land die met behulp van peercoaching samen bewegen. In het project ‘de Kwekerij’ zullen burgers elkaar ondersteunen om met een gezonde leefstijl meer grip te krijgen op hun diabetes. In WP 1 zal Leyden Academy de interventie ontwikkelen in co-creatie met burgers. Patiënten zullen leren wat het effect is van voeding en leefstijl op hun bloedsuikers en andere parameters. In WP 2 levert Quli de PGO waarmee mensen grip krijgen op hun data en dit veilig kunnen delen en wordt een portal ontwikkeld dat toegang biedt tot belangrijke wetenschappelijk onderbouwde informatie over leefstijl. In WP 3 zal het LUMC patiënten naar de kwekerij verwijzen en samen met burgers het effect onderzoeken. Uiteindelijk ontstaat een bewezen effectief zelforganiserend burgerinitiatief dat mensen met diabetes coacht in gezonde leefstijl.

Projecttitel: Emovere uit SOLK: een nieuwe weg van herstel door ervaringsdeskundigen en professionals
Projectbeschrijving: Somatisch Onvoldoende verklaarde Lichamelijke Klachten (SOLK) zijn een omvangrijk gezondheidsprobleem in Nederland. Er zijn meer dan twee miljoen mensen met chronische pijn en 40% van alle consulten bij huisartsen betreft SOLK. SOLK brengt hoge zorgkosten met zich mee, in 2019 ruim 3,8 miljard euro, en een lagere kwaliteit van leven. ..Ervaringsdeskundigen geven aan dat een nieuw perspectief op de aanpak van SOLK nodig is om mensen te helpen met herstel. Het gaat om een brede visie op ziekte en (positieve) gezondheid, waarin lichaam en geest onlosmakelijk met elkaar verbonden zijn. Dit met specifieke aandacht voor de rol van het gevoel en (onbewust) verdrongen emoties op het ontstaan en in stand houden van SOLK. Voor de nog nader te definiëren groepen mensen met SOLK worden interventies (door)ontwikkeld, zoals een eHealth zelfhulp programma en een recent gepilote groepsinterventie met groeps- en individuele elementen. De groepsinterventie kan door ervaringsdeskundigen en zorgprofessionals worden uitgevoerd vanuit de huisartsenpraktijk, of elders in de wijk. Met behulp van design thinking zal een bijscholing gemaakt worden voor zorgprofessionals over de mind-body connectie, het andere gesprek, en hun veranderende rol. Om bewustwording te creëren over deze andere aanpak zullen wijkgerichte activiteiten worden ontworpen, die ook worden benut om mensen uit te nodigen deel te nemen aan de interventies in het onderzoek. ..Ervaringsdeskundigen in deze innovatieve aanpak werken in dit project samen met SOLK-patiënten, hun omgeving, zorgprofessionals, ondernemers en onderzoekers, en zullen een leidende rol hebben in alle werkpakketten, als essentieel onderdeel van citizen science. De in co-creatie ontwikkelde interventies zullen onderzocht en geëvalueerd worden op basis van quadruple aim aspecten. Integratie van deze visie/aanpak van SOLK in de Nederlandse gezondheidszorg en maatschappij biedt veel kansen voor herstel, eigen zorg, een hogere kwaliteit van leven en besparingen op de hoge zorg- en maatschappelijke (uitvals)kosten. Daarnaast draagt het bij aan preventie en een duurzamere oplossing: SOLK kan namelijk voor een belangrijk deel voorkomen worden wanneer kinderen en volwassenen leren dat het (h)erkennen en uiten van emoties en kijken naar klachten als signaal van het lichaam de basis vormen van de eigen regie op gezondheid.
Partners: Huisartsenpraktijk Energiekwartier B.V., GEEN RECHTSPERSOON, Menzis Zorgverzekeraar N.V., Onderlinge Waarborgmaatschappij CZ groep U.A., Stichting Emovere, Stichting Lijn 1, Stichting Sardes, Therapieland B.V.

Projectbeschrijving: Ondanks de toenemende aandacht voor preventie leeft een grote groep Nederlanders.ongezond en nemen de gezondheidsverschillen tussen theoretisch en praktisch.opgeleiden toe. Gerichte en passende preventieve interventies zijn nodig om meer.mensen gezond te laten leven en verschillen tussen groepen te verkleinen. Op dit.moment geven financiers van preventie meestal de voorkeur aan het inzetten van.erkende leefstijlinterventies. Die zijn wetenschappelijk onderbouwd, hun effectiviteit.wordt bij deelnemers strak gemeten en de meerwaarde wordt in kaart gebracht. In de.praktijk blijft de effectiviteit vaak achter bij de verwachtingen. Naast deze erkende.interventies bestaan er heel veel informele leefstijlactiviteiten, vaak georganiseerd door.actieve bewoners, ervaringsdeskundigen, lotgenoten, sportclubs, buurthuizen,.welzijnsorganisaties en zzp-ers. Deze activiteiten hebben veel waarde, maar zijn vaak.onzichtbaar en blijven onder de radar..Het project onder de werktitel ‘GezondMeNu.nl’ wil hier verandering in brengen door een.online én real life open platform/online community te zijn waarin zichtbaar wordt wat de.burgerinitiatieven zijn en wat de ervaringen zijn met informele leefstijlactiviteiten voor.meer gezondheid door en voor (georganiseerde) bewoners, samen met of ondersteund.door professionals in een wijk, buurt of dorp of in een gemeenschap..De GezondMeNu-gemeenschap bouwt niet alleen aan direct beschikbare en bruikbare.kennis voor en met burgers en professionals over leefstijlactiviteiten, ze kijkt ook in die.gemeenschap naar ‘wat werkt’ in de overstijgende realiteit van het dagelijkse leven..Samen met onze partners ontwikkelen we een waarderingsmodel om informele en.laagdrempelige leefstijlactiviteiten op een gevalideerde manier te beoordelen die inzicht.verschaft over wat werkt, voor wie en in welke setting. Voor financiers van informele.leefstijlinitiatieven kan deelname aan GezondMeNu.nl wellicht een simpele (nietbureaucratische.en niet dure) randvoorwaarde worden om een subsidie gegund te.krijgen. Ook komen via GezondMeNu gegenereerde data beschikbaar die relevant zijn.voor diverse onderzoeksgroepen en onderzoekers, inclusief burgeronderzoekers zelf.

Projecttitel: Een sensitieve virtuele-assistent voor kwetsbare zorgvragers
Projectbeschrijving: Voor burgers in kwetsbare posities – zoals mensen met autisme, licht verstandelijke beperking (LVB), niet-aangeboren hersenletsel en/of GGZ-problematiek – is het om emotionele, cognitieve en infrastructurele redenen uitdagend om met specifieke zorgvragen bij de juiste instantie terecht te komen. Deze zorgvragers worden vaak (te) laat of niet geholpen, wat zwaardere zorg of verzwaring van de problematiek oplevert...Er is behoefte aan effectieve tools die deze zorgvragers kunnen ondersteunen in de vragen die ze hebben, waarbij tegelijkertijd rekening wordt gehouden met de drie uitdagingen die ten grondslag liggen aan de complexiteit van de situatie. Ervaringsdeskundigen gelieerd aan ErvaarMEE en initiatiefnemers van dit project verwachten dat een virtuele-assistent die aansluit bij de leefwereld van kwetsbare zorgvragers deze uitdagingen kan verminderen, daarmee hun empowerment verhoogt, en bijdraagt aan een effectievere hulpverlening; wat uiteindelijk gezondheidsverschillen kan verkleinen. . .In dit project wordt op basis van fundamenteel en industrieel onderzoek een sensitieve virtuele-assistent met unieke AI-technologie ontwikkeld die past bij de leefwereld van deze zorgvragers, te beginnen in de kwetsbare context van zorg- en welzijnsproblematiek. Met sensitief wordt bedoeld dat de virtuele-assistent kan aanvoelen wat de gewenste ervaringen en belangen zijn van de zorgvragers. Deze virtuele-assistent kan zorgvragers in een kwetsbare positie wijzen op passende ondersteuning voor sociale vragen op het gebied van (mentale en fysieke) gezondheid. ..In het project staat de doelgroep aan het roer als burgerwetenschapper, is gelijkwaardige partner en co-creator en tevens adviseur in een klankbordgroep. Daarmee kan bovendien bewijsvoering worden geleverd dat burgerwetenschappers waardevol en noodzakelijk zijn in technologische ontwikkel- en implementatie-onderzoeken om aan te kunnen sluiten bij de praktijk, zodat ‘citizen science’ breder toegepast kan worden. Naast de ervaringsdeskundigen en (co-)onderzoekers als burgerwetenschappers zijn in dit project welzijnsorganisatie MEE Gelderse Poort (MEE), AI-ontwikkelaar Mobile Water (MW), projectpartner Reframing Studio (RS) en kennisinstellingen Tilburg University (TiU) en Radboudumc (Rumc) betrokken.
Partners: Mobile Water B.V., Radboud universit. medisch centrum/Radboudumc, Stichting MEE Plus

Projecttitel: Van Vrouwen voor Vrouwen: deel je gezondheid met je eigen vaginale bacteriën.
Projectbeschrijving: De dominante aanwezigheid van vaginale Lactobacillus crispatus-bacteriën is geassocieerd met goede reproductieve en seksuele gezondheid, waaronder minder risico op vroeggeboorte, postmenopauzale klachten, urineweginfecties en vaginale infecties. Recent is duidelijk geworden dat deze crispatus-bacteriën vanuit een product goed en langdurig de vagina kunnen koloniseren en daar kunnen helpen om infecties te voorkomen. Deze nieuwe producten worden echter ontwikkeld in een geneesmiddeltraject met farmacologische formuleringen, met weinig oog voor de doelgroep. Het ontbreekt aan gebruikscomfort, aan toegankelijkheid voor het grote publiek en aan de diversiteit van verschillende crispatus-stammen die voorkomen in de vaginale ecologie. Daarnaast ontbreekt veel fundamentele kennis over de kolonisatie van verschillende crispatus-stammen en hoe de microbiële context van de gastvrouw deze kolonisatie beinvloedt...In dit project willen we als vrouwenonderzoekscollectief onder de vlag van Stichting crispatus onze eigen vaginale crispatus-bacterien isoleren om daarmee andere vrouwen te helpen urineweginfecties en bacteriële vaginose te voorkomen. Hiervoor vormen wij een consortium met onze partners: onderzoekers van de Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, de femcare-specialisten van Yoni, de genetische expertise van BaseClear en de probiotica-specialisten bij Winclove- We ontwikkelen een over-the-counter toegankelijk vrouwvriendelijk product met een grote diversiteit aan crispatus-isolaten. Bij dit product zijn de donateurs tevens burgerwetenschapper, productwikkelaar en mede-eigenaar van het eindproduct. Gedurende het traject vullen we kennishiaten in over de eigenschappen van efficiënt en duurzaam koloniserende stammen: verschilt kolonisatie per vrouw? Per type microbioom? Of per stam? ..Het voorgestelde project kent drie werkpakketten:.1) Het crowdsourcing practicum waarin de werkgroepen binnen het vrouwenonderzoekscollectief ingericht worden, we onderzoek doen naar ons eigen vaginaal microbioom en crispatus-bacteriën isoleren en karakteriseren. .2) Tijdens de ‘hackathon’ ontwerpen, ontwikkelen en produceren we twee verschillende prototypes met crispatus-bacteriën..3) In de derde fase doen we onderzoek naar veiligheid van het product en kolonisatie van de verschillende stammen in een diverse groep vrouwen met variërend microbioom...Dit project is zowel technisch als sociaal innovatief omdat hier burgerwetenschap een concreet product oplevert, waarbij de burgers mede-eigenaar blijven.

Projecttitel: VRbeelding: beeld van een goed leven met dementie via VR-brillen
Projectbeschrijving: Achtergrond.Voorjaar ‘21 vertelden ouderen aan onderzoekers van het VRbeelding-consortium dat veel mensen bang zijn om dementie te krijgen, uit angst voor een slechte kwaliteit van leven. Dit angstbeeld beïnvloedt ook de bejegening van en zorg voor een persoon met dementie. Hoewel negatieve associaties met dementie goed te begrijpen zijn, is het volgens het VRbeelding-consortium belangrijk om te laten zien dat het ook mogelijk is om een goed leven te leiden mét dementie. In tegenstelling tot veel eerdere studies, kijkt het VRbeelding-consortium niet alleen naar beïnvloedende factoren voor angst, maar juist naar beelden van een goed leven met dementie die angst kunnen afzwakken of ontkrachten...Doel.In het VRbeelding-project willen ouderen en professionals die in het dagelijks leven in aanraking komen met dementie onderzoeken welke angstbeelden over leven met dementie heersen onder burgers, en welke beelden burgers en ervaringsdeskundigen daar tegenover kunnen zetten om zo bij te dragen aan bewustwording over de mogelijkheden om met dementie een goed leven te leiden. ..Aanpak.Creatieve onderzoeksmethoden worden ingezet om beelden over leven met dementie op te halen onder grote groepen burgers, bijvoorbeeld photo-voice. Mensen met dementie, mantelzorgers en zorgprofessionals reflecteren op die beelden..Het inzicht in angst en de tegenbeelden hiervan gebruikt het consortium om (wetenschappelijke) publicaties te schrijven en daarnaast om een interventie met een dementie-ervaring via Virtual Reality-technologie (Dementiebril) en training te ontwikkelen. Met de interventie willen we angstbeelden verminderen en perspectieven en handelingsopties voor mantelzorgers en professionals voor een goed leven met dementie vergroten. ..Verwachte impact.Het VRbeelding-project sluit aan bij de missie van de overheid om mensen met dementie en hun naasten meer kwaliteit van leven te bieden door hen als waardevol lid van de samenleving mee te laten doen, zonder vooroordelen of stigma, en hen passende zorg en ondersteuning te bieden.
Partners: Alzheimer Nederland, Beleef Dementie B.V., Denktank 60+ Noord, Stichting Fontys, Stichting Netwerk Dementie Drenthe, Stichting Pelita

Projecttitel: The COPD exacerbation as a therapeutic window for lung repair
Projectbeschrijving: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is one of the most common lung diseases worldwide, characterized by an accelerated loss of lung function. A key problem underlying COPD is increased tissue destruction in combination with defective lung tissue repair. As current therapies do not modify the progression of the disease, new therapies aimed at restoring lung tissue repair in COPD need to be developed. ..The exacerbation period may offer an opportunity to overcome this problem. Lung function decline in COPD is highest in the period during and immediately following an exacerbation. Furthermore, the exacerbation appears to be a period characterized by both concentrated disease burden and oxidative stress, which impairs the endogenous repair response of the adult lung epithelium. Therefore, we hypothesize that the COPD exacerbation represents a therapeutic window for lung repair and that targeting this exacerbation period may resolve the deficit. ..As we currently lack suitable human disease modeling technology to model the impact of COPD exacerbations on lung repair in vitro, our aim is to establish such a model using organoid technology. Furthermore, we have recently identified novel drug targets (PGE2, PGI2) for lung repair, which we aim to evaluate for their suitability in targeting the exacerbation using this project. ..Specifically, we aim to:.a) To characterize which therapeutic window of the exacerbation and post-exacerbation repair is most sensitive to PGE1 and PGI2. With this knowledge, we will be able to target specific treatment windows and to identify new drug targets for lung repair.  .b) to develop in vitro organoid-based methods to assess the pharmacology associated with COPD exacerbations and defective lung repair.

Projecttitel: Development of a non-invasive gene therapy for multiple sclerosis
Projectbeschrijving: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an inflammatory demyelinating disease that affects 2.8 million people worldwide. Demyelination is accompanied by axon damage and disrupts the ability of nerve cells to transmit signals, resulting in physical and mental problems. Disease-modifying anti-inflammatory therapies counteract inflammation in relapsing-remitting MS. Although these immune-modifying treatments are important for reducing the relapse frequency, these drugs are of limited benefit for MS patients with a central nervous system (CNS) that is damaged due to the inflammatory process. ..The objective of this Health-Holland project is to develop a non-invasive restorative gene therapy for MS. Studies on MS-brain tissue from the Netherlands Brain Bank have resulted in the identification of two molecular targets (CD200 and osteopontin) that may potentially stop the progression of MS by preventing inflammation-induced tissue damage and promoting myelin repair. A novel non-invasive gene therapy approach, based on a new generation of adeno-associated viral vectors (AAV) that can pass the blood-brain-barrier, will be employed to deliver these targets directly to the CNS in an animal model for MS. The beneficial effects of CD200 and osteopontin gene therapy will be investigated by a battery of functional test and by histological analysis of myelin and axon regeneration in brain and spinal cord tissue. This project is an important first step towards developing a non-invasive restorative treatment for MS. ..This project lays the groundwork for a treatment for MS which is radically different from other treatment approaches that are currently used for MS in daily clinical practice. The development of a restorative treatment would have a tremendous positive impact on the quality of life of patients with progressive, chronic MS and would result in significant medical and socio-economic benefits.

Projecttitel: An implant-based sternal fixation system to facilitate handsfree speech in laryngectomized patients
Projectbeschrijving: Our goal is to enable hands-free speech for patients who have had their voice box removed due to cancer (laryngectomy). To achieve this, we have joined with Health-Holland, who have enabled us to perform research into the topic. After laryngectomy, patients breathe through an opening in the front of the neck, or tracheostoma. To enable this, an automatic stoma valve (ASV) and adhesive base plate (figure 1) are commonly used. The ASV closes automatically when people speak, so that air travels not from the lungs through the opening in the neck, but to the mouth through a puncture between the esophagus and windpipe. The ASV closes when patients ‘raise their voice’ and create a certain amount of air pressure
Aanvrager: Stichting Het Nederlands Kanker Instituut-Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Ziekenhuis

Projecttitel: Alternative strategies to block AT1R mediated signaling in Marfan Syndrome
Projectbeschrijving: Background .Prognosis in patients with Marfan Syndrome(MS) depends highly on aortic aneurysm formation with subsequently aortic dissection and to a lesser extend on mitral valve degeneration(MVD). .In MS mouse models, pharmacotherapy with an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) results in total prevention of aneurysm formation. In human studies, ARB slower aneurysm formation but do not prevent formation or dissection. .The majority of angiotensin II effects are mediated by the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R). Further downstream signaling is mediated by G-proteins, which increase e.g.  vasoconstriction, whereas other effects result from ß-arrestin recruitment which e.g. activates anti-apoptotic signals. It was also found that AT1R interacts with the monocyte chemoattractant protein-1(MCP-1) receptor resulting in the activation of inflammatory cascades...In order to better understand the role of ARBs in MS, we will study the effect of ß-arrestin mediated AT1R signaling (with ß-arrestin stimulation and inhibition) and the interaction with the MCP-1 Receptor(i.e. CCR2) in a MS mouse model and evaluate these effects in human arteries. ..Objective .To study the aspect of AT1R signaling on aneurysm development and MVD in a MS mouse and compare with signaling in human coronaries...Design .We will study selective ß-arrestin stimulation, selective ß-arrestin inhibition and combined AT1R and CCR2 inhibition in MS mouse model that develops non-lethal aneurysms and compare to wild type. We will perform echocardiography at 4, 8, 12 and 14-16 weeks, perform histology and measure mediators and proteins involved in further signaling of AT1R. Secondly, we will compare the effect of these drugs in human coronaries focusing on signaling and vasoreactivity.  ..Anticipated Social and Economic Impact.A better understanding of the downstream signaling in the AT1R, more specifically the role of ß-arrestin or AT1R-CCR2 interaction in MS will lead to better pharmacotherapeutical strategies in the treatment of MS and other connective tissue diseases.
Partners: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC), Radboud universit. medisch centrum/Radboudumc, Trevena Inc

Projecttitel: Reactivation of the latent reservoir and Removal of the provirus by HIV-specific gene therapy delivered by anti-gp160 lipid nanoparticles.
Projectbeschrijving: The latent HIV reservoir is the major hurdle to HIV cure. Latently infected cells can reactivate to produce infectious virus and in absence of antiretroviral therapy cause a rebound in viremia and reseed the viral reservoir. New insights into the viral reservoir demonstrated that the majority of clonally expanded cells can be activated to produce virus but can also revert to latency without being cleared by viral cytopathic effect or the host immune response. Our objective is therefore to reactivate HIV in these latently infected cells followed by HIV-specific targeting of lipid nanoparticles (LNP) carrying HIV-specific gene-editing tools which should enable clearance of the inducible viral reservoir..First of all, we will investigate if we can use small heavy chain only (VHH) antibodies directed against the viral envelope (HIV-gp160) to target the LNP to HIV-expressing cells. Since these VHH are only 1/10th the size of conventional antibodies we anticipate an increased targeting efficiency as compared to conventional antibodies. Next, we will assess the efficacy and specificity of two different gene-editing tools (CRISPR/Cas9 and BREC1) in the modification and/or excision of the proviral reservoir. These gene-editing tools will be delivered using the earlier developed HIV-specific LNP and will be assessed in HIV-reactivated cell lines. Finally, the most efficient and specific approach will be tested in reactivated CD4+ T cells derived from people with HIV on antiretroviral treatment..Taken together, we will REACTIVATE the latent viral reservoir and specifically deliver LNP containing HIV-directed gene-editing tools to these reactivated cells. Translation of the gene-editing tools will subsequently result in the specific REMOVAL of the inducible viral reservoir(Figure 1). Insights into the role of VHH in targeting specific cell populations in combination with gene-editing tools will not only guide HIV cure studies but will also be important for the development of nanomedicine in general.
Partners: QVQ Holding B.V., Single Cell Discoveries B.V.

Projecttitel: MetaFish: Identification of therapeutic targets for rare metabolic disorders in zebrafish
Projectbeschrijving: Inherited metabolic disorders are chronic and often lead to disabilies preventing the patient to engage in socioeconomic activities. When looked at individually, inherited metabolic disorders are rare, but combined they have an estimated occurence of 1 in every 500 newborns, making them one of the main causes of child death. Unfortunately, there are only very few inherited metabolic disorders for which an effective treatment exists. There is therefore a compelling need for the development of new therapies and the identification of therapeutic targets. The aim of this project is to develop new animal models to study inherited metabolic disorders and to use this models to identify new therapeutic targets in collaboration with our industrial partner. To achieve this we will use the zebrafish as it is amenable to genetic modifications, its embryos are transparent -allowing live microscopy imaging- and it’s physiology is conserved with human physiology. In this project, zebrafish models will be developed for a subset of inherited metabolic disorders that involve altered lipid metabolism that strongly affect the skeletal and heart muscles. These new models will be used to study the pathophysiology of these diseases and to identify the disease mechanisms that are responsible for the impaired muscle function. Furthermore, the zebrafish disease models developed in this project will be used to validate genetic disease modifiers that will be identified by our industrial partner for their effects on the progression of the disease-related phenotypes. Eventually, this work may lead to the identification and validation of potential new targets for drug development to treat inherited metabolic diseases in the near future.

Projecttitel: MEFORM; MEdia FOR Massive iPSC culture - Development of a cost-effective large-scale culturing platform to derive hematopoietic cells from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs).
Projectbeschrijving: In 2007, the seminal finding of Yamanaka et al. that human somatic cells can be reprogrammed to a pluripotent stem cell state comparable to bona fide, blastocyst-derived embryonic stem cells has defined a completely new field of research. The enormous potential of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) to differentiate into any human cell types has severely boosted the prospect of regenerative medicine using transfusable/transplantable cells derived from iPSCs 1. For instance, NK or T cells harboring chimeric antigen receptors, red blood cells carrying specific therapeutic cargo or retinal transplants are few of many examples. We established turbulent bioreactor conditions and protocols to produce hematopoietic cells from iPSC. However, large scale production of hematopoietic cells currently depends on costly media that are non-chemically defined with unknown consumption kinetics, and with unknown effects on iPSC culture metabolism..TKI-LSH (Match) PPP Allowance application form 2022.5.These severely curtail media optimization to control conditions at large volumes and translation to GMP grade closed bioreactor systems..In this project we specifically aim to formulate media and to understand media-component consumption to allow hematopoietic effector cell production from iPSC during the first initiation of iPSC to hematopoietic cells. We will validate the obtained media in scalable, GMP-compatible culture conditions, that are the most optimal for each iPSC differentiation phase and ultimately can give rise to sufficient numbers of hematopoietic effector cells. Characterization of medium consumption and composition through metabolic analysis of iPSC cultures during differentiation is a crucial step towards a cost-effective production of cellular products. The result of this project will pave the way towards production of advanced therapeutic medicinal products (ATMPs) from iPSC. Cost-effective production of ATMPs will lead to lower health care costs while providing novel treatments to a range of diseases. The derived media will also largely serve the iPSC community with currently absent optimal suspension differentiation media.

Projecttitel: Artificial intelligence for protein stabilization in vaccine design
Projectbeschrijving: The emergence of novel viral infections of zoonotic origin and mutations of existing human pathogenic viruses represent a serious concern for public health and in case of the COVID-19 pandemic even a threat to stability of societies and economies. The likelihood of such threats may likely increase due to climate change and growing world population. The most cost-effective and long-term solution for fighting infectious disease is the development of vaccines. Improving the process to develop efficacious vaccine is of high importance. Immunogens most often used in viral vaccines are the surface glycoproteins that catalyze fusion of the virus with the host cell since these are the targets of potent neutralizing antibodies. Viral fusion proteins are highly energetic meta-stable fusion machines that, upon triggering, refold to their low-energy post-fusion state. Therefore, in order to obtain a fusion protein as a component in an efficacious vaccine, the metastable structure needs to be maintained in its prefusion conformation by introduction of stabilizing mutations that prevent refolding. This approach of structure-based design has been used by us and others as a successful approach in vaccine research. .Artificial Intelligence (AI) has recently been used to solve many problems in structural biology, with the most famous example of DeepMind’s AlphaFold for protein structure prediction. Here, we will develop new AI technology for improving the process of fusion protein engineering. The goal of the project is to develop highly accurate deep learning models, that will detect destabilizing regions in proteins and suggest mutations to fix them. The ability of these new AI models to improve protein stability will be tested experimentally on selected fusion proteins, to guide the development of improved next generation models. Eventually, global protein structure-based models will be designed to predict experimental protein stability and guide future vaccine design.

Projecttitel: RSV Entry Pathway in Human Ciliated Airway Cells
Projectbeschrijving: The number of candidate vaccines for viral respiratory diseases that make it from the discovery phase to clinical testing and final market authorization is very limited. One of the reasons for this is the disconnect between preclinical animal and in vitro models on the one hand, and the actual human situation on the other. For example, the majority of the neutralization assays to test vaccine efficacy are based upon immortalized cell lines that have little in common with primary human epithelium. .A clinically important virus for which no vaccine has yet been licensed is Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), afflicting especially the very young, and the elderly. Janssen discovered that besides RSV fusion protein F, the attachment protein G can act as a neutralizing vaccine target. However, G-based neutralization can only be measured in differentiated human airway cultures rich in ciliated cells.. In ciliated cells, RSV apparently follows a distinct attachment and entry pathway. Building on breakthroughs of LUMC, LUMC and Janssen would like to develop a cell line that recapitulates native RSV attachment and entry. Using a variety of techniques, we will identify novel RSV entry factors in primary Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells (hPBECs). These factors, as well as previously suggested host factors, will be validated in hPBECs and also transferred to a non-permissive cell line developed by Janssen. Neutralization assays using this cell line will accurately mimic the in vivo respiratory infection and can provide a ‘correlate of protection’ contributing to the predictive outcome of human clinical trials and a decrease in the use of animal models. .In parallel we aim to improve upon the throughput of existing hPBEC–based systems by miniaturizing the system  making it compatible with automation. .Finally, the accumulated knowledge can serve as a paradigm for respiratory vaccine development in general.

Projecttitel: A Computational model to understand the Physiology, Etiology and Biological Behavior of Type II Endoleaks
Projectbeschrijving: Type II endoleaks are a persistent problem after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) with a prevalence of 15-25%. They are characterized by the reversal of blood into the aneurysmal sac from side branches and growth of the aneurysm thereof. The occurrence of type II endoleaks is thus related to unfavorable sac dynamics, that in turn is associated with reinterventions and long-term survival. Even after over 25 years of experience, type II endoleaks remain the Achilles heel of the technique. Prediction models of type II endoleaks occurrence/behavior are a clinical unmet need with regard to identifying patients at risk for development of a persistent type II endoleak, to predicting the association with unfavorable sac dynamics and to identify the optimal treatment algorithm. The reasons for the occurrence of type II endoleaks in some patients is an open question fundamentally..We will leverage fully resolved direct numerical simulation of flow on large supercomputers, combined with a model for wall movement as well as thrombosis to study the risk of type II endoleaks, based on patient data. We will conduct detailed simulations on supercomputers using the APES simulation framework (https://apes.osdn.io) to quantify intrinsic flow dynamics, and arrive at a fundamental understanding about endoleaks. This will lead to improvement in clinical practice in the management of patients, reduction in follow-up costs, reduced burden on the health costs in Netherlands..Research questions:.1. Why do type II endoleaks happen in some patients while not in others after the EVAR procedure?.2. Can we predict their persistence in time?.3. A type II endoleak can be related to a shrinking, a stable or a growing abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Can we predict sac remodeling with computational methods?.4. In case of a reintervention, can the primary target vessel(s) be identified to optimize the treatment success rate?
Partners: Medtronic Bakken Research Center B.V., Stichting Rijnstate Ziekenhuis

Projecttitel: Towards detecting early warning signs of dementia in the at-home setting: Feasibility and usability of remote digital passive monitoring of cognition in cognitively healthy elderly
Projectbeschrijving: Worldwide, 40 million patients suffer from dementia, with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) as its most common cause. Dementia has a high socioeconomic burden with exponentially increasing healthcare costs. Many healthy elderly worrying about potential first symptoms of dementia such as forgetfulness. At-home monitoring of cognitive performance could enable the detection of such early warning signs, thereby providing accessible care to the worried elderly...One at-home monitoring tool that shows promise is unobtrusive data collection through ‘passive monitoring’ via smartphone interactions. Smartphones are intensively used among elderly, and smartphone-derived data, such as keystroke-logging offer the possibility to measure participants throughout the day. This data set can be used to explore at-risk signatures of dementia...Our aim is to explore the feasibility and usability of a passive patient monitoring tool, Neurokeys, in cognitively healthy elderly (50+) as a proof-of-concept for at-home monitoring of cognition. Our objectives are to:.1.	Identify facilitators and barriers that cognitively healthy elderly might have regarding the use of passive monitoring..2.	Investigate the impact of potential confounders on the usage of and data collected by a passive monitoring tool..3.	Investigate the stability of passive monitoring in cognitively healthy elderly over 26 weeks. ..Using a mixed-methods design, we address the first aim by performing a qualitative study to identify potential barriers and facilitators towards passive monitoring in focus groups with cognitively healthy elderly (N=10, WP1). Next, we will relate smartphone-derived metrics with age, sex, and education using Neurokeys (N=300, WP2). Finally, we will investigate the stability of smartphone-derived metrics by assessing its reliability over time in participants enrolled in WP2 (WP3)...Passive monitoring is more cost-efficient than regular visits to a memory clinic, and therefore has potential economic impact. This research is a first step towards the screening of cognitive decline...Additive note: This project aligns with the ‘A Personalized Medicine Approach for Alzheimer’s Disease’ (ABOARD) project, in which passive monitoring is investigated in AD patients. The current project takes the necessary next step, which is the exploration of passive monitoring in cognitively healthy elderly. This link with the ABOARD project allows us to make use of the infrastructure of ABOARD, e.g., for patient recruitment.

Projecttitel: Clinical applicability of ctDNA testing for treatment response monitoring of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer
Projectbeschrijving: Background:.Monitoring of treatment response in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is currently performed by computed tomography (CT) imaging, which assesses changes in tumor size to determine whether response is complete, partial, stable or progressive. Detection of cell-free circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in liquid biopsies is indicative of abundance of viable neoplastic cells and may offer an alternative approach to monitor treatment response. Putative advantages of ctDNA-testing compared to CT-imaging include:.- Improved treatment decision-making, because:.o ctDNA-testing reflects viable tumor load..o More objective and standardized measurements..- Organization of patient care close to home instead of stressful hospital visits..DELFI’s ctDNA technology may offer a sensitive, affordable and broadly applicable ctDNA-test for treatment response monitoring..Objectives:.1. Evaluate treatment response monitoring by longitudinal ctDNA-measurements in comparison to CT-imaging and in relation to clinical outcome..2. Develop and apply a Delfi Monitoring Score (DMS) ctDNA-test for treatment response monitoring..3. Determine the optimal strategy to complement and/or partly replace CT-imaging with ctDNA-testing for treatment response monitoring..Plan of Investigation:.Perform a prospective multicenter observational study: accrue 400 mCRC patients who receive systemic treatment, using the Prospective Dutch ColoRectal Cancer cohort (www.PLCRC.nl) infrastructure. Blood samples are collected longitudinally in conjunction with regularly scheduled CT-scans every two months. Plasma cell-free DNA will be analyzed for tumor-specific fragmentation patterns (DELFI Diagnostics). ddPCR ctDNA-testing of hotspot mutations will be performed as reference. Clinical, imaging and molecular data will be used for modeling longitudinal ctDNA-testing and CT-imaging to identify an optimal treatment response monitoring strategy..Expected outcome:.This study will reveal the added clinical value of ctDNA-testing in treatment response monitoring of mCRC patients. It has potential to improve decision-making and propose strategies to further personalize treatment and safely replace part of CT-scans. This will result in better clinical outcome and transfer of disease monitoring to the extra-mural setting.
Aanvrager: Stichting Het Nederlands Kanker Instituut-Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Ziekenhuis
Partners: Delfi Diagnostics Inc., Stichting Amsterdam UMC, Universitair Medisch Centrum Utrecht

Projecttitel: Remotely controlled T cell therapies for cancer.
Projectbeschrijving: Adoptive T cell therapies have shown substantial activity in a number of human malignancies. Specifically, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has shown profound clinical activity in hematological malignancies, leading to a number of drug approvals.  Furthermore, in melanoma, the clinical activity of tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) has been well established. However, the impact of T cell receptor (TCR)-T cell, CAR-T cell and TIL therapy in other solid malignancies is thus far modest..The central thesis of this project is that next generation adoptive T cell therapies should not merely involve the infusion of tumor-reactive T cells, but that such T cell products should be endowed with the capacity to induce intratumoral inflammation in a precisely controlled manner to thereby increase anti-tumor activity. Specifically, a broad array of preclinical and clinical data provides compelling evidence that the local production of potent cytokines such as IL-12 can drive tumor control. However, systemic administration of these cytokines is precluded by severe toxicities. We aim to leverage the remote cell control technology that we have developed to engineer cell therapies that secrete potent payloads such as IL-12 in the tumor microenvironment (TME), in a strictly antigen-dependent and small molecule-controlled manner. Through this approach, we aim to precisely regulate the level of local inflammation, while preventing the potentially severe side effects associated with systemic inflammation. Key deliverable of this project will be the establishment of the feasibility of regulating intra-tumoral IL-12 production, and its effect on tumor control in in vitro and in vivo models. In view of the broad potential applicability of the technology, we will evaluate and compare potential of the technology in CAR-T, TCR-T and TIL. Results of this study will have wide-ranging implications for the treatment of solid tumors and will be followed by investigational new drug (IND)-enabling studies.
Aanvrager: Stichting Het Nederlands Kanker Instituut-Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Ziekenhuis

Projecttitel: Stimulating a healthy gut microbiome by using specific prebiotics generated by fungal enzymes
Projectbeschrijving: Diet is an important factor in our health and can both cause and prevent diseases. Prebiotics stimulate beneficial microbes in our gut, resulting in an overall increase in our health. .Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is the predominant human gut disorder and presents itself as chronic abdominal pain caused by bloating and/or distension due to gas build-up in the gut. Microbiome dysbiosis is fundamental to IBS, and patients are reliant on a low-FODMAP-diet to reduce the intake of fermentable compounds and alleviate IBS symptoms. .The common prebiotics are oligosaccharides, obtained by hydrolysis of polysaccharides or synthesis from monosaccharides. Most commercially available prebiotic oligosaccharides are undefined mixtures and it is unknown whether they contribute to its beneficial effects. We aim to determine whether defined oligosaccharide mixtures more efficiently stimulate a healthy gut microbiome than random oligosaccharide mixtures. .We will use specific fungal enzymes to obtain defined but diverse oligosaccharide mixtures from pea and/or soy, substrates already used for plantbased dairy alternatives. These oligosaccharides will be used as test-substrates for beneficial and non-desired intestinal microbes. We will also investigate if defined oligosaccharide mixtures cause a decrease in gas-production by intestinal microbes, compared to the standard undefined mixtures used in prebiotics..The potential social and economic impact of this project are significant. Alternatives for animal based food are urgently needed and therefore developed by many companies, including our partner DSM. Society also requests healthy foods that prevent disease, and prebiotics are a main element of that. Our project has the potential of opening up a new approach to developing healthy alternative foods. Participation of DSM in this project will ensure that issues, like upscaling and downstream processing are considered in the results-evaluation, opening the door for a follow-up applied project in which this knowledge is developed into actual production processes.

Projecttitel: AMR-Global: Reducing inappropriate exposure to antibiotics
Projectbeschrijving: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an urgent security threat to global health, driven by bacterial exposure to antibiotics. Unless serious action is taken now, drug resistant microorganisms will be responsible for an estimated 10 million annual deaths worldwide by 2050. Overarching factors contributing to AMR are the inappropriate use of antibiotics, the lack of rapid diagnostic tests, and antibiotic pollution. Whilst AMR prevalence is rapidly increasing in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), our worldwide vulnerability to infectious diseases – made painfully apparent by the COVID-19 pandemic – demands international efforts. The Netherlands, as one of the frontrunners in the fight against AMR, has an important role to play. ..GLORIA is an international collaboration aiming to reduce and prevent antibiotic exposure. Within the first submission of the GLORIA program (GLORIA-1) two interventions will be developed and within this subsequent submission (GLORIA-2) two additional complementary innovations are proposed: .- A point-of-care diagnostic antibiotic susceptibility screening test using nano-technology for suspected urinary tract infections (UTI), and .- A portable adaptive sequencing technology for AMR surveillance in respiratory infections..Collectively, the projects in the GLORIA program will work towards achieving equitable health and improving the health outlook of society. Thus, our program is aligned with one of the main objectives of the Knowledge and Innovation Agenda 2020-2023 Health & Care (KIA), its Central Mission, Mission I, and Mission II. ..The success of GLORIA will contribute to reducing inappropriate exposure to antibiotics in individuals and the environment. GLORIA will enable improved individual treatment outcomes and, through its expected public health impact, will help curb the colossal healthcare expenditure due to AMR in the near future. Furthermore, GLORIA will solidify the Health~Holland International Strategy by strengthening the global position of the Netherlands in the AMR field.
Partners: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC), KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation (KNCV), Mozand BV, ShanX MedTech B.V.

Projecttitel: Clean Air for Everyone: aerosols and viral transmission, practical interventions by ventilation and air cleaning
Projectbeschrijving: Addressing existing knowledge gaps on the actual impact of both fixed ventilation systems and mobile air cleaning technologies on risk reduction of aerogenic SARS-CoV-2 transmission is vital. As other preventive measures are scaled down, ventilation and/or air cleaning systems and technologies may become the main line of defence relied upon to control SARS-CoV-2 infections..The objective of this multidisciplinary project is therefore to assess the efficacy of ventilation and air cleaning systems in a real-life context, by characterizing their properties (air exchange, clean air delivery rate, air flow pattern) under different combinations of implementation contexts and intervention scenarios, while quantifying airborne (infectious) SARS-CoV-2. Feasibility and acceptability of these interventions will be studied in two different contexts: 1) elementary schools and 2) facilities for care of aged individuals..The project recognizes and deals with interdependencies between ventilation systems and air cleaning technologies. It is organized into two distinct but interlinked work streams. Work stream one starts with experimental research to refine our understanding of the performance of ventilation systems. Work stream two runs largely in parallel, but focuses on air cleaning by mobile units, aiming to develop improved insight as well as assessment and validation technologies using experimental deployment of a variety of solutions from different suppliers. Both work streams incorporate air sampling for the collection and quantification of airborne (infectious) SARS-CoV-2 virus and other (mostly viral) pathogens, to move beyond the state of the art in risk assessment modelling under different intervention scenarios..The improved knowledge base created will greatly expand options for accurate ex-ante and ex-post evaluation of the acceptability and feasibility of different intervention scenarios based on ventilation and air cleaning. This public-private partnership is also essential in order to prepare Dutch society, not only for future waves of SARS-CoV-2 variants, but also for future pandemics.
Partners: AL-KO Luchttechniek B.V., ActiZ, Dehaco B.V., Dolphin Global Trade Holding B.V., Euromate B.V., Fellowes Holdings B.V., Konvektco Nederland B.V., Nederlandse Organisatie voor toegepast-natuurwetenschappelijk onderzoek TNO, Noa Air B.V., PlasmaMade B.V., Stichting Binnenklimaattechniek, TROX Nederland B.V., GEEN RECHTSPERSOON, Ultrasun International B.V., Universiteit Leiden, Universiteit Utrecht, Vereniging Binnenklimaat Nederland, Wolf energiesystemen B.V.

Projecttitel: Rapid SARS-CoV-2 detection and variant characterization using mass spectrometry coupled to AI predictions of variants of high risk: Staying ahead of the virus
Projectbeschrijving: The COVID-19 pandemic has focused attention on the mechanisms of emergence and spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants that have increased transmissibility, virulence, or potential to escape the immune response induced by earlier infection or vaccination. In this project we aim to develop a modular Mass-Spectrometry (MS)-based platform to analyze peptide fragments of the SARS-CoV-2 NCAP and spike proteins for (i) the diagnosis and characterization of SARS-CoV-2 infections with a focus on variant detection and (ii) the characterization of immune response to SARS-CoV-2 infection with a focus on the clinical course of disease. The (MS)-based platform is scalable, and with complementary computational predictions of protein variant structures, these data can in principle be used by Artificial Intelligence systems to predict protein variants that are likely to emerge in the near future and their associated health risks including their potential to escape the immune response acquired by vaccination or earlier infections. As proof-of-concept, we will use in vitro models to test if predicted high risk variants can indeed escape antibodies due to earlier infections or vaccination. Central in this project is the development of an open data model based on FAIR Digital Twins (FDT) of individual protein variants. The FDT allows automated management of the real-world, experimental and computational data generated in this project and from external sources. The MS testing platform, real-world data collection, and prediction/validation platforms are synergistically linked via a FAIR data-enabled feedback AI loop, and decision-intelligence, accelerating the research cycle to game-changing speeds. Ultimately, any novel variant that is detected or predicted to be of concern will automatically trigger software updates to the globally distributed MS platform, allowing real-time, worldwide detection of novel variants of the ever-evolving SARS-CoV-2 virus. As this strategy can be applied to any viral infection, this kick-start project will be key to pandemic preparedness roadmaps.

Projecttitel: GLORIA 3: Safe drinking water production from AMR polluted surface water by improving innovative membrane technology
Projectbeschrijving: The project fits within the Knowledge and Innovation Agenda 2020-2023. A key pillar supporting the KIA is the concept that medical and social challenges in the field of health and care are not local, but are relevant worldwide. In addition it supports the goals of the KIA “Landbouw, water, voedsel: MMIP C4 Verbeteren waterkwaliteit”. This project, as part of the GLORIA program, was developed with a cross-sectoral approach in which the the challenge of AMR, like many other medical, environmental and social challenges, must be addressed with an integrated global perspective..The project intends to lead to new opportunities for drinking water production from polluted surface water without negative impact on human health. Consequently, this project aims to implement the outcomes in the most vulnerable places (i.e. LMICs) to tackle one of the root causes of AMR. Thereby contributing to the prevention of AMR emergence and spread to other countries, including the Netherlands. The project is key for the contribution to the strategic international development of Global Health and prevention of AMR and also to achieve the ambitions of SDG6.
Partners: NX Filtration BV, Stichting Amsterdam Institute for Global Health and Development (afgekort Stichting AIGHD), Stichting Deltares, Stichting Saxion, Stichting VU

Projecttitel: FucoQuest: The impact of fucosylated human milk oligosaccharides on infant gut microbiome, metabolism and gut function
Projectbeschrijving: Breastfeeding is recommended to be fed to young children up to 2 years of age and beyond. This project will focus on understanding of fucosylated milk oligosaccharides, such as 2’-FL, which are highly prevalent in human milk and likely play a big role in the establishment of a healthy infant-microbiome symbiosis. Ultimately, the results will allow development of novel, safe and health-promoting nutritional concepts for infants and toddlers with a significantly shorter time-to-market.
Partners: Danone Global Research & Innovation Center B.V.

Projecttitel: Controlling microbial contaminants in plant-based foods to reduce waste and ensure safety
Projectbeschrijving: The transition to more sustainable food production increases the risk of unintentional microbial contaminants in the food chain. This project develops knowledge-based predictive models and strategies to reduce microbiological quality and safety risks throughout the production chain of sustainable plant-protein based foods. Implementation of the project results will lead to in reduction of food waste and food safety incidents in practice.
Partners: Arla Foods Amba, Bel S.A., Coöperatie Koninklijke Cosun U.A., GEEN RECHTSPERSOON, HP Hood, Ripple Foods Pbc (Ripple), SPX Flow Technology Assen B.V., Societé Des Produits Nestlé S.A. (Nestlé), Stichting HAS Opleidingen, Tetra Pak Cheese and Powder systems B.V., The Coca Cola Company, Wageningen Universiteit/ Wageningen University, Yili Innovation Center Europe B.V.

Projecttitel: Effector-screening and Genome Wide Association Studies to enable breeding for resistance to Phytophthora capsici
Projectbeschrijving: Phytophthora capsici is a worldwide prevalent pathogen of pepper and is the most destructive and economically important disease of pepper. High relative humidity and extreme weather events (e.g. heavy rain fall and flooding) can initiate wide spread infections. Since commercial pepper cultivars are very susceptible or just partially resistant to P. capsici, the disease is controlled by application of chemicals. Within this project we aim to identify resistant pepper accessions, effectors from P. capsici and molecular markers that will enable the participating companies to breed for pepper cultivars more resistant to P. capsici and more robust to climate change.
Partners: BEJO Zaden, Henan Biological Breeding Center Co. Ltd., Rijk Zwaan Zaadteelt en Zaadhandel, Syngenta Seeds  B.V., VILMORIN & CIE

Projecttitel: Duurzame graszaadteelt in een duurzame akkerbouwrotatie
Projectbeschrijving: Doel van het project is de duurzaamheid en weerbaarheid van de graszaadteelt en van akkerbouwrotaties in Nederland te vergroten. De bijdragen aan klimaat-, biodiversiteits-, emissie- en andere duurzaamheidskenmerken worden in kaart gebracht. Innovatieve maatregelen worden ontwikkeld, waardoor de graszaadteelt ecologisch, agronomisch en economisch aantrekkelijker wordt. Het project richt zich op:.•	Berekenen duurzaamheid van de graszaadteelt.•	Mogelijkheden voor organische mest.•	Mechanische onkruidbestrijding.•	Verhogen biodiversiteit.•	Rendabiliteit

Projecttitel: Towards optimal nutrient content and taste of fresh vegetables: A value chain analysis
Projectbeschrijving: We systematically study the additive and interactive effects of variety, growing protocols and postharvest handling on carotenoids (incl. vit A.) metabolism. We focus on the crops:  tomato (fruit), spinach (leaf); and carrot (root). The germplasm screen consists of traditional and modern varieties; the growth protocols vary in blue light content in relation to vapor pressure deficit; and the postharvest conditions are either darkness or light. We conclude with a consumer taste panel.
Partners: Nunhems Netherlands B.V., Priva B.V., Signify Netherlands B.V., vanRijsingeningredients B.V. (Proverka)

Projecttitel: Variation in S gene and S gene dosage to increase Botrytis resistance in rose and strawberry
Projectbeschrijving: Botrytis cinerea causes gray mold in Rosaceae like rose and strawberry. As the disease is difficult to control by technical measurements alone, there is a need for more resistant varieties to reduce production losses and decrease chemical use. Breeding companies indicate that screening for resistance is time consuming and difficult to standardize. We aim to bring breeding for resistance to Botrytis in Rosaceae in The Netherlands to a higher level.
Partners: De Ruiter Innovations B.V., Dümmen Orange The Netherlands B.V., Fresh Forward Breeding B.V., Interplant, Limgroup B.V., Meilland International, United Selections B.V.

Projectbeschrijving: Dit project is gericht op het duurzaam verminderen van Verticillium-verwelkingsziekte in kasteelten (met name chrysant en biologische groenteteelten paprika en aubergine) door een geïntegreerde aanpak gebaseerd op detectie, verbeterde bedrijfshygiëne op te identificeren kritieke punten in het teeltsysteem en de inzet van minder gevoelige rassen, biologische middelen én methoden om plant en bodemweerbaarheid te verhogen en/of inzet van antagonisten.
Partners: Coöperatie Bionext, Dekker Chrysanten, Deliflor Chrysanten B.V., Dümmen Orange The Netherlands B.V., Stallingsbedrijf Glastuinbouw Nederland Groep B.V., Stichting Chrysant NL, Stichting Kennis in je Kas, Van Zanten Breeding B.V.

Projecttitel: Automated broiler phenotyping using smart technologies to improve health, welfare and performance
Projectbeschrijving: Manual or visual observations still form the basis of a considerable part of the phenotypic records that are collected in broiler breeding programs, even though these observations can be time-consuming and subjective. In this project, we will investigate the implementation of technologies to automatically phenotype existing and novel traits in broilers, including activity, leg health and body weight. Through implementation of the recordings in breeding programs, this project can contribute to improved health and robustness of broilers.
Partners: Cobb Europe B.V., Dorset Identification B.V., FarmResult B.V.

Projecttitel: Integrated sustainable processing of oil and functional protein from oilseeds (INTRINSIC)
Projectbeschrijving: Oilseed residues are the single largest global source of protein losses in the supply chain. Achieving a total-use case for these materials has a huge potential impact. While technology exists to extract protein from many oilseed residues, adoption in existing, full-scale plants is limited by difficulties in separating components, the need for capital expenditures and high energy costs of extraction. Novel mild aqueous extraction technology is currently under development and seems initially promising, but requires substantial further research to deliver proteins with sufficient market value to sustain the business case. In general, oilseed crops suffer from a knowledge gap in the interaction between processing and protein food functionality. The goal of this project is to develop a strong knowledge basis for a novel, safe, green and profitable processing, combining co-extraction of oil and high-value functional protein.
Partners: Cano-ela B.V., Champlor, Danone Global Research & Innovation Center B.V., FOSS, Riverina Oils & Bio Energy Pty Ltd, Stichting Wageningen Research

Projecttitel: Chitinnovation: Sustainable chitin/chitosan production and innovative applications.
Projectbeschrijving: Chitin is the second most abundant natural carbohydrate biopolymer in the world, behind only cellulose. Chitin is present in crustaceans, insects and fungi. Chitosan, a derivative of chitin, has a huge potential for all kind of applications. It can be most effectively produced from chitin derived from the skeleton of crustaceans, like shrimp. In the Netherlands about 25-30 kT grey shrimp is annually harvested and most of it (>90%) is transported to Morocco for peeling. After peeling about 2/3 of the shrimp is leftover that can be used for the extraction of chitin/chitosan. However, currently most of the material is used as landfill. In this project we investigate a circular approach for the processing of grey shrimp in the Netherlands. This includes automatic peeling, a more sustainable chitin/chitosan extraction process of the leftover using enzymes and producing less salt. Furthermore, together with the end-users (novel) applications in food and feed areas will be developed for the extracted chitosan. In this consortium Wageningen Food & Biobased Research, Ruitenberg Ingredients B.V., Agrifirm and GPC Kant join forces to develop a circular shrimp process in the Netherlands.
Partners: Garnalenpelcentrum Kant, Nutrition Sciences N.V., Ruitenberg Ingredients B.V.

Projecttitel: Enrichment of the diet with insect-based feed ingredients for 1 Star Better Life labelled broilers
Projectbeschrijving: An increase in the global population will result in a higher demand for human food. A major concern is to guarantee the global capacity to provide enough animal feed (in particular protein ingredients), trying to avoid as much as possible competition with human food demand. For this purpose, insects have been proposed as a high quality, efficient and sustainable alternative protein source for poultry. Use of insects in the food chain will result in (1) reduced use of land and water; (2) low greenhouse gas emissions; (3) high feed conversion efficiencies; (4) transformation of low-value organic by-products into high-quality feed ingredients and by this contributing significantly to circularity. Next to these benefits insect products may also improve animal health. In this project the final aim is to decrease the use of imported soy products for animal feed by replacing soy products with black soldier fly protein and black soldier fly oil in combination with inclusion of regionally grown alternative protein sources..The research will be conducted with 1 star Better Life broilers in three phases, starting with a first pilot to study effects of different inclusion levels of different insect-based products (meal, meal with extra chitin, and oil) on sustainability, broiler health and welfare, performance and carcass characteristics. Based on this pilot, insect-based products will be selected and included at low levels in broiler diets and tested on large scale in 1 star Better Life broiler farms to study effects on sustainability, broiler health and welfare, performance, and carcass characteristics. In a second pilot experiment insect products in broiler diets in combination with other alternative regionally grown protein sources (full replacement of soybean meal) will be tested to study effects on sustainability, broiler health and welfare, performance and carcass characteristics.
Partners: B.V. Esbro, ForFarmers Nederland B.V., Protix B.V., Verenigde Nederlandse Insectenkwekers (Venik)

Projecttitel: Cellular proteins: a sustainable source of food proteins
Projectbeschrijving: As a global agricultural leader with mature supply chains, The Netherlands has significant advantages in circular production systems for upcycling available biomass. The goal of this project is to investigate sustainable production chains for cellular proteins from microalgae, bacteria, fungi and yeast. The project comprises investigation of growth conditions, downstream processing, physico-chemical functionality, suitability for product application, and sustainability & consumer acceptance.
Partners: Anheuser-Busch Inbev Nv/Sa, Mauri Technology B.V., NIZO food research B.V., PeelPioneers B.V., Phycom B.V., Stichting HAS Opleidingen, Unilever Innovation Centre Wageningen B.V., Wageningen Universiteit/ Wageningen University, Westland Kaasspecialiteiten B.V.

Projecttitel: "Opening the 'intestinal black box' of protein digestion and absorption kinetics in the aging GI tract"
Projectbeschrijving: Worldwide, the aging population is increasing. Aging is associated with a decline in functional abilities and loss of independence, but also an increased risk of co-morbidity, such as metabolic diseases. Sufficient protein intake is imperative to maintain muscle mass, quality and function as well as various physiological processes and thereby stimulates healthy and active aging..Whereas the overall protein intake is generally lower in older adults, previous studies indicate that they need about 40% more dietary protein for muscle protein synthesis as compared to young adults. Although limited evidence shows some alterations in gastrointestinal (GI) tract physiology with aging, it is not clear to what extent actual digestion and absorption are altered in older individuals. On the one hand, less effective absorption will impact the efficacy of dietary interventions. On the other hand, this will lead to protein spill over to the colon and increased bacterial proteolytic fermentation associated with the production of noxious metabolites and negative intestinal health effects..The current project aims to open the 'intestinal black box' to get further insight in the digestion and absorption kinetics of protein in older individuals. The project will evaluate digestion, absorption and metabolism of protein in young and older adults based on two invasive mechanistic endoscopy intervention studies using stable isotope tracers in combination with analyses in small intestinal tissue, blood and fecal samples. This combined in vivo and ex vivo approach will deliver essential insight for follow-up studies on optimizing protein intake and thereby independency and health outcome of the growing aging population.

Om de weerbaarheid van bloembollen tegen aantasting door ziekten en plagen te verhogen, is onderzoek nodig naar het werkingsmechanisme van het aanschakelen van de plantafweer. Dit door beïnvloeding van inhoudsstoffen en veranderingen in de morfologie van blad en bol, door middel van externe factoren. De focus ligt op lelie en tulp, zowel tijdens de teelt als tijdens de bewaring, en weerbaarheid tegen insecten, Botrytis, Fusarium en Penicillium.
Partners: Agrifirm International B.V., CAV Agrotheek B.V., Coöperatieve Nederlandse Bloembollencentrale U.A. (CNB), Keukenhof B.V., Koninklijke Handelsbond voor Boomkwekerij- en Bolproducten, Profytodsd B.V., Stichting Bollenacademie, Stichting Innovatie & Verduurzaming Bloembollenteelt (IVB)

Projecttitel: Zuivel, een duurzame eiwitbron voor gezond ouder worden!
Projectbeschrijving: Dit project richt zich op het ontwikkelen van eiwitrijke en ecologisch duurzame voedingsconcepten als onderdeel van een actieve leefstijl ter bevordering van gezond ouder worden. Voor de ontwikkeling van duurzame voedingsconcepten zoeken we beargumenteerd naar innovatieve voedingsproducten op basis van zowel plantaardige als zuiveleiwitbronnen. Op basis van de eiwittransitie wordt hierbij gestreefd naar een verandering van 40:60 naar 60:40 verhouding plantaardig:dierlijke eiwitbronnen in de voedingsconcepten. Leidend in deze ontwikkeling zijn de criteria: 1. Ecologische duurzaamheid, 2. Eiwitkwaliteit in relatie tot (spier)gezondheid, en 3. Behoefte en voorkeur van consumenten. De voedingsconcepten worden geëvalueerd door consumenten en bestudeerd in een leefstijlinterventie met training en e-health ondersteuning. Dit project draagt bij aan duurzame voeding, als onderdeel van een actieve leefstijl, met het doel om actief en gezond ouder te worden in een gezonde omgeving.

Dit onderzoek richt zich binnen het thema bodemkwaliteit op de aaltjesbeheersingsstrategie in de bloembollen. We willen via een BodemKwaliteitPlan de bodem duurzaam verbeteren, integraal voor eigen en gehuurde percelen. Er wordt nieuwe kennis ontwikkeld op het gebied van waardplantstatus en schadegevoeligheid, beheersing van stengelaaltjes en van Trichodoriden. Praktijkimplementatie krijgt aandacht via pilotbedrijven en de Boerderij van de Toekomst.
