Cancer is one of the leading causes of death worldwide. The development of therapeutics targeting novel.mechanisms contributing to cancer progression and metastasis will lead to new therapies and paradigms in the.fight against cancer. Like all other cells, cancer cells are covered by carbohydrate structures (glycans) expressed.on proteins and lipids. There is a growing body of literature showing that the glycan pattern of cancer cells is very.different from that of healthy cells. It is still unclear whether aberrant glycosylation of cancer cells is a cause or.consequence of tumorigenesis but it is associated with aggressive and invasive forms of cancer and hence a poor.prognosis. Hence, glycosylation in cancer is emerging as a new target to develop anti-cancer drugs. Specifically,.the overexpression of sialic acid and fucose sugars is associated with the local suppression of the immune.response, increased metastasis via extravasation and migration and increased cancer growth and resistance to.chemo- and radiotherapy. We and others have shown that cancer glycosylation is a bona fide therapeutic target in.cancer. Moreover, we developed small molecule inhibitors, coined Sialostatin and Fucotrim, which decrease the.cellular sialic acid and fucose expression, respectively. This proposal is aimed to advance the development of.Sialostatin and Fucotrim as novel anti-cancer drugs. In work package 1 of this project we will identify tumor types.that are sensitive to fucose and sialic acid glycosylation inhibitors. To this end, we propose the in silico profiling of.fucose and sialic acid biosynthesis pathways and correlate their expression to tumor progression and patient.survival. Preclinical murine models for the selected cancer indications will be employed to establish the efficacy of.glycosylation inhibitors in vivo and we will explore the biological mechanism(s) that underpin the anti-tumor.effect. Secondly, to progress Sialostatin and Fucotrim along the preclinical pipeline, their drug-like properties and.safety will be improved in work package 2. These improved derivatives will be tested in vivo using the preselected.models identified in work package 1 to arrive at optimized compounds and mouse models to enable subsequent.investigational new drug (IND) enabling studies.

Projecttitel: RADIATHE - Real-time Absolute Dose-control In Anti-cancer THErmotherapy
Projectbeschrijving: Background.Clinical studies showed that thermotherapy (TT), heating of tumors to 40-44°C, significantly enhances.the therapeutic efficacy of radiotherapy and chemotherapy without adding side effects. TT acts along.multiple mechanisms on cellular and tissue level that make malignant tissue more susceptible to ionizin.g radiation and cytotoxic/molecular-targeted drugs. Despite these results, widespread TT use in.oncology is hampered by the complex and laborious workflow of the treatment. Recently, magnetic.resonance imaging (MRI) guided TT was developed for monitoring temperature and TT-biomarkers, but.this approach is too expensive for broad application in general hospitals. Moreover, while temperature.and biomarkers are important, they are almost impossible to prescribe. Currently, the uncertain TT.delivery reduces treatment outcome, complicates TT treatment and is a roadblock for widespread TT ap.plication..Alternatively, the absorbed power level during TT, expressed in the absolute cumulative specific.absorption rate (SAR), can be prescribed in clear-cut treatment protocols, correlates with induced.temperature and associates with treatment outcome. However, absolute SAR control is to date not possi.ble..Objectives.RADIATHE aims to develop sensory-guided TT, and technology that enables to validate sensory-guided.TT both experimentally and in-vivo using MRI guided TT..Hypothesis.Our hypothesis is that sensory-guided TT enables a strong improvement in TT delivery control leading to.a streamlined treatment protocol ready for widespread adoption..Design.The main objective splits into two tasks.A device and software for instant dynamic characterization of TT applicators..A device and software for accurate prospective dose control..Social and economic impact.RADIATHE aims to offer tightly controlled TT to a large group of cancer patients for improving cure and/.or decreasing toxicity (by replacement of part of radiotherapy/chemo dose by TT) for improved quality.of life and reduction of costs of aftercare. Automation (replacing one operator) and sensing (avoiding.MRI occupation) also reduce the burden on the healthcare system.

Projecttitel: Wnt inhibitors to treat Colorectal Cancer
Projectbeschrijving: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a common and deadly disease, with more than 1.9 million new cases and 935,000 deaths worldwide in 2020. New therapies to treat CRC are therefore urgently needed. Considering the central role of the Wnt pathway activation in CRCs (>80% of CRCs are Wnt-dependent), direct inhibition of oncogenic Wnt signalling represents an appealing therapeutic strategy. Project partner Tom Grossmann and team have developed different peptidomimetic Wnt inhibitors and have recently identified a family of peptidomimetics that interfere with the Wnt pathway by binding ß-catenin and inhibiting its interaction with the TCF/LEF transcription factors. These agents are first-in-class and will be the basis of this WINCE project where we aim to develop therapeutics that selectively inhibit oncogenic Wnt signalling .

Projecttitel: Overcoming Barriers to Potentiate Localized Treatment Against Pancreatic Cancer
Projectbeschrijving: Problem description: Pancreatic cancer is the most lethal cancer type with 5-year surivial rate of only 8%. Surgery is considered.as a curative treatment for localized tumor, but is possible in only 15% patients, while others are treated with chemotherapy..However, chemotherapy fails to show significant improvement in the therapeutic outcome. One major reason of this failure is the.presence of abundant fibrotic stroma, which hinders tumor delivery of chemotherapy, confers resistance against the treatment and.feed tumor cell toproliferate..Solution: To solve the problem of poor tumor delivery and stroma-supported mechanisms, we propose to apply two key.approaches: (i) local injection of chemotherapy using thermosensitive hydrogel in order to deliver high amounts directly into the.tumor with prolonged release. Local injections are feasible in patients using endoscopic ultrasound fine needle injection. (ii).combine anti-stromal agent to enhance intra-tumoral distribution and inhibit stroma-supported mechanisms to enhance therapeutic.efficacy..Aim: The main aim is to develop innovative tools to deliver chemotherapy locally into the tumor while combining antistromal.therapy to overcome the stromal barriers, thereby achieving sustained delivery of chemotherapy with induced intra-tumoral.distribution and reduced resistance..Plan of investigation: First, chemotherapy (gemcitabine and paclitaxel) and the anti-stromal cyclic peptide will be loaded into a.thermosensitive hydrogel to achieve sustained release of both components while maintaining essential properties of the hydrogel.i.e. thermoresponse and injectability. Second, in parallel, a co-culture stroma-rich 3D tumor model will be developed to test and.optimize drug-loaded hydrogels to select best formulations for in vivo testing. Third, the hydrogel will be tested and validated for its.effect on the intratumoral distribution of chemotherapy and then followed by efficacy studies in relevant mouse tumor models to.establish enhanced therapeutic effects..Expected outcome: Results from this project will provide insights and proof-of-concept data on the use of this unique combination.of locally injectable chemotherapy and anti-stromal therapy against pancreatic cancer. When successful, the industrial partners will.take steps to develop it as a product which can provide new opportunity for patients with marginally-resectable or unresectable.localized pancreatic cancer to undergo surgery and have a better quality of life.

Projecttitel: Unlocking the potential of autotaxin inhibition for the treatment of NASH-HCC
Projectbeschrijving: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common and deadly malignancies with over 905000 new diagnosed cases and 830000 deathsin 2020. Due to the increasing prevalence of obesity, diabetes, and metabolic syndrome, a high proportion of HCC is now attributed to non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), a severe form of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Owing to growing prevalence of NASH-HCC and non/poor-responsiveness of NASH-HCC patients to (immune)therapy, more efforts are needed to discover new therapies for NASH-HCC.   The involvement and prognostic significance of autotaxin-lysophosphatidic acid (ATX-LPA) pathway (and transforming growth factor beta, TGFß) has been established in (NASH)-HCC. Recently, we have shown that type IV ATX inhibitors possess favorable therapeutic efficacy in preclinical mouse models; and galunisertib (TGFBR1 inhibitor) supplementation improved overall survival in HCC patients as reported earlier. We aim to examine inhibitors developed by iOnctura: IOA-289, an oral type IV ATX inhibitor (with successful phase 1a clinical study and under clinical development for pancreatic cancer) and the selective oral TGFBR1 inhibitor (IOA-359), in NASH-HCC, while developing an understanding of the mechanism. In this ATX-HCC project, we will assess the safety, efficacy and establish the mechanism-of-actions of ATX inhibitor (IOA-289) and TGFBR1 inhibitor (IOA-359) (alone and in combination) using 2D and 3D cell-based models; and pre-clinical NASH-HCC murine models. Promising preliminary results obtained in cell-based models, and preclinical pancreatic tumor models demonstrate the feasibility of this project. The results obtained will improve our mechanistic understanding and will forward the clinical development of the IOA drugs for NASH-HCC and other cancers. This project, therefore, will have a significant impact on the society including scientific community and patients. Moreover, since these drugs are cost-effective and cheaper compared to the currently used immunotherapies or antibody-.based therapies, this project will have huge economic impact on the healthcare system worldwide.

Projecttitel: Creating a bi-specific antibody-based therapy to eliminate CD117-positive AML
Projectbeschrijving: Background AML is characterized by an uncontrolled proliferation and enhanced survival of abnormal myeloid precursors in the BM. The 7+3 regimen (7 days cytarabine, 3 days daunorubicin) is the standard of care of AML, resulting in long-term cures of young patients (30-40%), a 5-years survival rate of 40-45% of patients between 50-55-years old, a 5-years survival rate of 30-35% between 55-60-years old patients and a less than 15% 5-years survival rate of older patients (13). In the BM-niches, the molecular interactions between the AML cells and BM protect the LSC from the standard treatments (14, 15). Stem Cell Factor (SCF) is a cytokine that binds to CD117 expressed on HSPCs and leads to the activation of pro-survival signaling pathways of HSCs (16, 17). Recent single cell analysis show that CD117 is highly expressed on quiescent stem-like cells and proliferating stem/progenitor-like cells in AML (18). CD117 is expressed on AML cells in up to 85% of AML patients (19). Moreover, paracrine and autocrine expression of SCF and CD117 self-activating mutations are described in AML and strongly suggest that SCF signaling is an essential survival factor for LSCs (12, 20-22). The high expression of CD117 on LSC and their dependency on SCF signaling makes therapies that target CD117 desirable as clonal escape of CD117-negative LSCs is impeded by it...Available antibodies to deplete CD117-positive cells A number of anti-CD117 antibodies are in development for use in human but their efficacy remains low. An anti-human CD117 mouse monoclonal antibody, called SR-1, inhibits HSC in-vitro. A humanized version of SR-1 antibody (AMG191, WO2019/113437-A1) has been developed. This antibody lacks direct killing capacity , as it is aglycosylated and therefore unable to be recognized by Fc receptors and promote downstream effector functions such as antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) and complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC). However, humanized AMG191 is still capable of depleting HSPCs by inhibiting CD117 signaling, which is essential for HSC survival (23). In non-human primates, the circulation time of AMG191 is dependent on the dose having a T½ of 1.88 days (0.1 mg/kg) to 4.3 days (25 mg/kg). In non-human primates and human BM CD34+ xenografted immune-deficient mice, AMG191 treatment depleted endogenous HSPCs and conditioned the BM for HSC engraftment without toxicity (24). Although the aforementioned studies show proof of concept, the first results of an ongoing clinical trial (Trial: NCT02963064) using CD117-targeting for conditioning in patients with severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), report low percentages of chimerism (3-10%) after allogeneic HSCT (25). In this study, the full length AMG191 was used, and HSCT was only performed 20 days post-treatment, when AMG191 antibody plasma levels post-injection reached

Projectbeschrijving: Monoclonal antibodies Monoclonal antibodies (mAb) have become the most successful class of biologics in history to fight cancer. This is due to the highly specific nature of antibodies, whereby the Fab-region specifically binds part of an epitope overexpressed on tumor cells. Recognition of Fc-receptor expressing cells of the immune system activates these cells mounting an immune response against cancer, thereby activating the immune system via its Fc tail in a controlled fashion.

Projecttitel: Improved Thyroid Nodule Assessment and Stratification using Optoacoustic-Ultrasound Imaging with Machine Learning
Projectbeschrijving: Decisions that lead to overdiagnosis have several effects that may be life-long: diagnostic or therapeutic surgery has risks of laryngeal nerve injury and hypoparathyroidism [50], and often lifelong thyroid-replacement therapy with blood level monitoring. Overdiagnosed thyroid nodules, can thus be categorized as a widespread physiological or chronic condition. A successful OA-US imaging technology will see improved negative predictive value which will preclude subjects from being labelled “thyroid cancer patients” thereby releasing them from unnecessary surveillance, invasive procedures, and extensive stress. By this, our project contributes directly to (i) the Central Mission of the Top Sector LSH which aims to achieve by 2040 that all Dutch citizens will live at least five years longer in good health, and to (ii) Mission III Top Sector LSH’s aim of achieving by 2030, an increase by 25% of the proportion of people with a chronic disease or lifelong disability who can play an active role in society.

Projecttitel: Improved Detection, Surveillance and Resection of Rectal Cancer using Near-Infrared Fluorescent-Labelled Peptide-Based Probes
Projectbeschrijving: The main objective is to make use of existed data and AI-software to I) identify novel tumor targets which are overexpressed in rectal cancer compared to healthy rectal and surrounding tissue; and II) develop, synthesize and evaluate tracers conjugated to clinically applied NIR dye to visualize the identified tumors in rectal cell lines and in animal tumor models.

Engineered T-cells are revolutionizing cancer therapy. Currently CAR T-cells have generated exciting clinical data in leukemia underlining their tremendous potential. But their application is not straightforward. Current clinical protocols require isolation of T-cells form the patient, ex vivo transduction of these T-cells with viral vectors to induce CAR expression, amplification of the engineered CAR-T-cells and reinfusion into the patient. The patient needs to be pretreated with chemotherapy to maximize CAR T-cell effectivity. The total costs of therapy are ~300-400 k€. A targeted lipid nanoparticle that could engineer T-cells in situ inside the patient removes the need for the complex, and costly ex vivo manufacturing that is the current state-of the art, and it avoids hazardous patient treatment steps required for these procedures altogether. This would be a truly next-generation advanced therapeutic tool that will drastically reduce the costliness, complexity, associated risks, and inefficacy of CAR T-cell therapy that increases the accessibility of these therapies for patients. The switch to in vivo generation of engineered T-cells instead of ex vivo has dramatic implications for the accessibility of this technology for larger patient groups.

Projecttitel: (OSCAR) bOne metaStasis chip with microphysiological Circulation for cAncer pRofiling
Projectbeschrijving: Cancer treatments have improved significantly over the past decades. However, metastasis, the spreading of tumour cells to distant organs, remains incurable and represents the major cause of death of cancer patients. Skeletal metastasis is frequent in multiple cancer types, particularly in prostate (85%) breast cancer (70%) patients, which strongly impact the patients’ quality of life. We do not understand what mechanisms drive circulating tumour cells (CTCs) extravasation from the blood into the soft and nutrient-rich bone marrow, and to invade towards the stiffer bone compartment, where they establish specific interactions with bone-forming (osteoblasts) and bone-degrading (osteoclasts) cell types. The understanding of the cancer-specific crosstalk and remodelling of the bone environment is crucial to establish better options for prevention, prediction, and treatment of bone metastases. Current bone models lack the important vascularized bone marrow compartment, thereby neglecting the contribution of the bone marrow as transition site with its unique mechanical and physical properties. The aim of this project is to develop a “bone-metastasis-chip” (OSCAR) with a recirculation system (CRIS) that recapitulates the passage of cancer cells from the blood stream to stiff bone structures to profile the CTC-specific crosstalk and bone marrow changes. We will adopt available chip designs and modify them according to the requirements of OSCAR. CRIS will be designed with an emphasis on compatibility with circulating cells and easy operation with a small footprint to scale up experiments. An oxygen gradient will be established in OSCAR and measured using commercial sensors. This project will deliver an advanced and tuneable bone-on-chip system that faithfully mimics the anatomy and physiology of human bone allowing the study of CTC behaviour during the earliest stages of bone metastatic development. Importantly, OSCAR and the knowledge generated has pan-cancer relevance with application in a broad field of preclinical research.
Aanvrager: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC)

Projecttitel: The Netherlands Network for Difficult-To-Treat Depression: Towards a better positioning of novel pharmacological treatment
Projectbeschrijving: Background: Depression represents one of the most common mental disorders and is.currently listed as one of the main contributors to the overall disease burden. In the.Netherlands, around 5% of the general population is affected by this mood disorder and.approximately 19% develops depression in the course of a lifetime. Despite the application.of evidence-based treatment strategies, research indicates that around 20-30% of the.patients does not respond to conventional antidepressant treatment. These patients are.classified as difficult-to-treat depression (DTD). The pharmaceutical industry has.developed several pharmacological treatment strategies that specifically target the DTD.population (i.e., esketamine, psilocybin, MIJ821). While the efficacy of these innovative.treatment strategies has been established in clinical trials (or are currently under.investigation) more research is needed to position these novel agents in the current.treatment landscape..Objective: The overall objective of the proposed project is to improve the positioning of.novel pharmacological agents in the treatment landscape of DTD using biomarkers,.functionality markers, and big data..Design: The proposed research includes state of the art data science methods to evaluate.the benefits and limitations of current treatment strategies using routine healthcare data..Previously collected clinical trial data and biobank materials will be analysed to identify.patient characteristics that predict treatment outcomes (i.e., treatment predictors) and to.elucidate the underlying mechanisms of treatment strategies (i.e., treatment targets). The.results will be utilized to develop treatment allocation strategies for novel pharmacological.agents in clinical practice..Social and economic impact: The proposed project provides important insights to advance.the treatment of DTD. More effective treatment reduces the proportion of individuals living.with chronic depression, and, hence, lifelong disability. This will lead to a considerable.reduction in healthcare utilization and a significant increase in societal participation,.reducing the economic burden for the society.

Scope: ImmuneHealthSeed is the foundation for ImmuneHealthXL. We are convinced that cross-disease approaches provide the best route towards precision and preventive evidence-based treatment for the million patients with Immune Mediated Inflammatory Diseases (IMID)..ImmuneHealthSeed prioritises to:.(1) synergize building upon successes of the three existing Immunology Public Private Partnerships in identifying IMID-overarching immune networks, generating high-quality disease-overarching data, and generating novel cross-disease solutions for immunomonitoring and immunotherapies..(2) multiply investments by combining the expertises of researchers from academic and for-profit sectors, patients, treating physicians, health foundations, and regulators to translate together and identify key opportunities to tackle chronic IMIDs..Ambition: No IMID therapy repairs defective immunological networks sufficiently to induce long-term, drug-free, clinical remission in all patients. In ImmuneHealthSeed, we will identify disease-overarching “immunological disease activity” (IDA) signatures, associated with disease reactivation/remission, to find key regulatory networks per patient. We aim to make chronic IMIDs diseases of the past by identifying the right therapy for the appropriate immune profile of each patient..Design: We will monitor IDA via serum/plasma immune proteomics and identify common underlying immune mechanisms driving (re)activation of disease-associated dendritic cell (DC)-T-B cell networks. Synergy is created by continuation of our disease-overarching prospective clinical studies and by implementing our new, harmonised technological and analytical pipelines to monitor DC-T-B immune profiles developed in TIMID, Target2B, and DC4Balance. In parallel, we will design novel nanotherapeutic immunotherapies to counter disease reactivation mechanisms. We will generate various formulations of tolerance-inducing- or immune-silencing nanoparticles and evaluate which formulation is best suited. We will achieve translation together by integrating experimental data with clinical disease activity and patient-reported IDAs..Impact: Advanced understanding of disease-overarching immune profiles and regulatory networks of individual patients in relation to their IDA will translate into patient-tailored therapies that reset specific pathological immune profiles in IMIDs.

Projecttitel: Scan2Go: autonomous MRI for large scale diagnostics of brain integrity
Projectbeschrijving: Most people experiencing cognitive decline want a timely and accurate diagnosis. They also want to know what to expect (prognosis) and seek treatment to prevent further cognitive decline, particularly since emerging treatments are considered most effective in early disease stages. MRI is a powerful tool for diagnosis, prognostication, and assessment of effects of novel treatments. It is, however, relatively expensive as it requires experts for scanner operating and diagnostic reporting, which is subject to interpretation. From patients’ perspective, MRI can be unpleasant and results difficult to understand. Our objective is to make MRI more accessible for timely dementia assessment at large by reducing costs ten-fold, improving patient friendliness, and facilitating automatic, comprehensible reporting. We will design an easy-to-use autonomous MRI dedicated for diagnosing neurodegeneration and cerebrovascular injury consistent with (early-stage) dementia. By bringing together recent advances in hardware technology we will simplify operation and minimize anxiety so that people can scan themselves. Moreover, we will use artificial intelligence(AI) to interpret the images, with clearly understandable communication of results(Amsterdam-UMC). Innovations include embedding high-conductive RF-coil arrays(TeslaDC) to facilitate automated patient couch(Inno-metaal) and metal detection for safe(UMCU) and autonomous MRI in Helium-free magnets(Philips), using quantified fast 3D acquisition(UMCU) with gradients(Futura) driven(Prodrive) above the human-hearing frequency to minimize anxiety, and AI(ErasmusMC) automated diagnostic reporting(Quantib) directly operated by patients outside the hospital(QuaRijn). Synchronized to international programs and supported by industry-partners, we will deliver the demonstrator, ready for implementation/industrialization, that can provide sustainable diagnosis of early-stage cognitive impairments at large.

Projecttitel: Identification of a new microRNA as a diagnostic and therapeutic target for Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Targeted expression of AAV sponge vectors to normalize aberrant microRNA levels in Motor Neurons and Microglial cells
Projectbeschrijving: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a chronic neurological disease without any cure. Life expectancy is short as patients die of respiratory failure within 3-5 years after symptom onset. Current therapies for ALS involve usage of small molecules targeting dysregulated pathways among the various cell types. However, the available drugs often cause significant off-target effects, due to the lack of properties of these treatments to target a specific cell type, leading to cellular toxicity. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) act as master regulators that can regulate multiple pathways and deregulation of miRNAs has been shown to be associated with aberrant cellular phenotypes in ALS. Our approach relies on cell-type specific targeting of a miRNA deregulated in motor neurons (MNs) and microglia cells carrying ATAXIN2 and C9ORF72 patient mutations. To re-establish cellular homeostasis we will antagonize the expression of miRNA in individual cell types by generating adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapy tools that drive cell type-specific expression of miRNA sponge transcripts. For our investigations, we will use patient-derived human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) to generate human MNs in 2D and human microglia cells from cerebral organoids in 3D. In addition we will investigate the mode-of-action (MoA), biomarker potential and effect on rescuing disease phenotypes of the anti-miRNA sponge treatment. Most people who develop ALS are between the ages of 40 and 70. It goes without saying, ALS has a huge impact not only on these patients but equally on the beloved ones of patients and caregivers. The direct economic burden is significant as this devastating disease comes with a high loss of productive years. The results from this project will potentially lead towards development of a new treatment paradigm that will provide clinicians with an additional source of therapy.

Projecttitel: Extension of the Cuore for noninvasive analysis of muscle-on-a-chip: increased throughput, exercise modules, and application to muscle disease
Projectbeschrijving: There is increasing interest to develop advanced systems for the modeling of human disease using organ-on-chip technology. For 3D-tissue engineered skeletal muscles (3D-TESMs), two major systems can be distinguished based on sensing contractile force: those using video imaging, and those requiring dissection and attachment to a force transducer. In collaboration with the company Optics11 we have generated the Cuore, a device that can electrically stimulate and measure contractile force using optical fibers integrated in a smart lid. This presents several advantages: it can continuously monitor contractile force in the incubator in a noninvasive manner, it has integrated electrodes enabling long-term muscle exercise programs, and it has superior sensitivity. In the pre-version of the system, only one 3D-TESM at a time could be analyzed. We made adjustments and can now measure contractile forces in a 24-wells plate. Here, we will further develop the Cuore to enable even higher throughput analysis. In addition, we will develop and test muscle exercise programs, required for the maintenance of skeletal muscle. We will generate hardware and software that will enable parallel stimulation and measurement of four 24-well plates to analyze 96 3D-TESMs simultaneously. To reduce the number of required cells, we will decrease the volume of 3D-TESMs. We will monitor the effect of different muscle exercise programs, and we will apply exercise to 3D-TESMs generated from patients with Pompe disease and facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy. We will compare the effects of exercise on contractile force and molecular and cell biological parameters including disease hallmarks. We anticipate that these advancements will contribute to better understanding of human neuromuscular disease, and provide means for personalized testing of therapies. Ultimately, this should result in accelerated treatment development, leading to enhanced societal and economic participation of patients.

Projecttitel: Mechanisms behind the anti-microbial and barrier-protective activity of non-digestible oligosaccharides against E.coli and Clostridium-related early life intestinal infections.
Projectbeschrijving: Background: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is the most severe inflammatory disease of the gut that primarily impacts premature infants and is commonly encountered in neonatal intensive care units worldwide. The etiology of NEC multifactorial with intestinal dysbiosis being a major factor involved in NEC pathogenesis. The intestinal microbiota of NEC patients showed an increased abundance of Clostridium and Enterobacteriaceae genera, including Escherichia coli. Antibiotics are one of the primary treatments in these infants. There is a growing concern for short and long term adverse effects with early-life antibiotic exposure and the emergence of resistant strains. Therefore, alternatives that can tackle these problems are needed. The objective is to provide an alternative treatment and/or prevention strategy for E. coli and Clostridum-related infections using specific non-digestible oligosaccharides (NDOs) and human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs). Design: We will evaluate 1) the effects of NDOs/HMOs on E. coli and Clostridum growth, and 2) on E. coli and Clostridum-disturbed intestinal barrier and immune function. 3) We aim to characterize the underlying mechanism of their antimicrobial/barrier-protective properties and use these NDOs/HMOs in combination with antibiotics to investigate additive effects. 4) The additive/synergistic effects of combinations of different promising NDOs/HMOs that possess antimicrobial/barrier-protective properties will be explored and these combinations might be used in future clinical trials.Social impact: Prevention or treatment (without side effects) of increased abundance of E. coli and Clostridum related to NEC will have major consequences on associated morbidity, mortality and adverse effects on future health. The suppression of further development of antibiotic resistance will have an important impact on the society as a whole. Economic Impact: To control the increased abundance of E. coli and Clostridum in early life will mitigate the burden of NEC and associated hospitalizations and (health)care costs. NDOs/HMOs may increase the effectiveness of antibiotics resulting in a decreased antibiotic use.

Projecttitel: Advanced complexity in human derived organoid models for virology
Projectbeschrijving: Understanding neurological infectious diseases is needed as they are a major threat to human health. Poliovirus has lead to debilitating outbreaks of paralytic disease, and the polio-related enteroviruses are still the most common causes of viral brain infections. Neuro-infections lead to high hospitalisation rates and long-term complications with often no treatment available. Neuropathogenicity of human viruses is notoriously difficult to study in animal models. Therefore, suitable human experimental models are needed such as organoids, which accurately mimic the human physiological environment. The Amsterdam UMC (AMC) has already established gut, airway, and brain organoids as tools for studying viral infections and viral vector-based gene therapy. To further study virus-host interplay, advanced organoid models are needed. In the ADVOCATE study, the Amsterdam UMC and VectorY bring in means and expertise to expand knowledge on neurovirulence and countermeasures. Amsterdam UMC has expertise in establishing stem cell-derived organotypic cultures for studying viruses and antiviral testing. VectorY has an innovative platform for delivery of antibodies to the central nervous system and has developed a unique neuro-muscular organoid (NMO) model. The ADVOCATE study is structured into two work packages. In WP1, a NMO will be implemented for neuro-infection of non-polio enteroviruses and assessing how these viruses affect NMO function. WP2 will focus on potential antiviral strategies by studying the spread of vectorized antibodies in NMO and testing of existing antivirals against neurovirulent enteroviruses with the aim to develop efficient antiviral strategies. Overall, the ADVOCATE study will deliver an advanced NMO model for virology which lowers the barriers for the implementation of organoids in virology and enable a smooth transition to animal-free innovations

Projecttitel: Breaking the bond: Inhibiting the formation of T-cell rosettes in Hodgkin lymphoma using Microorganosheres to develop more targeted less toxic treatment
Projectbeschrijving: Cure rates for pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) currently exceeds 80%, but survivors areconfronted with chronic health conditions later in life. The HL micro-environment is.characterized by T-cells that surround, protect, and promote survival of tumor cells (socalled.rosettes). Our aim is to study which molecular pathways drive rosette.formation and develop interventions to beak this bond. However, current in vitro.model systems do not recapitulate these complex cell-cell interactions, hampering us to.screen for potential interventions. We will use Xilis’ proprietary MicroOrganoSphere (MOS).technology that allows for generating and studying spheroids in which the tumor-niche is.retained.

Projecttitel: Breaking the bond: Inhibiting the formation of T-cell rosettes in  Hodgkin lymphoma using MicroOrganoSheres to develop more targeted less toxic treatment
Projectbeschrijving: With close to 47.000 cancer-related deaths in 2019, cancer is the leading cause of death in the Netherlands. The emergence of new treatment strategies such as those with an immuno-oncology approach holds much promise/ However, cancer is a collection of multi-faceted and ever-changing diseases, whose core biology enables fast adaptation to or escape from most therapies. Despite much research and investment in development of new immuno-oncology therapies, response to treatment is often limited and development of resistance to treatment is frequent. It is thus evident that a fundamental understanding of cancer biology is vital to enable the discovery of new therapeutics. Oncode established as a network organization bringing together public and private parties under one strategic mission: to crack the code of cancer for a future in which everyone can survive cancer with the best possible quality of life.This project, which is representative of the research performed under Oncode, aims to lay a solid basis for new immuno-oncology-based therapeutic strategies, with the objectives to i) gain fundamental insights into tumor-immune cell interactions, and ii) discover potential new therapeutic targets and/or treatment combinations for new therapeutic strategies.This strategic public-private partnership joins forces, to unite incredible collection of complementary expertise, facilities, key enabling technologies, methods, models, and experimental drugs from Dutch research institutions and multinational large pharmaceutical companies, with the common goal to understand cancer, and improve cancer care.
Aanvrager: Stichting Het Nederlands Kanker Instituut-Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Ziekenhuis

Projecttitel: Vector Innovation for Improved VACcine Efficacy
Projectbeschrijving: Messenger RNA-lipid nanoparticles emerged as exciting new vaccine modality amidst de COVID-19 pandemic. Although the concept had been around longer, doubts on scalability and pharmaceutical quality/stability prevented application. These doubts have been effectively confronted with the rollout of Comirnaty™ and Spikevax™..Despite this success, the mRNA-lipid nanoparticles leave room for improvements. The formulations need cold/ultracold storage, mRNA expression is short-lived and delivery inefficient. Moreover, control over target cell expression and type of immune response is limited. .In VIVACE we aim to build the next generation of RNA nanovectors to make RNA based vaccines more efficacious and to be able to steer the immune response to  a wider variety of diseases, without the need for sub-zero storage. .Vaccines have far-reaching health, social and economic benefits when they are broadly available and accessible and are often described as one of the greatest public health interventions. VIVACE contributes to wider availability and accessibility of vaccines, while also investigating novel formulations and improving methods to investigate these. Obviously, such improved vaccine formulations are of economic interest, not only because of the monetary value of the sales and public health impact for such improved products but also because of the wider implications of vaccines for preventing outbreaks and associated public health measures, like lockdowns.

Projecttitel: : Technology-based tool to support IBS patients towards a healthy diet
Projectbeschrijving: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is the most prevalent gastrointestinal disorder, affecting up to 10% of the general population. IBS is a chronic disorder and associated with a reduction in patients’ quality of life due to a variety of gastrointestinal complaints (e.g., abdominal pain, altered bowel habits). Dietary modification is a promising approach, as diet seems to play a keel role in the occurrence of symptoms. Up to 85% of IBS patients indicate that certain foods induce gastrointestinal complaints. Yet, tailored dietary intervention (tools) are lacking. The proposed IBS-DietSup project follows a user-centred design approach for the design of a dietary support tool tailored to IBS patients. In WP1, needs and preferences of IBS patients are mapped. These insights will be used to tailor the tool to patients’ needs. Additionally, a short questionnaire on frequently avoided (trigger) foods will be developed which will be integrated in the tool to generate (alternative) dietary suggestions that avoid trigger foods. In WP2, the actual tool will be created together with IBS patients and in consultation with an advice committee comprising relevant stakeholders. For the actual development, we will build upon dietary tools previously developed by the different applicants. Finally, in WP3, a pilot study will be conducted to evaluate the short-term effects of the tool on diet quality of IBS patients. In addition, usability of the tool will be assessed. This interdisciplinary project makes optimal use of broad expertise in IBS, dietary assessment and interventions, and technological innovations. This project will result in a prototype for a patient population in desperate need of dietary support. Results from this project will be used for larger grant applications for an extensive intervention study on long-term effects and tailoring towards use in other groups with similar complaints (e.g., non-coeliac wheat sensitivity, functional dyspepsia, inflammatory bowel disease).

Projecttitel: Targeted PRECIsion NUTrition strategy to prevent chronic metabolic diseases
Projectbeschrijving: The whole project fits under industrial research. The goal of this project is to ascertain the utility of a.more detailed and valid classification of the diet-sensitive phenotypes in improving nutritional.prevention (macronutrients and specific food products) of type 2 diabetes and cardiometabolic.outcomes as well as mental performance and well-being. The precision-based nutrition strategy, which.is developed and tested in the current proposal, aims to acquire knowledge based on which new.products and concepts are developed (during as well as after the project) to support specific subgroups.(phenotypes) in promoting health and preventing chronic metabolic diseases.

Projecttitel: From diet to a healthy immune system: understanding biological food paths to oppose metabolic syndromes and infectious diseases
Projectbeschrijving: A healthy, balanced diet is important for keeping metabolic health and supporting immune system. Hyperglycemia and lipid accumulation may lead to an overproduction of cytokines, hyperactivation of complement system and coagulation system, which all serve as immunological triggers to severe infection of COVID-19 as well as other infectious diseases. The DIYUFOOD project aims to leverage extensive multi-omics and clinical data collected from four population-based cohort studies set up in Israel, the Netherlands, the UK and China, with diverse ethnicity backgrounds, dietary patterns and socioeconomic status, to disentangle casual pathways using both mediation analysis in observational studies and Mendelian randomization analysis for causal inference. Our project will provide deeper understanding of underlying causal pathways of the biological “food path” from dietary intake to disease outcomes, which is imperative to develop effective food solutions to combat disease risks.

Projecttitel: : A prosthesis to restore vision in the blind
Projectbeschrijving: The rapidly emerging scientific field of neurotechnology is changing medical practice. POSITIONED aims to develop a new link between digital technology and the nervous system to improve the lives of patients with disorders of the nervous system. We develop a new type of neuroprosthesis called “fountain probe”, which is a high-density interface with neurons in a relatively small volume in the brain. The new probe can be implanted through a small burr hole in the skull. We will ultimately aim to position hundreds of electrodes in a volume of less than 200 mm3. As example use-case we choose blindness, a condition that affects more than 40 million people across the world. To enable sight, visual information is registered in the retina of the eye, passed on to the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN), from where it reaches the visual cortex. In humans, the LGN has a volume of approximately 120 mm3 and previous studies have demonstrated that electrical stimulation of LGN electrodes causes the perception of dots of light, called “phosphenes”. We expect that the fountain probe will cover the entire LGN with electrodes and that it can be implanted with a procedure that is as invasive as deep-brain stimulation. The probe will enable perception in the entire visual field, which has been impossible to achieve with previous approaches. The future user will wear a camera, and the video stream is processed to give rise to phosphenes that outline the relevant objects in the user’s vicinity. We will test the probe in mice to assess functionality, how well it integrates with the brain tissue and how long it keeps working. POSITIONED will thereby provide insight into the short and long-term functionality of a device that could restore a simple form of vision for people who are blind.
This project aims to detect and predict flare-ups and help patients monitor IBD at home using smart technologies

Projecttitel: Drivers of antimicrobial resistance in enteric pathogens: proximity-ligation metagenomics to track antimicrobial resistance genes across microbes in space and time
Projectbeschrijving: The rapidly rising numbers of infections with pathogenic bacteria resistant to antimicrobials represents a major threat to global health and economic security. To combat this threat, intricate knowledge of the processes underlying the emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance is necessary..In this project, we aim to fill an important knowledge gap in antimicrobial resistance research, namely: how do bacterial enteropathogens acquire antimicrobial resistance genes and what are the roles of antibiotic usage and the indigenous human microbiome in this process. The human microbiome is known to be a reservoir for antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs), but tracking ARGs and their spread among different bacteria has been inherently difficult due to methodological limitations..The development of proximity-ligation sequencing technology (Hi-C) and its application to metagenomics enables analyses tracking the spread of ARGs between bacteria within the human microbiome in situ. Within this project, we will apply this technology to a unique cohort, which combines time-series sampling of the developing microbiome of children in Zambia and Ghana with targeted sampling of enteropathogenic infections within the cohort..The generated datasets will be used to characterise and quantify the spread of ARGs within the microbiome in response to antibiotic usage and during infection. We will develop methodologies to pinpoint the source of horizontal transfer events.  This work will uncover the developing human microbiome’s role as an antibiotic resistance reservoir. Further, our analyses will describe the spread of ARGs from the microbiome to disease-causing bacterial enteropathogens. These insights are needed to design evidence-based interventions to stop the spread of ARG within our microbiome and towards pathogens capable of causing disease.

Projecttitel: Development of a robust method to simultaneously detect ribosome profiles and transfer RNAs in individual fixed cells
Projectbeschrijving: In recent years novel single-cell sequencing methods have allowed an in-depth analysis of the diversity of cell types and states in a wide range of organisms. Due to the continuous optimization of experimental and computational methods by many research groups, it is now possible to sequence the transcriptomes of thousands to millions of individual cells (Tang et al., 2009; Islam et al., 2011; Ramsköld et al., 2012; Hashimshony et al., 2012; Shalek et al., 2013; Jaitin et al., 2014; Zeisel et al., 2015). Albeit an exciting development, transcription only covers the first step in the central dogma. The second step, the process of translation, is currently much harder to explore in single cells. Despite recent progress in detecting proteins by mass spectrometry with single-cell resolution (Budnik et al., 2018), it remains a major challenge to measure translation in individual cells. Building upon existing ribosome profiling protocols (Ingolia et al., 2009; Reid et al., 2015; Darnell et al., 2018), our laboratory recently majorly increased the sensitivity of these assays allowing ribosome profiling in single cells (scRibo-seq; VanInsberghe et al., 2021). Integrated with a machine learning approach, this method achieves single-codon resolution in individual cells. The major goal of this proposal is to further improve scRibo-seq to include a freezing and/or fixation step. Projecttitel: D4P: A digital, data driven approach for differentiated prevention
Projectbeschrijving: Although data is considered the new oil, having tremendous value, its use in health care is relatively limited compared to other fields. Refining data could reveal its potential and could provide remarkable opportunities for more personalized health care, prevention of disease and mitigation of disease complications. Moreover, data-driven approaches could help to reduce existing healthcare inequalities, such as socioeconomic differences. In D4P (digital, data-driven approach for differentiated prevention) we ultimately aim to provide personalized health care and prevention through a data-driven and differentiated approach. As a proof of concept we will focus on HIV, as this is a progressive, innovative and rapidly evolving field, in which socioeconomic inequality plays a substantial role. This demonstration project also perfectly aligns with the current international movement towards eliminating HIV: zero new HIV-cases in 2030. While the Netherlands has made significant progress towards ending the HIV-epidemic and has an ambition to end the epidemic by 2027, current, relatively general prevention measures fail to reach the remaining people with undiagnosed HIV. This calls for an innovative, personalized data-driven approach. In D4P we will develop a novel data-driven approach to more tailored and targeted prevention of disease and mitigation of disease complications. D4P builds upon the existing data-infrastructure from CBS and SHM to engage in a research approach that:.(1) generates scientific knowledge on new HIV diagnoses and retainment in HIV care;.(2) forms the building blocks of the data-driven approach for prevention by translating research into actionable and quantitative insights with which we actively support health care providers, public health and community groups in their attempts to eliminate HIV by 2027 in the Netherlands..Since scientific knowledge does not automatically reach clinical practice, we believe this novel approach will be able to facilitate prevention and transform the Netherlands into a leading country in HIV elimination.

Projecttitel: FUrther developmenT of holography to improve brain tUmor Resection in childrEn in 3  Dimensions.
Projectbeschrijving: The use of 3D holography in resection of brain tumors in children is a novel application of mixed reality in a complex neurosurgical procedure. Since radicality of resection of brain tumors in children is of prognostic value for survival of the patient, the use of Intra-operative (Io)MRI is considered valuable. IoMRI is used to identify remnant tumor tissue and provides an up-to-date anatomy of the brain that may be affected by brain-shift during surgery. The IoMRI images can be translated into the neuronavigation system, and the updated neuronavigation supports the neurosurgeon to safely resect additional remnant tumor tissue. An automated segmentation algorithm (WP1) would create an updated 3D hologram of the remnant tumor; and with an automatic patient-to-image registration an anatomic overlay would become available to the neurosurgeon (WP2) that can be validated with the neuronavigation system (WP3). The potential value of an updated mixed reality overlay in this per-operative setting is 1. a reliable no-touch localization of the remnant tumor and 2. a better identification of the 3D shape of the remnant tumor. This unique combination of 3D holography with IoMRI in this neurosurgical setting may contribute to a better outcome for these children (1 societal), to an optimal surgical result from a single operative procedure (2 economic), and to a translation and a validation of per-operative imaging into a complex medical application (3 scientific).
Aanvrager: Prinses Maxima Centrum voor Kinderoncologie B.V.

Projecttitel: Innovative Surgical techniques for Eyes with Advanced glaucoma (ISEA)
Projectbeschrijving: Glaucoma, a degenerative optic neuropathy characterized by progressive visual field loss, is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. Currently, the only proven therapy is lowering the main risk factor, intraocular pressure (IOP), to a target that is low enough to halt progression of the disease. Surgical intervention (often implant surgery) is indicated when medication and/or laser therapy are unsuccessful. However, surgery often fails (50% within five years), due to hypotony (IOP < 5 mmHg), or due to hypertony (often even higher than the IOP at baseline, caused by fibrosis and subsequent scarring of the implant site), or other (possibly severe) complications (e.g., tube or device extrusion, corneal decompensation). .To improve surgical outcomes, a consortium of excellent researchers from the University Eye Clinic (Maastricht UMC+), Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e, Eindhoven, NL), and large industry partner InnFocus Inc., a Santen company (Miami, USA), recently developed a minimally invasive miniature long-tube glaucoma drainage implant from an inert innovative biopolymer (SIBS). This research was catalyzed and funded by the Chemelot Institute for Science and Technology (InSciTe, Maastricht, NL) in two projects (The SEAMS [https://www.chemelot-inscite.com/en/project/seams] and ISEA [https://www.chemelot-inscite.com/en/project/isea] projects). The proposed project will be a spin-off project (performed by partners of the same consortium) in which we prepare the novel miniature glaucoma drainage device for a first-in-man feasibility study. During this project we will transfer production of the miniature glaucoma drainage device from a laboratory setting to a cleanroom facility (ISO 13485 certified, Medace bv). In a cleanroom we will optimize and validate production. In parallel, we aim to develop a second implant that is able to non-invasively adjust postoperative IOP for patients with refractory glaucoma.

Projecttitel: PANDIA-Paranodal Antibodies in acute and chronic immune-mediated Neuropathies: improved DIAgnostics for better treatment
Projectbeschrijving: Background. During the last decade, novel autoantibodies have been discovered in a subgroup of patients with acute and chronic immune-mediated neuropathies. These antibodies are directly pathogenic and target proteins connecting myelin loops to axons at paranodal areas flanking nodes of Ranvier. Generally, patients with these anti-paranodal antibodies respond poorly to standard treatment, yet recovery can be spectacular when treated aggressively, eg with B-cell-depleting agents. Currently, methods to detect these antibodies are suboptimal — non-quantitative, subjective, laborious, and haveing long turn-around times— delaying start of aggressive treatment. Furthermore, the mechanisms underlying differing disease courses and response to therapy are poorly understood. Objective. Improve diagnostic methods for detection of anti-paranodal antibodies and investigate whether acute and chronic immune-mediated neuropathies differ in antibody and B cell kinetics. Study design. Our multidisciplinary team will develop a robust, plate-based quantitative assay for the detection of anti-paranodal antibodies. We will validate the assays in a routine diagnostic setting and screen (inter-)national cohorts of patients with acute and chronic immune-mediated neuropathies (n>1000). Technology for detection of antigen-specific B cells will be used for the generation of monoclonal antibodies allowing assay standardisation and to investigate the effect of immunomodulatory treatment on these B cells specifically. Results will be related to clinical course and outcome. Expected results and impact. With novel assays we expect to improve stratification of patients with immune-mediated neuropathies at an earlier stage. We anticipate detecting B cells specific for paranodal antigens that can be used for disease monitoring and to guide treatment choices. The project will lead to standardization, higher quality and shorter turn-around times of diagnostic tests for anti-paranodal antibodies, promoting more adequate and timely treatment and improving the quality of life of patients with immune-mediated neuropathies.
Aanvrager: Erasmus Universitair Medisch Centrum Rotterdam (Erasmus MC)

Projecttitel: IMMUNOFIRE – Lighting the Fire in Immuno-cold Brain Tumors
Projectbeschrijving: Children with high-grade brain tumors have an unacceptably poor long-term prognosis. The high mortality rates and long-term disabilities are not only caused by the cancer, but also by intensive chemo- and radiotherapy these young patients are treated with. Therefore, new treatment paradigms must be developed that simultaneously result in higher cure rates and improved quality of life by preventing detrimental damage to the developing brain. Although immunotherapy strategies hold great promise, they are ineffective in brain tumors due to this type of tumor’s highly immunosuppressive nature. In this project, we aim to overcome immunosuppression in high-grade brain tumors with proprietary nanobiologic therapeutics developed by Trained Therapeutix Discovery (TTxD). Nanobiologics are nanomedicines that effectively and safely induce trained immunity in the bone marrow.

Projecttitel: Predict and Prevent - The integration of pan-genomics, population dynamics and clinical outcomes to elucidate emerging pathogen threats using machine learning.
Projectbeschrijving: The revolution in infectious disease surveillance brought about by the widespread adoption of whole genome sequencing has had a profound impact on the ability to track the spread of outbreaks, elucidate transmission and target public health measures.  However, the ability to mine these vast data resources to decipher genotype to phenotype relationships, or to utilise the data in a predictive setting, to better profile novel and emerging strains, is underdeveloped.  This research will extend cutting edge methodologies in structuring large, connected data sets and employ machine learning strategies to analyse the information content and leverage its predictive power.  Specifically, we will catalogue genomic variation in conjunction with information about strain prevalence and clinical outcome in novel and optimised mathematical graphs.  These graph structures will then be transformed into a machine learning framework, Graph Neural Networks for several classification tasks. We will identify node combinations that are predictive for an outcome of interest (e.g. clinical outcome, pathogen spread) thereby unravelling the genetic basis underlying these traits and expose novel sequence data from emerging strains to quantify their epidemic or virulence potential.  This innovative approach tackles both the structuring and analysis of petabyte scale microbial pathogen data to drive pathogen genome surveillance into a new era.  This generalisable approach will initially be applied to the key foodborne pathogens Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli.  These globally important pathogens are responsible for considerable morbidity, mortality and economic losses. There is a critical need to better understand the differential risk that different strain types pose through the food chain so targeted and proportional interventions that maximise public safety and minimise economic losses are developed. These pathogens have benefited from several years of longitudinal genomic surveillance in the human, animal and food sectors across several continents and are the perfect exemplar for this project.

Projecttitel: Early detection of work-related health risks
Projectbeschrijving: In the Netherlands, the responsibility of providing a safe and healthy workplace to employees is the responsibility of the employer. As a consequence, occupational health services and care are privatised. However, occupational health services and employers lack the capacity to broadly screen for chemical exposures and therefore novel risks can go unnoticed for many years. . .Technologies based on untargeted mass spectrometric-based metabolomics can screen for presence of compounds having a health risk. However, there are still challenges to overcome before these workflows can be applied to screen for chemicals causing risks for workers. Sensitive, targeted and untargeted screening methods need to be developed for relevant chemicals present in low concentrations in a specific company, industry and/or environmental setting. Endogenous (effect) biomarkers related to clinical markers resulting from health damage should also be monitored. . .The aim of RISK@WORK is to develop an innovative mass spectrometric-based risk assessment workflow to identify possible risks due to worker exposure to hazardous chemicals.. .We will achieve this by building a pipeline to allow informed risk assessment based on presence of possible chemicals in a specific environment that a worker is exposed to. We will optimize our existing exposome pipeline to target specific occupational exposures including experimental transformation of potentially hazardous chemicals. A pilot study involving samples taken from workers under supervision of an occupational physician will be used to evaluate the developed pipeline for early detection of work-related risks. This will allow us to prepare a roadmap for the implementation of the developed pipeline in occupational health.. .RISK@WORK will show how informed exposomics profiling can be used to identify early health risk of workers that are exposed to chemicals in the workplace and present ways of implementing such an early risk assessment in occupational health monitoring to reduce occurrence of work-related diseases and sick leave.

Projecttitel: Beta cell Xpress: An open retrievable stem cell islet delivery
Projectbeschrijving: Regenerative medicine aims to restore, diseased or damaged tissues and organs, restoring.their function using a combination of bioengineering, cell biology and medicine, to reduce.long-term symptomatic treatment of chronic diseases and healthcare costs..Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune disorder caused by specific destruction of insulinproducing.beta-cells. These patients are not able to regulate their blood glucose levels,.and if left untreated this results in severe complications and ultimately death. Current care.involves lifelong exogenous insulin therapy using pumps or pens accompanied by daily.multiple glucose checks via fingerpricks. Apart from physical aspects of the disease, daily.management of healthy blood glucose levels, increased risks of long-term complications.such as blindness, cardiovascular disease, renal failure and nerve damage, patients and.their family experience significantly cause significant stress leading to further reduction in.quality of life..Tremendous progress has been made in the first project of the RegMed XB Diabetes.Moonshot, human donor pancreatic islets can now be combined with a dedicated cell.delivery device. In parallel, the consortium members have been working on creating stem.cell-derived beta cells so-called “stem cell-islets” a future unlimited source. In this follow.up project we will develop a cell delivery device especially for stem cell islets. We will use.experience and the lessons learned from the previous Diabetes Moonshot, aiding us in.making informed decisions and design criteria to create a dedicated delivery device for.stem cell-islets using an open retrievable device concept.

Myocardial infarction (MI) diagnosis in patients presenting with chest pain at the ER or in a pre-hospital setting remains a major challenge. Protocols focus on identifying ST-elevation, while ST-elevation MI only accounts for 30% of MI. But in 70%, the ECG can demonstrate non-specific abnormalities or even shows no abnormalities. Quality of ECG interpretation (especially in first line triage) hinders effective timely identification of MI. On average (JAMA IM 09-2022) only 54% of 12-lead ECGs are interpretated correctly by physicians. CineECG is a new technology to improve and increase correct ECG interpretation based on digital twin and AI technologies. CineECG applies computerized inverse cardiac modelling to instantly reconstruct heart activation and recovery features from standard 12 lead ECG data. CineECG compares recorded value against normal healthy values and indicates positions of ischemia within the heart. In the FLC (first line CineECG) project, the consortium will study the added value of applying CineECG for improved first line diagnosis of MI. This is achieved by adding CineECG, complementary to the existing work flow. The primary endpoint is to demonstrate and validate the added clinical and economic value of CineECG in both pre-hospital ECG (GP, ambulance) and SEH based triage. Secondary endpoints are: a) Develop and validate CineECG parameters for MI detection, and compare CineECG results with standard practice results of ECG interpretation b) Develop and validate the added value of serial (Cine)ECG comparison during the admission and triage process for patients with chest pain based on the CineECG serial ECG Comparison functionality. Key challenges are: a) selection of parameters from CineECG features to have optimal triage result; b) selection of software settings and parameters of and from the CineECG Compare function to have optimal clinical value; c) integrating CineECG analysis and CineECG data transfer in ambulance and ED decision support chain.

With an ageing population and increasing.chronic diseases, the demand for heparin is expected to surpass current production.capacities, which depend on pig intestines..Our project’s primary goal is to ensure the sustainability of access to life-saving blood.thinners by reducing dependence on animal-derived sources and geographical locations. Projecttitel: Fixation-Restitution Breeding – analysis and synthesis of haplotype compositions of diploid germplasm
Projectbeschrijving: "Motivation: Fixation and pyramiding of biotic and abiotic stress resistance, to develop potato varieties with a high sustainability and resilience profile, is impossible to achieve using conventional breeding at the tetraploid level. During meiosis the genetic quality of parental clones disperse across gametes, leading to a segregating offspring with very few desirable individuals. True seed F1 hybrid breeding is promising, but has a steep learning curve in terms of breeding efforts. In a previous TKI project we developed the first components towards Fixation-Restitution breeding. Here, self-compatible diploids allow Fixation of beneficial traits, but homozygosity for F1 hybrid uniformity, associated with the loss of vigour and fertility due to inbreeding depression, is not required. With 2n gametes (2nG) by First Division Restitution (FDR) all fixed alleles are transferred to tetraploid offspring from which commercial varieties can be selected. ..Objective: In this project we focus on the analysis and synthesis of haplotype compositions in diploid potato.  We will recombine several biotic resistance genes (pyramiding) from different genomes and bring them in coupling phase. This will deliver valuable multi-resistant haplotypes. Resistance genes in coupling phase do not disperse after selfing but can be fixed!  In addition, we aim to increase the number of beneficial alleles available at the diploid level, but also purge this gene pool of deleterious alleles. To achieve this objective we will generate much more knowledge on allelic diversity and develop new methods to evaluate the value of this diversity.  ..Impact: This project contributes an innovative system for potato breeding that can overcome limitations of the current breeding methods. The participating breeding companies can remain competitive in a future market where true seed F1 hybrid breeding is reaching maturity, and contribute to a diverse European potato breeding landscape and long term viability of SME potato breeding companies."

Projectbeschrijving: De Toekomstvisie Gewasbescherming wil een blijvend economisch perspectief voor de Nederlandse land- en tuinbouw realiseren door duurzaam te gaan produceren met weerbare planten en weerbare teeltsystemen. Ziekten en plagen krijgen daardoor minder kans en het gebruik van gewasbeschermingsmiddelen wordt zo veel mogelijk voorkomen. Dit project draagt direct bij aan deze doelstelling: een sterk verminderde afhankelijkheid, input en impact van chemische gewasbeschermingsmiddelen voor de beheersing van bladschimmels in de akkerbouw...Alternatieve, low impact, beheersingsstrategieën zijn noodzakelijk om in de toekomst te kunnen voldoen aan de doelstellingen van o.a. het Actieplan Plantgezondheid, de Toekomstvisie Gewasbescherming en de EU “farm to fork” strategie. Grosso modo moeten deze plannen leiden tot een 50% gereduceerd gebruik van chemische gewasbeschermingsmiddelen in 2030..In dit project worden ICM strategieën voor bladschimmelbeheersing in aardappelen, suikerbieten en granen daarom verder ingevuld met nieuwe kennis over laag-risico middelen (op vatbare en resistente(re) rassen), schade- en actiedrempels en verbeterde ondersteunende systemen. Projecttitel: Safe precision fermentation for production of dairy and meat protein analogues (SAFERMENT)
Projectbeschrijving: The SAFERMENT project aims to identify and analyze potential food safety hazards in production chains of dairy protein analogues based on precision fermentation (PF), from the substrate to the end-product and consumer. An inventory and assessment of the potential hazards will aid stakeholders in this field to develop safe production chains and end products derived from precision fermentation. The focus is on genetically modified micro-organisms (GMMs) that produce analogues of dairy proteins, and the proposed research will address food safety as an integral part of the safety culture surrounding innovative fermentation-based production methods and novel food development and manufacturing. .. ..The specific food safety aspects that will be addressed in this project are 1) the allergenic properties of recombinant dairy protein analogues, 2) differences in protein modifications between recombinant analogues and natural variants of dairy proteins and how this might be used in food authentication, 3) the presence of recombinant genetic material in protein fractions to be used in novel food products, 4) hazard identification and risk analysis in production chains of dairy protein analogues, and 5) consumer risk perception for the consumption of novel food products containing animal-free dairy proteins produced using GMMs.  .. ..Outcomes from the project will contribute to the implementation of safe production chains for recombinant dairy protein analogues and their safe use as food ingredients. Early identification of safety issues in the production chains and how to address them will be of importance for both producers and end-users of these food ingredients. The project will also provide an overview of consumer attitudes towards products containing animal-free yet recombinant dairy protein analogues. The outcomes of this project will thus be important for safe and successful commercialization of recombinant animal-free dairy protein analogues.

Projecttitel: App ’n eiwit: leefstijlinterventie met eiwit en e-health voor gezond ouder worden
Projectbeschrijving: Dit project richt zich op het realiseren van een adequate eiwitinname van oudere volwassenen door middel van in de praktijk beschikbare eiwitrijke voedingsproducten. Een actieve leefstijl met voldoende hoogwaardig eiwit en beweging speelt een belangrijke rol in het gezond en vitaal ouder worden en het voorkomen van (chronische) aandoeningen en ziektes. Om een gezonde leefstijl in het dagelijks leven te ondersteunen, wordt een specifiek ontwikkelde e-health applicatie ingezet, die consumptie van eiwitrijke voedingsproducten stimuleert en daarnaast een gepersonaliseerd beweegadvies geeft. De e-health leefstijlinterventie gericht op een adequate eiwitinname zal inzichten genereren hoe consumenten het best geholpen kunnen worden om weloverwogen voedselkeuzes te maken en langdurige gedragsveranderingen te realiseren. De verwachting is dat voor de inactieve oudere volwassenen, al dan niet in combinatie met lagere sociaal-economische status, een grotere gedragsverandering nodig zal zijn. Deze inzichten zullen helpen bij de implementatie van een actieve leefstijl met een adequate eiwitinname in het dagelijks leven van oudere volwassenen met als doel spierbehoud te ondersteunen en te verbeteren als essentiële factor bij gezond ouder worden.

Projecttitel: Controlling food safety and spoilage of cocoa and plant protein containing products
Projectbeschrijving: The hydration of ingredients (particularly of hydrophobic ones) is a critical step in ensuring microbial stability of beverages. Improperly hydrated ingredients will contain dry pockets, and bacterial spores in such dry pockets survive thermal processing regimes and can subsequently cause spoilage of liquid food products. In this consortium, scientific methods are developed to monitor the hydration state of selected powders during product preparation and (inverse) relation between hydration state and spoilage is investigated as a function of ingredient composition and physical properties and processing conditions. The ultimate goal of the project is to define strategies to hydrate poorly dispersible powders and improve heat inactivation of microbial contaminants during UHT treatment of products to reduce non-sterility of UHT products.

Projecttitel: Immuunstatus via dry blood spot analyse
Projectbeschrijving: Het huidige project geeft op twee manieren richting aan toekomstige ontwikkelingen. Enerzijds op het gebied .van het type en de toegankelijkheid van bloedsamples voor studies in kinderen. Daarnaast wordt er binnen dit .project inzicht verkregen in de effecten van de vetbron voor kindervoeding op het immuunsysteem. .In veel klinische trials worden veneuze bloedsamples verzameld om de respons op een interventie te bestuderen. .Voor effecten op het immuunsysteem worden vaak cytokines gemeten. De verzameling van bloedsamples, zeker .als het om meerdere afnames op een dag gaat, is behoorlijk invasief voor de deelnemer. Tenzij het over medische .redenen gaat, is bloedafname in kinderen en zeker babies alleen in zeer beperkte mate toegestaan. Dry blood .spots (DBS) worden al decennialang bij babies en kleine kinderen afgenomen voor de detectie van allerlei .metabole ziektes, bijvoorbeeld via de hielprik. Hiervoor zijn slechts enkele druppels bloed noodzakelijk en de .soort analyses die in deze DBS samples uitgevoerd kunnen worden, bijvoorbeeld cytokines, is hard in .ontwikkeling. Dit biedt goede perspectieven voor de mogelijkheden van analyses in toekomstige klinische trials .in kinderen. In een project van de huidige projectvoorstelpartners is een humane studie uitgevoerd waar op .verscheidene metabolieten in het (veneuze) bloed een effect van verschillende vetbronnen uit kindervoeding op .het immuunsysteem werd gevonden. Er zijn zowel DBS als veneuze bloedsamples verzameld (op dezelfde .tijdspunten) in deze studie, maar het budget was ontoereikend voor de vergelijkende analyse van cytokines in .veneuze bloedsamples en de DBS-samples. Deze gekoppelde DBS en veneuze bloedsamples geven een unieke .kans voor de validatie van DBS voor parameters die inzicht geven in het immuunsysteem en de mogelijkheid om .het effect van een kindervoeding-gerelateerde interventie hierop te zien.

Projecttitel: Metabolic Impact of Future Food Processing (Meta-Pro)
Projectbeschrijving: Much of the current emphasis in societal dialogue is on the negative aspects of food processing. However, food processing can also positively influence the efficiency of nutrient digestion, enhance the release and absorption of nutrients and promote more sustainable and healthy nutrition. Mild processing approaches such as dry processing and mild fractionation have greatly reduced energy consumption and water usage, and can be used to enhance ingredient functionality, bioavailability, and digestion..Understanding the impact of mild food processing approaches on metabolic and sensory responses will enable ingredient and food production tailored for specific applications rather than for general use. Further research is now needed to demonstrate the metabolic and sensory impact of ingredients and foods produced by milder processing techniques compared to traditional intensive processing approaches..The MetaPro project will compare the impact of conventional and mild processing on food matrix, macronutrient digestion, metabolic responses and nutrient bio-availability using established digestion models and human feeding trials. This knowledge will be used to develop guidelines (design rules) for the development of healthier and more sustainable approaches to food processing.

Het centrale onderwerp van dit project is de drijvende teelt van de snijbloemen chrysant, Lisianthus, Matricaria.en Campanula. Omdat.de ervaring met Campanula op dit systeem nog beperkt is zal het onderzoek zich bij dit gewas focussen op de.potentie van het systeem voor dit gewas. Het vervolgens opzetten van praktijkproeven vindt – bij alle.gewassen - alleen plaats als de resultaten van de eerste fase dat rechtvaardigen.De drijvende teelt biedt veel voordelen: het is een van ondergrond gescheiden, volledig gesloten systeem.waardoor de emissie nihil is, maar waardoor er ook efficiënt kan worden omgegaan met water en meststoffen..Het aardgasgebruik is fors lager doordat er niet gestoomd hoeft te worden en er op een lagere temperatuur.geteeld kan worden. Het systeem levert daarmee een belangrijke bijdrage aan de ‘License to produce’..Ook zijn planten in dit systeem zeer mobiel en dat biedt volop mogelijkheden voor vergaande automatisering.en verbetering van arbeidsomstandigheden
